papers.title: Quantum Simulation of Electronic Structure using Quantum Density Functional Theory on a Programmable Integrated Photonic Circuit
papers.abstract: Quantum simulations of molecular electronic structure hold the potential for computational advantage but are inherently limited by the linear scaling of qubit requirements with respect to system size. Quantum Density Functional Theory (Q-DFT) addresses this constraint by reformulating the interacting many-body problem in terms of a non-interacting Kohn--Sham reference system. Here, we present and experimentally validate a Q-DFT algorithm that requires only $\mathcal{O}(\log_2(N))$ qubits to simulate a system of $N$ orbitals, thereby reducing resource overhead. More precisely, we solve the Kohn--Sham problem for the lithium hydride (LiH) molecule using the ensemble extension of the variational quantum eigensolver paradigm that minimizes the energy of the system in the subspace spanned by the ground and first excited states. To execute this task, we encode the problem with qubits on a quantum photonic platform, utilizing an architecture that combines a deterministic quantum dot single-photon source with a programmable integrated photonic circuit. By evaluating the molecular ground- and first excited-state properties, this work establishes a pathway for simulating larger molecular systems, demonstrating the viability of integrating qubit-efficient algorithms with advanced reconfigurable photonic hardware for near-term quantum chemistry applications.

papers.title: Universal quantum gate set for multimode Schrödinger cat states stabilized by nonlocal dissipation engineering
papers.abstract: Schrödinger cat states provide a hardware-efficient platform for bosonic quantum error correction by encoding logical information in protected manifolds of harmonic oscillators. While previous work has demonstrated the dissipative stabilization of multi-mode Schrödinger cat states as robust quantum …

papers.title: Chiral Entangled-State Generation through Dissipative Quantum Dynamics
papers.abstract: Dissipation, though often detrimental to quantum entanglement, can be manipulated for the preparation of entangled states, wherein ingeniously designed quantum jump processes drive the system toward the desired steady state. Here we venture beyond this paradigm, and demonstrate a new type of entangl…

papers.title: Four-fermion condensates in curved spacetimes: A functional approach
papers.abstract: Four-fermion interactions appear in effective descriptions of particle physics, many-body systems, and gravitational theories with fermions. Although the same local operator may enter perturbative scattering, a vacuum Nambu–Jona-Lasinio (NJL) instability, or finite-density Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer …

papers.title: Dynamical aspects of steady-state subradiance: Detailed balance and its breakdown
papers.abstract: The dynamics of dissipative many-body quantum systems sometimes admit an emergent classical description in terms of a Markov chain even though the corresponding state space contains highly entangled states. In particular, a bad-cavity laser is a paradigm system whose dynamics can be formulated as a …

papers.title: Wigner-Function Fingerprints of Collective Excitations in Mirror-Terminated Waveguide QED
papers.abstract: We investigate the emission profiles of singly excited collective states and propose a matched-mode witnessing protocol in a mirror-terminated waveguide quantum electrodynamics system. The amplitudes and relative phases of the initial collective excitation are encoded in the temporal mode of the emitted single-photon wavepacket, providing a route to state verification through the common waveguide output. We identify the emission mode associated with a chosen target state and employ an auxiliary virtual-cavity representation to evaluate the quantum state of this selected output mode. For a matched initial state, the selected mode contains the emitted single photon, whose Wigner function exhibits a pronounced non-classical negative dip, serving as a distinct fingerprint of the target many-body state. With the reference mode held fixed, different initial configurations yield different photon occupations and phase-space distributions, demonstrating the state selectivity of the protocol. These results connect collective-state verification with temporal-mode analysis of the emitted radiation, offering access to collective coherence with reduced reliance on qubit-resolved correlation measurements.

papers.title: Reasoning about Shared-Qubit Concurrency in Quantum Computing
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a semantic model for the parallel execution of quantum circuits, providing a formal foundation for studying shared-qubit concurrency in quantum computing. As in classical shared-memory concurrency, parallel quantum circuits may interfere with one another through operations on shared qubits. However, quantum entanglement and the noncommutativity of quantum operations introduce additional challenges for reasoning about their correctness. To address these challenges, we generalise the classical Owicki-Gries method to quantum computing at the level of quantum circuits. Our approach enables compositional reasoning about parallel quantum circuits by separating the verification of individual components from the analysis of interference between them. We formulate proof rules for establishing the correctness of parallel quantum circuits and prove their soundness with respect to the proposed semantic model.

papers.title: Initialization-controlled fault sensitivity and force-balance plateaus in noisy variational quantum optimization
papers.abstract: We study deep variational circuits for a periodic Heisenberg chain under local gate depolarization, at depths where noiseless training is coherently exact. Full-width initializations reach low coherent error faster than circuits with confined transverse generators, but incur a larger noise shift and need an order of magnitude more updates for noisy convergence. In many-body-localization-inspired initialization, bounding the initial transverse generator amplitudes keeps the operator support localized and suffices for low-fragility optimization, so longitudinal disorder and Floquet layer repetition are unnecessary. The fault-erasure fraction, the mean fraction of coherent energy removed per fault, sets the effective visibility through a parameter-free exponential model. Full-width circuits start with delocalized operator support, and once coherent energy builds up, each fault erases nearly all of it. Initially, their noise-induced gradient almost uniformly attenuates the coherent gradient, so coherent descent proceeds at the noiseless rate. They then stall on a high-noise force-balance plateau, where finite coherent and noise-induced gradients cancel to first order. At late times all initializations reach the same fault-erasure fraction and noisy-error band, but operator support contracts more slowly, at a rate set by the plateau residence time.

papers.title: Gaussian Quantum Integrated Sensing and Communication
papers.abstract: We consider a quantum integrated sensing and communication problem over an optical link in which a low-power transmitter simultaneously communicates with a receiver and identifies the range of a defect producing a backscattered signal. We model the system as a lossy thermal-noise bosonic channel, in which the target, modeled as a beamsplitter, affects the timing of the backscattered signal through its location. Motivated by the envisioned deployment of entanglement-enabled quantum networks, we develop two protocols that allow the transmitter to leverage shared Gaussian entanglement, in the form of independent two-mode squeezed vacuum states or coupled three-mode squeezed vacuum states, to assist both sensing and communication. Since entanglement is known to enhance sensing, as demonstrated in quantum illumination, and to increase communication rates through entanglement-assisted communication, the transmitter faces a trade-off in allocating its entanglement resources between the two tasks. Our main results characterize these trade-offs under the proposed protocols in terms of achievable communication rate/sensing error-exponent regions, which outperform time-sharing schemes and demonstrate a quantum advantage.

papers.title: Pump quantization changes optimal measurements for quantum sensing
papers.abstract: Standard analyses of quantum phase sensing often neglect the overhead of generating squeezed-light by treating the pump as an undepleted classical resource. Realistically, the pump is a quantum object that undergoes significant depletion and entangles with the produced squeezed light, raising the question of how the crossover from a classical to a quantum pump limits the quantum advantage in sensing. Contrary to prior analyses, we show that quantum advantage persists despite pump quantization, but depends critically on the nonlinear $(χ^{(2)})$ source dynamics. In particular, we demonstrate that Heisenberg scaling emerges in the regime of strong pump depletion, rather than maximum signal squeezing. At maximum squeezing, the quantum Fisher information (QFI) for interferometric sensing of an unknown phase scales as $N^{3/2}$, where $N$ is the pump photon number, surpassing the shot-noise limit but establishing that squeezing itself is insufficient to attain Heisenberg scaling of $N^2$. At maximal pump depletion, where the signal flux is maximized, the QFI scales as $N^2$. In this regime, standard photon counting is suboptimal, while a joint nonlinear measurement of the entire pump-signal system is shown to achieve Heisenberg scaling. Our work shows that pump quantization changes both the optimal operating point and the measurement strategies required to preserve a realistic quantum advantage in phase estimation and, more broadly, many-body quantum dynamics.

papers.title: Liouvillian Kramers Degeneracy
papers.abstract: The Kramers theorem generally guarantees the spectral degeneracy of time-reversal-invariant Hamiltonian operators with half-integer spin, underlying a variety of physical phenomena. Despite its fundamental significance, the Kramers degeneracy has been argued to be absent in Liouvillian superoperators acting on mixed states because of the double structure of the Hilbert space. Here, we instead demonstrate that the interplay of time-reversal symmetry$^†$ and parity symmetry enforces the Kramers degeneracy in Liouvillians. We explicitly construct dissipative many-body models of interacting fermions and spins exhibiting the Kramers degeneracy and show that their complex spectral statistics follow those of non-Hermitian random matrices in the corresponding symplectic symmetry classes. Of the three fundamental universality classes of non-Hermitian random matrices, the symplectic class has never been realized in symmetry-resolved many-body Liouvillians. Our constructions provide its explicit realizations and spectral signatures of nonintegrability in symplectic open quantum systems.

papers.title: Reconstruction of the conformal algebra from a critical groundstate on the (fuzzy) sphere
papers.abstract: Recently, we found a method to reconstruct the dilatation operator (sphere Hamiltonian) from a regulated conformal field theory groundstate. In this paper, we explore methods to construct the whole global conformal algebra, and test our construction using fuzzy sphere regularization. Starting from a groundstate of the same Hamiltonian, these methods perform better than constructions of the conformal generators based on a Hamiltonian density, are model-independent, require no additional tuning, and improve with system size. One purpose of reconstructing the conformal algebra is to identify conformal primary states, which we do with some success. We also find further evidence supporting the model of the short-distance corrections to the entanglement Hamiltonian proposed earlier and use it to make systematic improvements.

papers.title: Long-range entangled criticality from coherent errors
papers.abstract: We find that coherent error can induce a phase transition from the clean surface code phase into an extended long-range entangled critical regime with diverging Markov length. To demonstrate this, we establish two general results of independent interest. The first relates topology and quantum information to mixed-state entanglement: we show that when a noise channel acting on a topological code preserves a higher-form symmetry and nonzero coherent information, the noisy state for generic logical input is long-range entangled. The second generalizes the local recovery construction based on finite Markov length to any locally parameterized family, thus encompassing local Lindbladian evolution, coherent errors followed by syndrome dephasing, and thermal states. We apply these results to the honeycomb surface code, in which we find an extended long-range entangled critical regime that is a quasi-long-ranged counterpart of 1-form strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking. As a byproduct of these studies, we relate the conditional mutual information to conductance in a Majorana network model.

papers.title: Optimised finite key for satellite up-link entangled quantum key distribution
papers.abstract: Entanglement-based quantum key distribution from ground to satellite has been proposed as a scalable primitive for global quantum networks and will be demonstrated as part of the imminent QEYSSat mission. Both theoretical studies and experimental emulations have shown that a significant asymptotic key rate can be expected. In this work we investigate this scenario with a more rigorous security analysis taking into account the finite size effects that arise from short block lengths common in satellite transmission. Our findings suggest a slight alteration of the optimal source operation when informed by finite statistics as opposed to the asymptotic regime, notably that the pump power should be slightly lowered. We quantify the annual key rate based on a dynamically optimised source operation for the Heriot-Watt ground station and several satellite parameters. We find an improved annual key rate when accumulating all raw key material before extracting a secure key instead of doing so for each overpass. We ultimately show that QEYSSat will be able to generate a significant secure annual key with both strategies.

papers.title: Studentized inference in randomized experiments when a few units dominate the outcome variation
papers.abstract: In completely randomized experiments with heavy-tailed outcomes, a few units can carry a share of the residual variation that does not vanish as the number of units grows. We study the studentized difference in means and Lin's regression-adjusted estimator, with covariates whose leverage vanishes, when the finite population is fixed, and the treatment assignment is the only source of randomness. The studentized statistic then has a nonnormal limit in general. Populations with the same marginal distributions of potential outcomes can have different limits, as the limit depends on the unobserved pairing mechanism of the two potential outcomes of each dominant unit. When the outcome errors are drawn from a heavy-tailed law, the limit is random and, outside a degenerate case, varies with the population. Under balanced allocation, the conventional Wald interval has an explicit asymptotic coverage floor. At the nominal level $0.95$, the floor is about $0.42$ for every population and about $0.84$ when the two potential residuals of each unit are equal. Both floors are close to the best possible, and without balanced allocation, the coverage can fall to the smaller of the proportions of treated and control units.

papers.title: On the Failure Probability of Quantum Leftover Hashing with Bad Seeds
papers.abstract: We study hashing against quantum adversaries, as used in cryptographic applications, and provide bounds on the probability of failure in practical settings where seeds might be reused and might be non-ideal. Randomness extraction and privacy amplification are key components of quantum cryptographic protocols, such as quantum randomness generation or key distribution, that allow the compression of partially secure raw data into shorter output with high security. To ensure the security of any cryptographic construction that integrates them, it is desirable to establish composable security. This can be done by using methods based on universal hashing and leveraging the general leftover hash lemma, which allows extraction of near-uniform random numbers from an imperfect entropy source by sampling from an almost two-universal family of hash functions using a seed. This approach is taken in many practical implementations, commonly using Toeplitz hashing. The lemma provides an upper bound $\varepsilon$ on the distance of the output to uniform randomness, which holds on average over the choice of seeds. It makes no claim that any particular seed yields near-uniform random numbers. This poses a problem for practical applications where a seed is sampled once and reused for many rounds (blockwise hashing). Here, we study the subset of \textit{bad} seeds yielding far-from-uniform outputs. We show that randomness extraction against quantum side information is guaranteed to produce $δ$-close-to-uniform random numbers except with failure probability $\left(\frac{\varepsilon}δ\right)^2$. This result is generalised to blockwise hashing providing a guarantee of the security of $k$ rounds except with failure probability $\big(\frac{(2k-1)\varepsilon}δ\big)^2$. Moreover, we extend the general leftover hash lemma to blockwise hashing and relax the assumption of almost two-universality.

papers.title: Exceptional Points and Optimized Encoding in Qubit Stabilizer Codes
papers.abstract: Continuous blind stabilizer measurements turn stabilizer codes into a Liouvillian spectral problem in which Hamiltonian terms compete with dissipative error channels. We show that this competition generically enables Liouvillian exceptional points, whose occurrence at weak error rates is constrained by the code distance. Exceptional points are detrimental in this regime of error correction as they maximize the decay rate of encoded coherences. We then optimize the encoding of the logical qubit using the eigenmodes of the Lindblad operator. This phase-optimized encoding cancels the linear short-time decay of logical qubit coherences. We apply this encoding to the [[5,1,3]] code and demonstrate that it outperforms naive encoding methods near the exceptional point, improves the fidelity of a logical $π$ rotation and remains effective in the presence of additional weak error channels.

papers.title: Lossless propagation bounds for long-range fermionic interactions
papers.abstract: We prove propagation estimates for extensive fermionic many-body interactions with polynomial time growth, no loss of spatial decay, and an optimal threshold for the polynomial spatial exponent. More precisely, we construct local representatives of evolved fermionic many-body interactions on metric spaces with polynomial volume growth of order $d_{\mathrm{vol}}$ and suitable cell partitions. For the even Hamiltonian interaction $Φ_u$ and the even interaction $Ψ$ being evolved, we assume bounds, uniform in the site, on sums of term norms over finite supports $X$ containing a given site, with weights $e^{κ|X|}(1+\operatorname{diam}X)^a$ and $e^{κ|X|}(1+\operatorname{diam}X)^p$, respectively. Here $a>d_{\mathrm{vol}}$, $0\le p\le a$, $κ$ is sufficiently large, and the Hamiltonian bound is uniform in time. We construct local representatives whose interaction norms with weight $e^{c(1+|t-s|)^{-b}|X|}(1+\operatorname{diam}X)^p$ grow at most polynomially in $|t-s|$, for suitable $c,b>0$. In particular, $p=a$ is allowed: the Hamiltonian need not decay faster than the interaction being evolved. The threshold $a>d_{\mathrm{vol}}$ is optimal in general: uniform polynomial time bounds at $p=a$ fail for $0<a\le d_{\mathrm{vol}}$, even for smooth time-dependent two-site interactions. Polynomial time growth permits integration against filters with sufficiently many finite absolute moments, including those used in quasi-adiabatic constructions and quantum belief propagation. We derive consequences for filtered interactions and the dynamics they generate, providing dynamical estimates for perturbation theory with extensive perturbations, including gap stability, the principle that local perturbations perturb locally (LPPL), adiabatic theory, and response theory. All results also hold for quantum spin systems.

papers.title: Taming a macroscopic free mass through continuous quantum measurement
papers.abstract: The free particle is the most elementary dynamical system in quantum mechanics. Despite remarkable progress in quantum control of increasingly massive solid-state mechanical oscillators, the analogous control of the free-particle counterpart has remained elusive. Dissipation and environmental noise have prevented such control in the inherently low-frequency domain of free-particle dynamics---a regime of growing importance for quantum sensing and tests of fundamental physics. Here we realize a suspended 1-milligram rotor operating in the free-particle regime with exceptional environmental isolation. Combining this isolation with a low-noise measurement architecture, we directly resolve thermal fluctuations in the motion associated with a damping rate of only 7~nHz. Through continuous quantum measurement of the rotor, we localize its otherwise unconfined motion, obtaining conditional states with entropic temperatures as low as 140~nK as a quantitative measure of control in the free-particle regime. This is two orders of magnitude below temperatures previously achieved in tabletop optomechanical experiments. We demonstrate immediate utilities of the new operating regime, setting new constraints on modifications of quantum mechanics and benchmarking inferred entanglement-to-decoherence rate ratios nearly two orders of magnitude beyond the state of the art for tests of gravity at the quantum-classical interface.

papers.title: Belief Propagation-Informed Tesseract Decoding of Quantum LDPC Codes
papers.abstract: In quantum error correction, the decoder must estimate the errors from the measurement data accurately and fast enough to avoid a backlog. Search-based decoders such as Tesseract achieve high accuracy by finding a minimum-weight set of error events with an A* search, but their search effort grows rapidly with the physical error rate and the code size. To reduce this search effort while maintaining a logical error rate close to that of Tesseract, we propose a belief propagation (BP)-guided modification of the Tesseract decoder for quantum low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes. Damped sum-product BP is applied to the triggered detectors before the Tesseract search. If the detectors triggered by the BP hard decision match the triggered detectors, this hard decision is accepted directly, and the Tesseract search is skipped. Otherwise, the BP marginal probability estimates, weighted by a trust coefficient, modify the search priority, while the path cost keeps the channel-prior weights so that the decoding objective is unchanged. The framework also supports BP-based initialization, in which selected BP decisions form the starting point of a residual search whose signed-cost objective allows incorrect initial decisions to be removed. A node-exploration limit bounds this residual search; if the limit is reached, the decoder falls back to the BP-guided search on the original triggered detector set. The method is evaluated on the [[72,12,6]], [[90,8,10]], and [[144,12,12]] bivariate bicycle codes under circuit-level noise. With BP-based initialization and a global trust coefficient, the number of Tesseract search nodes expanded is reduced by up to more than two orders of magnitude at low physical error rates, while the logical error rate remains close to that of Tesseract.

papers.title: Needle-beam generation from SPDC photons using inverse-designed flat optics
papers.abstract: We experimentally demonstrate the generation of needle-like beams from spontaneous parametric downconversion (SPDC) light using a compact inverse-designed multilevel diffractive lens (MDL). The nonclassical nature of the SPDC source is independently verified through a three-detector heralded Hanbury Brown-Twiss measurement performed before the MDL, yielding a zero-delay second-order correlation value of approximately 0.14. Spatial measurements using an intensified charge-coupled device reveal that the MDL maintains a tightly confined focal distribution over an axial distance of approximately 11 mm under collinear SPDC illumination, substantially reducing diffraction-induced broadening compared with a conventional plano-convex lens of the same nominal focal length. Under non-collinear SPDC illumination, two distinct regions of extended axial confinement are observed, demonstrating the dependence of the engineered focal distribution on the incident spatial field. These results establish a compact flat-optical approach for engineering extended-focus SPDC photon fields, with potential applications in structured quantum photonics.

papers.title: Towards Optimal Routing Strategies for qLDPC codes on Silicon Spin Qubits
papers.abstract: One of the major challenges of implementing high-rate quantum error correction codes, like qLDPC codes, is realizing the required long-range interactions. Spin qubit platforms can provide this connectivity by shuttling qubits next to each other whenever they need to interact. When doing this, the performance of the code depends on the shuttling strategy. We study memory experiments of the [[144,12,12]] bivariate bicycle (Gross) code on two shuttling grids for future spin qubit devices: a square grid and a square grid with diagonals. We compare three shuttling strategies, structured and random initial layouts, and a range of shuttling noise models spanning best- and worst-case scenarios. The best strategy minimizes the longest distance travelled rather than the total distance. The initial layout has only a weak effect, whereas adding diagonals to the grid reduces the logical error rate by up to two orders of magnitude which may have implications for future hardware design.

papers.title: Resource-efficient quantum noise spectroscopy with sequential weak measurements
papers.abstract: Environmental fluctuations constitute a major source of decoherence in quantum devices, rendering their spectral characterization essential for robust control and error correction. Existing qubit noise spectroscopy methods often rely on elaborate control sequences or extensive scans over evolution t…

papers.title: Generalized $η$-pairing approach to interacting non-Hermitian systems in arbitrary dimensions
papers.abstract: Developing a general and rigorous analytical approach to non-Hermitian many-body systems is a challenging task. Here, we generalize the eta-pairing theory to very general non-Hermitian Hubbard models and find many interesting phenomena without Hermitian analogs. For instance, the Hermitian conjugate…

papers.title: Dynamical and stable spin squeezing via magnon Kerr nonlinearity in a hybrid solid-state system
papers.abstract: Spin squeezing is a genuine multipartite entanglement resource enabling quantum-enhanced metrology beyond classical limits. Based on a hybrid solid-state system of nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers and magnons, we propose a scheme for generating spin squeezing via Kerr nonlinearity. In the large-detunin…

papers.title: Quantum electron quasicrystal
papers.abstract: The strongly correlated phases of the homogeneous electron gas constitute the vocabulary of many-body condensed matter physics and find a natural realization in semiconductors. In this setting, recent neural-network variational Monte Carlo calculations discovered an unexpected quantum phase of matte…

papers.title: Around the Clock. New Twists on Fitch Cheney's Five-Card Trick
papers.abstract: Fitch Cheney's five-card trick is one of the purest two-person effects in card magic, and it has attracted mathematicians for more than seventy five years. This article retells the effect and its classic method, surveys how far it can be pushed, and presents several new results that matter to performers. We give a version of Cheney's method that needs no fixed first suit and no fixed ``lowest card'': shifting every card one step in rank and one step in suit shifts the display in the same way. A heckler who may swap two neighboring cards of the display defeats every method with a full deck. We show that a 29-card deck is the largest for which such a swap can be corrected, and that the corresponding maximum is 14 cards if any two cards may be swapped. We give simple methods that achieve both bounds. Finally, we make Berlekamp's arithmetic method for the 124-card deck independent of where the numbering starts. We also describe a pocket version with eight cards.

papers.title: Achievability of CSS codes performance limits over Pauli channels under separate ML decoding with bounded graphical complexity
papers.abstract: Capacity-approaching quantum error correction faces a fundamental tension: the required parity-check matrices need to become increasingly dense, while practical decoding and syndrome extraction favor sparse, bounded-degree structures. Reconciling these competing requirements remains an important open problem in quantum code design. We construct Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) code ensembles that approach the CSS rate over memoryless Pauli channels under maximum-likelihood decoding while retaining sparse, bounded-degree graphical representations. The construction separates parity-check density from graphical complexity: although capacity-approaching components may require dense parity-check matrices, they are represented by sparse concatenated factor graphs. We first study a construction combining low-density parity-check (LDPC) and low-density generator-matrix (LDGM) component codes and numerically analyze the average weight distributions of the resulting codes. Motivated by these results, we introduce a second construction based on concatenated LDPC and LDGM codes and generalized irregular repeat-accumulate (GIRA) codes. We derive bounds on the average weight distribution of the resulting sum ensemble and use the Miller-Burshtein framework to prove simultaneous reliability of the two CSS decoding components. Consequently, the proposed ensemble achieves rates arbitrarily close to the CSS hashing bound under separate bit- and phase-error correction, while maintaining bounded graphical complexity, thus providing a foundation for future iterative decoders and indirect syndrome-extraction architectures.

papers.title: Qubrio: High-Performance Quantum Compilation via Multi-Agent LLM Collaboration
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) offer an adaptable alternative to traditional quantum compilation heuristics, which bottleneck progress by demanding costly manual redesigns whenever hardware evolves. However, naive single-pass LLM approaches fail under the unique challenges introduced by quantum compilation. We introduce Qubrio, a practical agentic framework that significantly reduces heuristic redesigns through a three-level decomposition. By (1) partitioning programs into sequential operation stages, (2) deploying specialized agents for placement, routing and optimization, and (3) using disaggregated feedback for precise error correction, our system reliably navigates complex physical constraints. Beyond serving as a direct compiler, our LLM framework also uncovers novel strategies that facilitate convoy-style shuttling, substantially enhancing hardware concurrency without sacrificing fidelity. We further integrate these strategies into the previous state-of-the-art (SOTA) compiler, recovering a significant fraction of the LLM's performance advantages. On realistic workloads, our compiler achieves significant improvements in hardware runtime and program fidelity over the SOTA baseline PowerMove, seamlessly adapting to new hardware capabilities. Qubrio features an open user interface for practical use, and its code is publicly available at https://github.com/crosaa/Qubrio.

papers.title: Classical and Quantum Dynamics in State Space: Projective Hilbert Space, Measurement, and Classical Emergence
papers.abstract: We develop a geometric formulation of classical and quantum dynamics in which projective Hilbert space is taken as the primary state space and classical configuration and phase spaces arise as submanifolds of localized quantum states. The Fubini-Study metric induces the Euclidean metric on these submanifolds, while the tangential component of Schrödinger evolution reproduces Hamiltonian and Newtonian dynamics. We then extend the construction to stochastic motion. Brownian dynamics on the localized classical manifold is lifted to a common stochastic unitary evolution in projective Hilbert space; under homogeneity, isotropy, and independence assumptions, the corresponding Hermitian increments have Gaussian Unitary Ensemble statistics. This yields a random-matrix Schrödinger dynamics whose transition probabilities depend only on Fubini-Study distance. Through the embedding of localized states, the classical Gaussian transition law becomes the Born rule in projective state space. Measurement outcomes are identified with first arrival at detector-defined finite-resolution equivalence classes, while each realized state-space evolution remains linear and unitary. The framework is applied to classical emergence, macroscopic stabilization, double-slit experiments, composite systems, and entangled states. A spatially local Caldeira-Leggett-type system-environment model is also shown, under explicit thermal, symmetry, Ohmic, and coarse-graining assumptions, to generate the Brownian family required by the stochastic lift. The remaining open problem is to establish the range and universality of this mechanism for realistic many-body measuring environments.

papers.title: An Observable-Algebra Approach to Quantum Coherence in Anyonic Systems
papers.abstract: Physical restrictions on operations can make quantum coherence inaccessible. Quantifying off-diagonal density matrix elements in a chosen basis alone does not reveal which information is hidden by each restriction. To distinguish their effects, we describe physical restrictions through subalgebras of accessible observables. The associated trace-preserving conditional expectations unify two reconstruction principles: each gives both the maximum-entropy state compatible with the accessible data and the closest state in the corresponding subalgebra in relative entropy. We apply this framework to anyonic systems to separate the contributions from local-charge superselection and non-Abelian fusion rules. We prove that the charge-line severing map is the conditional expectation onto the local-product subalgebra. It is completely positive and quantum-trace-preserving, and uniquely reconstructs a state in this space from all local-product expectation values. The hierarchy of measurement restrictions then separates total bipartite coherence into three nonnegative contributions: coherence between local charges, inaccessible fusion information, and conventional coherence. The first two decompose the anyonic charge entanglement and distinguish the effects of local-charge superselection from the remaining fusion information. Finally, we relate basis-independent measures of anyonic coherence to entanglement. For pure anyonic states with vacuum total charge, the optimized total and correlated coherence equal the total and conventional relative-entropy entanglement, respectively.

papers.title: Decoherence suppression in quantum dense coding
papers.abstract: By harnessing entanglement to transmit information beyond the limits of classical communication, quantum dense coding serves as a key component in various quantum technologies. However, in the noisy intermediate-scale quantum era, noise-induced decoherence poses inevitable challenges to its practical implementation. By investigating the non-Markovian decoherence dynamics of the two categories of quantum dense coding protocols realized in discrete- and continuous-variable systems, we demonstrate a physical mechanism to suppress the decoherence in quantum dense coding. It is found that the formation of a bound state in the energy spectrum of the entire system consisting of each subsystem and its local environment of the quantum channel restores the quantum advantage of dense coding in the presence of decoherence. Refreshing our understanding on the noisy effect on quantum dense coding, our finding offers a guide toward the practical realization of noise-tolerant quantum dense coding.

papers.title: Access Resources and Stability of Error-Correction Capabilities in Continuous Strategic Codes
papers.abstract: Continuous quantum error correction depends on which parts of a measurement record remain available to the controller at recovery. We study this temporal access using continuous strategic codes, formulated as open continuous process tensors contracted with causal instruments and conditional recovery. For monitored stabilizer codes, a common-optimal-correction criterion identifies when records can be merged without loss and yields a factorization for separated CSS inference. Terminal decision labels and causal persistent memory carry different costs: five persistent classical states reach the complete-record optimum in a finite-strength counting model, whereas its two-window diffusive counterpart has nine terminal decision labels and requires unbounded memory for exact causal recovery. Uniform lower and constructive upper bounds establish an optimal fidelity deficit of order $m^{-2}$ for $m$ persistent states in the diffusive model. Counting and diffusive stability bounds translate open-process approximation into guarantees for deployed-controller performance and retained access advantages, quantified by explicit quantizers and model-mismatch curves. The same process--instrument framework connects storage with persistent environments and irreversible noise to spacetime interrogation and record-selected paths for a logical $T$ gate. These results specify which record distinctions recovery needs, the memory cost of approximating them, and the logical protection retained under model error.

papers.title: Graph-Covariant Bottom-Up Scale-Bridging Reconstruction of Ground and Excited States of Extended Systems
papers.abstract: We propose a hierarchical scale-bridging construction for building first principles electronic structure models of extended molecular aggregates with disorder, and its practical realization in exciton systems. The general construction, referred here as to the encapsulation, is based on a recursive operator-valued hierarchy cast in a dual graph-theoretic (discrete) and configuration-space (continuous) structure, in which variables associated with a coarser level parameterize operators governing the degrees of freedom at the next finer level in a graph-covariant, geometry-preserving fashion. In an exemplary application of this scheme, aggregate-level ground- and excited-state operators are constructed through a many-body expansion (MBE), with matrix elements evaluated in a basis comprising the aggregate ground state and local Frenkel excitations. The required monomer and dimer building blocks are obtained from DFT and TDDFT calculations, yielding aggregate-level 1-particle transition density matrices as well as Hamiltonian, dipole moment and other operators that can be evaluated at the level of the building blocks. Starting from structural models obtained from experiment or molecular dynamics, this approach generates aggregate-level operators in a bottom-up fashion without fitting parameters to spectroscopic data or performing calculations on larger system cutouts. A numerical demonstration is given for an excitonic manifold in crystalline quaterthiophene. In particular, through its intrinsic configuration-dependence encoded in the encapsulations, it will provide a bridge between static electronic structure calculations for realistic, structurally disordered aggregates and quantum or quantum-classical simulations of exciton-vibrational dynamics.

papers.title: All-to-All Connectivity in Superconducting Qubits via Metamaterial-Mediated Interactions
papers.abstract: We show that encoding superconducting qubits as dual-rail or spin-locked transmons lets a metamaterial waveguide couple them all-to-all while suppressing the spurious entanglement that burdens shared-mode architectures, a step toward the non-local connectivity that quantum low-density parity-check codes require. In a bare-transmon architecture, the dispersive coupling between each populated mode and every idle qubit attached to it entangles spectators with the gate, and cancelling it by dynamical decoupling lengthens every gate. The encoding suppresses this coupling at the hardware level, from second to fourth order in the inverse qubit--mode detuning. A two-tone cross-resonance drive then generates a Mølmer-Sørensen interaction between encoded qubits, which we use for an entangling gate and a joint parity measurement, both selective and parallelizable through different modes. Simulating two dual-rail transmons sharing three resonators with a mode lifetime of $30\,μ$s, we find that heralding transmon relaxation as erasure leaves a gate infidelity of $1.4\times10^{-3}$ at $152$~ns, dominated by photon loss. Photon loss and mode crowding together bound the array size. The gate duration must exceed the inverse mode spacing, which shrinks as the array lengthens, while photon loss grows with gate duration. This bound grows linearly with the mode lifetime and with the inter-resonator coupling; at a lifetime of $150\,μ$s, five times the simulated value, and a coupling of $80$~MHz, a $10^{-3}$ error budget admits $13$ qubits on $25$ resonators.

papers.title: Normal Factor Graph Representations of Stabilizer Quantum Codes with Applications
papers.abstract: We develop normal factor graph (NFG) representations of stabilizer quantum error-correcting codes and entanglement-assisted quantum error-correcting codes. We introduce two complementary representations. Quantum-code NFGs describe stabilizer and normalizer label codes and provide a graphical framework for establishing self-orthogonality, constructing codes from component codes, and identifying encoding and decoding circuits. Quantum-probability NFGs represent the quantum-mechanical probabilities associated with encoding, noise, and measurement. We also introduce a doubleedge formulation that makes the relationship between these two representations explicit. We apply the framework to convolutional and tail-biting convolutional stabilizer codes, as well as to two classes of low-density parity-check stabilizer codes. Finally, we extend the quantum-probability representation to entanglementassisted codes.

papers.title: Quantum Mpemba effect of Z2 symmetry restoration in the Dicke model
papers.abstract: We study a symmetry-restoration quantum Mpemba effect in the dissipative Dicke model as an example of a weakly $\mathbb Z_2$-symmetric open quantum system, where the full Liouvillian is parity covariant although individual quantum jumps connect the two Hilbert-space parity sectors. Using the entanglement-asymmetry (EA) diagnostic to monitor parity restoration, we compare coherent-product and cat-product initial states. Coherent-product states show conventional relaxation, with larger initial asymmetry decaying more slowly and no Mpemba crossing observed. Cat-product states, by contrast, can reverse this hierarchy over a finite region of initial-state space. This reversal is enabled by initial-state mode filtering: the cat-product superposition suppresses the contributions of the leading slow Liouvillian modes, allowing a more asymmetric state to restore parity through faster decay channels. Our results reveal that symmetry-restoration QME can arise even when parity is preserved only as a weak Liouvillian symmetry, with quantum jumps mixing the Hilbert-space parity sectors. The anomalous relaxation is governed by initial-state-dependent filtering of the leading slow Liouvillian modes, providing a mechanism for symmetry-restoration QME beyond strongly conserved symmetry sectors.

papers.title: Lieb-Robinson Light Cones in Long-Range Bosonic Systems
papers.abstract: Lieb-Robinson bounds formulate emergent causality in quantum many-body dynamics. In this Letter, we study interacting bosonic systems with long-range interactions, in which both the standard assumptions of short-range interactions and uniformly bounded local energy scales are absent. We derive upper and lower bounds whose effective light-cone exponents are governed by a nontrivial interplay between the decay exponent $α$ and the bosonic interaction order $p$. The propagation protocol concentrates bosons within blocks, creating a mediating sublattice with amplified interactions. For $p\ge4$ and $2d<α\le2d+1$, the resulting exponents coincide, determining the optimal leading light-cone power. The upper bound includes $α=2d+1$ with arbitrarily small exponent loss, using a fixed-$k$ extension of the bounded-interaction result. Our results reveal that the interplay between long-range couplings and unbounded bosonic degrees of freedom gives rise to a richer light-cone structure than in either long-range bounded systems or short-range bosonic systems alone.

papers.title: Zero mode, Zero influence: Spatial-derivative coupling in particle detectors
papers.abstract: It is common in particle detector models in cavity QED to often omit zero modes or assume their state, compromising causality or introducing ambiguity in their predictions. We show that spatial-derivative coupling eliminates both problems. For free massless scalar fields in static periodic or Neumann cavities of any spatial dimension, cavity-frame spatial derivatives annihilate the zero-mode operator while preserving microcausality. Detector dynamics and entanglement harvesting then depend only on the reduced detector-oscillator state, nonperturbatively and even with initial correlations with the zero mode. Time derivatives and moving-detector rest-frame spatial derivatives can retain zero-mode state dependence not compromising causality. Realized through current coupling in superconducting circuits, spatial-derivative coupling thus makes zero-mode state assumptions unnecessary.

papers.title: Exhaustive Construction of Generalized Parent Hamiltonians for Matrix Product States
papers.abstract: Characterizing local Hamiltonians that host interesting many-body states as eigenstates has been an important problem in quantum many-body physics. For matrix product states (MPS), there is a well-known construction of parent Hamiltonians that have the MPS as the frustration-free ground state. However, recent results on quantum many-body scars have shown that such a construction does not exhaust all possible Hamiltonians that have the MPS as an eigenstate. In this work, we develop an exhaustive construction of generalized parent Hamiltonians that have a given translation-invariant MPS as an eigenstate. These go beyond the conventional projector-based construction of frustration-free parent Hamiltonians, where each local Hermitian term has the MPS as an eigenstate, by allowing non-Hermitian telescoping terms that cancel out with periodic boundary conditions (PBC). We derive a local tensor equation that establishes a correspondence between inequivalent classes of generalized parent Hamiltonians, i.e., those that cannot be related using linear combinations with frustration-free Hamiltonians, and the MPS transfer matrix spectrum. We illustrate the connection to intrinsic physical properties, including non-Abelian symmetries and zero correlation length, and further extend this construction to block-injective MPS. Our framework hence provides a systematic bridge between generalized parent Hamiltonians and the local structure of quantum states.

papers.title: Solvable coupled cluster states in $d=\infty$ with prescribed momentum distribution
papers.abstract: Two of the most successful ideas in many-body theory, the exponential coupled cluster ansatz and DMFT, have to date developed separately. We establish a connection between them, by showing that the infinite dimensional limit of the hypercubic lattice allows the exact closed-form evaluation of static expectation values of coupled cluster wave functions, provided the cluster amplitudes admit a low-rank decomposition. As a result, evaluation errors -- a serious concern in conventional coupled cluster theory -- can be disentangled from limitations to expressivity of coupled cluster states. For this family of coupled cluster states, the cavity construction in $d\to\infty$ exactly reduces the environment of a lattice site to a Gaussian Grassmann kernel, and irreducible diagrams for one-body expectation values are found to be site-diagonal (in analogy to the DMFT self-energy). The resulting ``impurity problem" is an integral over a finite number of Grassmann variables rather than a dynamical quantum impurity problem, so that static observables derive exactly from a static self-consistency condition: a wave function counterpart of DMFT. For the simplest case of a cluster amplitude restricted to rank-one doubles, we obtain the momentum distribution in closed form. We show that any momentum distribution can be realized by a state that is the exact and unique ground state of an explicit parent Hamiltonian with a gapless single-particle tunnelling spectrum. By construction these coupled cluster states variationally recover low order perturbation theory for the Hubbard model. Their failure in the strong coupling regime near the Mott transition diagnoses a fundamental limitation of coupled cluster doubles. Intriguingly, our family of coupled cluster wave functions includes a gapless state with zero quasiparticle weight, with a momentum distribution that is completely smooth at the Fermi energy.

papers.title: Physically-motivated primitive path analysis of entangled polymer networks
papers.abstract: Physical entanglements between polymer chains demonstrably enhance the modulus, strength, and toughness of elastomers and gels. However, it remains difficult to directly relate entanglement micromechanics to their macroscopic mechanical benefits. Experimentally investigating entanglements is difficu…

papers.title: Quantifying irreversibility of quantum channels via dual maps
papers.abstract: The irreversibility of quantum channels is directly linked to both exact quantum error correction and the data-processing inequality, and plays a key role in quantum information theory. In this work, we introduce a quantifier for irreversibility of quantum channels using normalized dual maps, which …

papers.title: Extraordinary light transmission through a zero-mode waveguide at the Brewster angle
papers.abstract: In optics, Brewster’s effect is a significant phenomenon widely used in photonics and laser physics to control radiation polarization at the interface between two dielectric media. In this work, we show that the Brewster effect is clearly evident when light passes through a small nanohole made in a …

papers.title: Rare-Event Quantum Sensing Using Logical Qubits
papers.abstract: Integrating quantum error correction into a sensing protocol improves detection of rare events in noisy environment.

papers.title: Measuring the complete set of spatial Schmidt modes of entangled two-photon fields
papers.abstract: Spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) is the most widely used source of high-dimensional entangled two-photon states, and the entanglement in the spatial degree of freedom is considered best suited for harnessing high-dimensional advantages. Although the Schmidt basis provides a natural choi…

papers.title: Resolving phonons in superconductor Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+δ at sub-unit-cell resolution
papers.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 06 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77617-7The role of phonons in cuprate superconductivity remains debated, partly because their layered structures host complex lattice dynamics. Here, sub-unit-cell spectroscopy resolves layer-localized phonons in Bi-2212 and reveals a spatial correlation between superstructure-driven phonon frequency modulations and superconducting gap variations.

papers.title: Full-sunlight-driven photocatalytic recovery of critical metals from spent lithium-ion batteries via organic acid leaching
papers.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 06 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78307-0Researchers developed a light-driven method using organic acids to recover critical metals from used lithium-ion batteries, offering a more sustainable route for battery recycling powered by natural sunlight.

papers.title: Provable circuit-level thresholds for non-abelian topological phases
papers.abstract: We provide an explicit scheme to realize a quantum memory in any 2D non-chiral topological order. For this, we construct syndrome extraction circuits based on the Turaev-Viro path integral as well as a classical algorithm for decoding on the fly. We prove that our scheme has a threshold under a local stochastic circuit-level noise model and discuss how to generalize it to implement topological logical gates.

papers.title: Hyperpolarity of polar foliations of codimension two
papers.abstract: We consider polar foliations of codimension two on compact simply connected irreducible symmetric spaces. In rank at least two, we prove that these foliations are hyperpolar, settling the remaining case of the hyperpolarity problem discussed by Lytchak. We show that, for irreducible spherical Coxeter quotients, the horizontal universal cover fails to be a spherical building precisely on the Cayley plane, where every such foliation is congruent to one of the two known homogeneous models.

papers.title: An Accelerated Proximal Gradient Method for Bures-Wasserstein Space
papers.abstract: We study composite optimization over the Bures--Wasserstein (BW) space of Gaussian measures. Our main observation is that a useful class of BW problems can be lifted into the Euclidean space of affine transport maps, such that the lifted problems can be solved efficiently using accelerated proximal gradient methods. For objectives whose smooth and nonsmooth components admit convex smooth and convex proximable affine lifts, respectively, our algorithm BW-FISTA achieves minimax-optimal objective gap $O(k^{-2})$ after $k$ iterations. We verify these regularity conditions for potential and interaction energies together with common spectral regularizers, and we treat stochastic gradients under a suitable noise model. As a principal application, we consider Gaussian variational inference with a log-concave, log-smooth target. Here, the resulting entropy term is handled by an efficient, exact proximal step, and we improve the previous rate of $O(k^{-1})$ to $O(k^{-2})$. We numerically verify this predicted boost with synthetic experiments.

papers.title: Almost sure bounds and tail phases for critical non-Gaussian holomorphic chaos
papers.abstract: Gu and Zhang asked for almost sure upper and lower bounds on the Taylor coefficients $a_n$ of $\exp(\sum_{k\ge1}X_kz^k/\sqrt{k})$ in the unit disc, and for the dependence of these bounds on the input tail. For independent, identically distributed, rotationally invariant complex inputs with $\mathbb E|X_1|^2=1$, we prove the universal almost sure bound $|a_n|=O((\log n)^{1/4})$. Almost surely, $\limsup_{n\to\infty}|a_n|/(\log n)^{1/4}$ is positive and finite exactly when $\mathbb E[|X_1|^2\log^+|X_1|^2]<\infty$, and is zero otherwise. For each input law, we define a deterministic scale such that, almost surely, the coefficients are bounded exactly when the scale is bounded, and tend to zero exactly when it vanishes. We also determine the almost sure logarithmic growth exponent as the maximum of contributions from collective fluctuations and individual large inputs. Explicit tails exhibit distinct thresholds for boundedness and for upper bounds at the scale in the phase criteria. Examples show that neither the leading tail nor the set of finite logarithmic moments determines the almost sure phase.

papers.title: Symplectic singularities in Relative Langlands duality for products of general linear groups
papers.abstract: It was shown by Braverman-Finkelberg-Nakajima that the regular perverse sheaf on the affine Grassmannian of type A is isomorphic to the ring object associated to a Gelfand-Tsetlin quiver. We use this result to identify, for any finite dimensional representation $\mathbf{N}$ of a product of general linear groups, the relative Langlands dual $(T^*\mathbf{N})^\vee$ of $T^*\mathbf{N}$ with the Coulomb branch of a suitable representation. By a result of Bellamy, this implies that $(T^*\mathbf{N})^\vee$ has symplectic singularities.

papers.title: Quantum Knowledge Distillation: State-of-the-art, Applications and Open Problems
papers.abstract: Knowledge distillation transfers predictions, representations, or other supervisory information between learning models and is increasingly investigated in quantum machine learning. Its applications extend beyond compression to cross-architecture transfer, circuit approximation, distributed learning, and classical deployment of models trained using quantum-derived supervision. This survey reviews these approaches using two complementary classification axes: teacher-student configuration and the role of quantum resources in the distillation process. Quantum-inspired methods are discussed separately from methods that simulate quantum computations classically or execute them on quantum hardware. We explain how measurement probabilities, expectation values, classical readouts, state overlaps, and circuit-level objectives support different transfer mechanisms. We then critically assess the presented results against baseline design, execution conditions, uncertainty, and resource costs. The evidence shows that distillation can improve selected quantum students, but benefits are task- and architecture-dependent, and several studies find negligible gains or even performance degradation. Evaluations on physical quantum hardware remain limited, with some testing individual quantum components rather than complete learning pipelines. Heterogeneous protocols and incomplete resource reporting prevent general conclusions about practical quantum advantage. We identify priorities for controlled benchmarking, noise-aware learning, reproducible evaluation, and efficient transfer between quantum and classical models.

papers.title: Room-Temperature Quantum Emission from Boron Nitride Nanotubes
papers.abstract: Quantum information systems such as quantum key distribution and quantum communications require bright, high-purity, stable sources of single photons to act as carriers of quantum information. As such, methods for obtaining single photon emitters (SPEs) in solid-state devices capable of articulating with quantum photonic circuits are a necessary obstacle that must be overcome. Hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) flakes have been extensively studied as a host material for SPEs, though working in two dimensions is accompanied by engineering complexity. However, dimensionality can be reduced through the implementation of boron nitride nanotubes (BNNTs). Here we investigate the potential of BNNTs as room-temperature SPEs using confocal photoluminescence microscopy and Hanbury Brown-Twiss interferometry. Quantum emitters were found in BNNTs spanning the entirety of the visible spectrum, including spectral regions where SPEs within hBN have not been reported. Furthermore, each tube was found to possess multiple SPEs at varying emission wavelengths along the length, exhibiting lifetimes as fast as 0.5 ns, which is about two-fold faster than the fastest hBN SPEs. Additionally, we demonstrate that surface passivation/coating mitigates blinking events, therefore increasing the emitter stability. Thus, BNNTs can function as a single structure supporting a variety of multiwavelength SPE sources, while maintaining a compact radius of ~25 nm, making them ideally suited for deterministic placement and integration within nanophotonic devices such as waveguides and interferometric filters.

papers.title: Adversarial Training with Large Step Sizes: Implicit Bias, Optimization, and Sharpness
papers.abstract: Adversarial Training (AT) is an important method for improving model robustness. We study the dynamics of deterministic Gradient Descent (GD) in AT. Most existing works in this direction focus on the small or vanishing step sizes regime, where GD resembles a continuous-time flow. However, such step sizes can make training inefficient and are rarely used in practice. In this paper, we study the AT dynamics of GD with large constant step sizes. We first study GD in adversarial linear logistic regression, focusing on two aspects: where the model parameters converge (implicit bias) and how quickly the losses decrease (optimization). We then turn to neural networks training and study how the sharpness of losses evolve during AT. Our results advance the understanding of the behaviors of GD with large step sizes in AT and highlight three key differences from its behavior in Standard Training (ST): (i) the implicit bias gap between AT and ST, previously established only for small step sizes, persists for arbitrarily large constant step sizes, (ii) different from ST, there is no uniform rate of convergence for the optimization error in AT, and (iii) sharpness can exhibit two-stage dynamics that differ from the Edge-of-Stability behavior observed in ST.

papers.title: Tusnády's problem and online two-sample thinning
papers.abstract: We determine the sharp order of discrepancy in Tusnády's problem in every fixed dimension $d\ge 2$. The largest combinatorial discrepancy of $N$ points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with respect to axis-parallel boxes is $Θ_d((\log N)^{d-1/2})$, extending Wei's planar result and matching Nikolov's upper bound. More strongly, with high probability, this lower bound holds simultaneously for every subset obtained by deleting at most a sufficiently small fixed fraction of a uniform $N$-point sample. We apply this geometric estimate to online thinning of two independent samples of size $n$ from an unknown common distribution, where observations must be kept or discarded upon arrival. For every fixed dimension $k\ge 1$ and expected deletion budget $ρn$, with $0<ρ<2$, we prove that the minimax expected prefix discrepancy over lower orthants is $Θ_{k,ρ}((\log n)^{k+1/2})$. In dimension one, the optimal terminal discrepancy is instead $Θ_ρ((\log\log n)^{3/2})$, giving a sharp separation between the prefix and terminal objectives. For $k\ge 2$, we obtain terminal bounds differing by a factor of $\log n$. The lower bounds are based on Gaussian small-ball estimates for box-incidence matrices, while the upper bounds use stationary Metropolis thinning and, in one dimension, a terminal cancellation procedure.

papers.title: On do Carmo's Question: The Properly Embedded Case
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove that every complete noncompact two-sided properly embedded constant mean curvature hypersurface of finite Morse index in Euclidean space is minimal. The result holds in every dimension. We assume no bounds on curvature or volume growth. This establishes the properly embedded case of the finite-index version of do Carmo's question. For nonzero mean curvature, we use the radii of inscribed balls to define a positive weight. This weight gives a polynomial bound on weighted volume, while its reciprocal satisfies a differential inequality involving the Jacobi operator. We combine these properties with stability outside a compact set to obtain finite total area. This leads to a contradiction.

papers.title: h-dichotomies via noncritical uniformity and expansiveness for noninvertible evolution families
papers.abstract: We establish characterizations of h-dichotomies for noninvertible evolution families acting on Banach spaces, in terms of appropriate notions of expansiveness and uniform noncriticality. Our results extend the corresponding characterizations previously obtained for invertible evolution families. To the best of our knowledge, no such characterizations have previously been established for general noninvertible evolution families. A key difference is that noninvertibility makes the structure of the stable spaces more delicate: in our positive-half-line result, finite codimension must be imposed at every time, rather than only at the initial time. We show by an example that the latter, weaker condition is insufficient. We also study evolution families on the negative half-line, using duality to obtain corresponding characterizations in terms of dual expansiveness and dual uniform noncriticality. General growth rates are treated by a time-rescaling argument.

papers.title: Improved Index and Intersection bounds for Min-Max Geodesics
papers.abstract: In this note, we show that the sum of the Morse index and number of intersections of min-max geodesics achieving the p-widths of a closed surface are bounded above by $p$, improving a result from our previous work. A key idea is that deformations coming from vertex desingularization and eigenfunctions of the Jacobi operator on geodesics are sufficiently independent.

papers.title: Gelfand numbers of Schatten class embeddings in the quasi-Banach range
papers.abstract: We prove Conjecture 1.4 of Prochno and Strzelecki [J. Approx. Theory 277 (2022), 105736] on Gelfand numbers of embeddings between finite-dimensional Schatten classes. For $0<p\le1$ and indices bounded away from the ambient dimension by a fixed proportion, we obtain the conjectured lower bound, uniformly in the target exponent $2\le q\le\infty$. Together with the known upper estimate obtained by Hinrichs, Prochno and Vybíral [Math. Ann., 380(3-4):1563-1593, 2021], this gives the exact asymptotic order in the previously unresolved range. As a consequence, we obtain a complete all-index description by combining our result with the estimates of Hinrichs, Prochno and Vybíral and of Prochno and Strzelecki. The proof is deterministic and is based on Hilbert--Schmidt projections on rectangular matrix spaces.

papers.title: A Central Limit Theorem For Random Variables Under A Constraint
papers.abstract: We consider vectors chosen randomly from high-dimensional hypersurfaces of the form $\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n: \sum_{j=1}^n V_j(x_j)=an\}$. These in general asymmetric surfaces generalize classical spheres and include unbounded and disconnected surfaces. We show that under mild assumptions as $n\to\infty$, any weighted sum of the random coordinates is asymptotically Gaussian, provided that no weight dominates. An explicit reduction in the variance compared to the unconstrained case is observed. We also study a model with penalization of deviations from the constraint, interpolating between the unconstrained and the constrained case. Our approach involves an explicit representation of the characteristic function of the constrained random variables in terms of independent random variables.

papers.title: DiffSequence-Q: Diffusion Design with Quantum Assistance for Biologically Active Proteins
papers.abstract: Designing protein sequences that satisfy both secondary structure requirements and solubility targets remains challenging. We present DiffSequence-Q, a hybrid multinomial diffusion model conditioned on secondary structure at each residue and a continuous solubility target. To introduce quantum auxiliary supervision during training, we employ a quantum neural network (QNN) or quantum Kolmogorov-Arnold network (QKAN) as an auxiliary solubility prediction head over shared Transformer representations. The auxiliary prediction loss is jointly optimized with the diffusion objective, allowing quantum auxiliary supervision to influence the learned denoising model. Once trained, protein sequences are generated entirely through classical reverse diffusion. On the CATH benchmark, DiffSequence-Q achieved the highest secondary structure recovery among the four evaluated models for complete sequence generation. Evaluation with a separately trained solubility prediction model showed that the best QNN and QKAN configurations achieved mean predicted solubility scores 14.0% and 22.7% higher than the multilayer perceptron (MLP) baseline, respectively. Experimental characterization further demonstrated biological activity across three distinct protein families. Selected defensins exhibited pronounced inhibitory activity against Aspergillus niger, while xylanases and short-chain dehydrogenases exhibited substantial enzymatic activity. Together, these results support DiffSequence-Q as a framework for integrating structural requirements and solubility targets in protein generation, with experimentally demonstrated biological activity.

papers.title: An improved minimum degree threshold for fractional clique decompositions in partite graphs
papers.abstract: We prove a Dirac-type condition for an $r$-partite graph to admit a fractional clique decomposition: every sufficiently large $r$-partite graph with $n$ vertices in each part and partite minimum degree at least $(1 - \frac{1}{30r^2}) n$ admits a fractional $K_r$-decomposition, subject to necessary divisibility conditions. This implies the same upper bound on the asymptotic minimum degree threshold for $r$-partite graphs to admit a $K_r$-decomposition, using a well-known reduction.

papers.title: Preconditioning for the time-dependent Stokes equations: stage-weighted Radau IIA and weighted discontinuous Galerkin time-stepping
papers.abstract: We determine field-of-values equivalent preconditioners for the time-dependent Stokes equations discretized in time by stage-weighted Radau IIA Runge--Kutta time-stepping and discontinuous Galerkin time-stepping methods. By weighing each stage of the Radau IIA Runge--Kutta method differently we obtain preconditioners that are field-of-values equivalent, with constants independent of viscosity, timestep, and mesh size, to the system matrix. Similarly, by using weighted inner products in time to define the discontinuous Galerkin time-stepping method, we again obtain field-of-values equivalent preconditioners for the resulting system matrix. Numerical experiments are performed in two and three-dimensions which demonstrate robustness of the proposed preconditioners.

papers.title: Quantum enhanced beam displacement estimation: sensitivity limits, optimal probes, and measurement schemes
papers.abstract: We investigate the ultimate sensitivity limits for measuring small transverse beam displacements and identify optimal strategies that attain them, using the framework of mode parameter estimation. We contrast two families of states with different resource constraints, using Hermite-Gauss and Laguerre-Gauss mode pairs. First, for fixed total photon number states, the optimal state is identified and we show that it asymptotically approaches a rotated NOON state. The sensitivity bound is compared to that of an asymptotically optimal pure Gaussian state with fixed average photon number. Finally, we propose concrete measurement schemes using the method of moments and show that the twin-Fock state may provide a viable alternative to the rotated NOON state for this task. Our work provides a broader benchmark for developing practical strategies for spatial sensing at the quantum limit.

papers.title: Disorder-blind Mpemba acceleration of quantum state preparation
papers.abstract: Using the strong Mpemba effect to accelerate relaxation by initial-state design requires suppressing the slowest mode, which typically needs prior knowledge of the system. However, in disordered systems, this mode is sample-dependent, so a fixed preparation generally retains a slow-mode overlap. We show that a ``blind'' preparation, designed from the clean chain without knowledge of the disorder realisation or its distribution, can start farther from stationarity yet overtake a reference in typical samples of a dephased disordered XX chain. It requires only the chain geometry and the particle number. At strong dephasing, the density dynamics maps to a resistor chain, and an exact inverse-generator identity links the residual overlap to the spatial resistance profile. We find two distinct thresholds: a finite mean resistance suffices for diffusion, but the residual overlap decays as $L^{-1/2}$ with chain length $L$ only when the resistance variance is finite; rare weak links slow this decay. We predict the fraction of samples in which the blind preparation wins, which is an ensemble-level measure of its reliability. Finite-size calculations support both scaling regimes with interactions at strong dephasing. We give preparation circuits and a density readout for the residual overlap.

papers.title: Spheres with transitive families of CMC hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: The goal of this paper is to investigate the following question: what geometric restrictions does the existence of a transitive family of constant mean curvature hyperspheres impose on a Riemannian metric on $\mathbb S^n$? The notion of a transitive family can be made precise through the theory of Zoll families developed by Ambrozio, Marques, and Neves. Within this framework, we partially extend their local rigidity theorem for even conformal factors on $\mathbb S^3$ to every dimension $n\ge4$, assuming each hypersphere in the minimal Zoll family has the area of a round equator. Moreover, we give a partial answer to the following higher-dimensional version of a question posed by Robert Bryant: must a metric on $\mathbb S^n$, conformal to the round metric and admitting a Zoll family of hyperspheres with a common nonzero constant mean curvature, have constant sectional curvature? Finally, we also investigate inverse problems in the spirit of Hangan, asking which metrics make a fixed family of geodesic spheres have a common prescribed mean curvature.

papers.title: Data-driven discovery of intrinsic Lie point symmetries of differential equation systems
papers.abstract: Discovering continuous symmetries directly from differential-equation data can reveal geometric structure for model reduction and scientific machine learning without symbolic determining equations or a closed-form representation of the governing system. We formulate intrinsic Lie point-symmetry discovery as an operator-theoretic problem on sampled jet-space data. Admissible generators are identified from a sampled determining operator and separated from redundant, solution-dependent, and geometrically trivial directions. The framework combines prolongation, sequential subspace restrictions, and a fixed nonlinear dictionary linear in trainable coefficients. A rank-stabilization preflight test diagnoses systems whose represented intrinsic symmetry algebra does not stabilize under dictionary refinement. On a controlled differential-equation benchmark with an analytically known 11-dimensional represented intrinsic symmetry algebra, the method recovers the complete represented generator set, reproduces its Lie-bracket structure to numerical precision, and approximates a known generator beyond the training domain. Here we show that explicit intrinsic continuous-symmetry generators can be recovered from data obtained from exact or approximate differential systems.

papers.title: A half-line of Schur idempotent norms
papers.abstract: Using a family of bipartite graphs constructed by hanging identical rooted trees at every vertex of a highly symmetric graph, we show that every sufficiently large real number is the norm of an idempotent Schur multiplier on the bounded operators on $\ell^2$. This answers a question previously raised by the author.

papers.title: $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$- and $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$-invariant multidifferential operators
papers.abstract: We determine the dimension of the space of $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$-invariant (n)-ary differential operators on weighted densities for arbitrary weights, including the singular cases in which the usual elimination procedure breaks down. The proof relies on the strong Lefschetz property established by Stanley \cite{s} and Watanabe \cite{w}. We also investigate the corresponding problem in the super case.

papers.title: Low-Temperature Sampling via Equilibrium Disagreements
papers.abstract: We develop a new framework for sampling at low temperatures using Glauber dynamics. In this regime, the coexistence of competing modes (commonly referred to as phases) creates bottlenecks that can make worst-case mixing exponentially slow. The main new ingredient in our framework is to relate convergence within a phase to the geometry of disagreements between two independent configurations drawn from that phase. As applications of our approach, we consider three canonical models on random regular graphs that have been central to low-temperature sampling, and establish fast convergence from natural initialisations of Glauber dynamics for every fixed degree. We show: --- For the hard-core model on random bipartite $d$-regular graphs, Glauber dynamics initialised from either one-sided independent set mixes within the corresponding phase in $n^{3/2+o(1)}$ steps throughout the non-uniqueness regime $λ>λ_c(d)$. --- For the random-cluster model on random $d$-regular graphs, for every real $q>2$, Glauber dynamics initialised from the all-in edge set mixes within the ordered phase in $n^{3/2+o(1)}$ steps for all $β\geq β_c$. Similarly, Glauber dynamics initialised from the all-out edge set mixes within the disordered phase in $n^{3/2+o(1)}$ steps for $β\leq β_c$. --- For the ferromagnetic Ising model on random $d$-regular graphs, Glauber dynamics initialised from all-plus or all-minus mixes within the corresponding phase in $n^{3/2+o(1)}$ steps throughout the low-temperature regime $β>β_c(d)$. We also give an $n^{2+o(1)}$-time algorithm that combines phase samples into samples from the full distribution, avoiding in particular time-costly approximations of the corresponding partition functions to the target sampling accuracy.

papers.title: Shades and Convexity of Hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: Let $f\colon M^n\to\mathbf{R}^{n+1}$, $n\geq2$, be a smooth immersion of a closed oriented manifold, with Gauss map $ν\colon M\to\mathbf{S}^n$. For each unit vector $u$, the shade $S_u\subset M$ is the set of points where $ν$ makes an acute angle with $u$. We show that $f$ is a convex embedding if and only if every shade is contractible. More generally, if every shade is $k$-connected, then $f$ is a convex embedding provided that $n\leq 2k+1$, or $n=2k+2$ and $H_{k+1}(M;\mathbf{Z})=0$. On the other hand, for every $n\geq 2k+3$ there is a nonconvex embedding $f\colon\mathbf{S}^n\to\mathbf{R}^{n+1}$ all of whose shades are $k$-connected. These results give sharp answers to a question of H. Wente in all dimensions.

papers.title: Averages of sub-additive functions through non-Følner sequences
