Nesterov's scientific career, then introduce the language of oracle complexity together with a classification of objective function models (geometric, algebraic, and structural), and subsequently discuss his main results in chronological order: the fast gradient method, fast automatic differentiation, the theory of self-concordant barriers and polynomial-time interior-point methods, the $π/2$ theorem, the stable dynamics model of traffic flows, the smoothing technique, primal-dual methods, cubic regularization of Newton's method, the modified Gauss--Newton scheme, coordinate descent methods and methods for huge-scale problems, gradient-free methods, universal gradient methods, implementable tensor methods, and "superfast" methods. Each topic is accompanied by historical background, precise statements specifying the problem class, oracle, and type of guarantee, examples, and a discussion of the current state of the art.

papers.title: Sleep-Disordered Breathing Detection with Quantum Recurrent Neural Networks
papers.abstract: This work investigates the application of Quantum Recurrent Neural Networks to the binary classification of sleep-disordered breathing events in time-series data, aiming to distinguish between apneic and normal breathing episodes. A variational classical--quantum architecture is proposed and evaluated against classical Recurrent Neural Network models. Experiments were conducted on multiple real-world datasets with varying levels of complexity to assess the strengths and limitations of the quantum approach. In the comparative analysis, both classical and quantum models showed comparable performance. The quantum model achieved superior performance on the smallest dataset, while yielding slightly weaker results in the most complex setting. However, the quantum approach exhibited notable strengths, such as competitive performance despite a drastically reduced parameter count and low-qubit regime, as well as good generalization capabilities. These results suggest that, despite current hardware and algorithmic limitations, variational quantum recurrent models represent a promising alternative for time-series classification as Quantum Computing technologies continue to mature.

papers.title: Matrix-weighted $Z$-spaces and tent spaces:characterizations, duality and interpolation
papers.abstract: Let $α\in\mathbb R$, $0<p<\infty$, $0<q,r\le\infty$, and $W$ be a matrix $\mathcal A_p$ weight on ${\mathbb R}^n$. We introduce the matrix-weighted $Z$-spaces $Z^{p,q,r}_α(W)$ and tent spaces $T^{p,q,r}_α(W)$ on the upper half-space and establish their characterizations using reducing operators. We then characterize homogeneous matrix-weighted Besov and Triebel--Lizorkin spaces in terms of the corresponding $Z$-spaces and tent spaces, respectively, using Schwartz kernels satisfying Tauberian and finite moment conditions. Furthermore, we establish duality for the matrix-weighted $Z$-spaces and tent spaces and obtain real and complex interpolation results for these spaces and the associated homogeneous matrix-weighted Besov and Triebel--Lizorkin spaces.

papers.title: Four problems about the irreducible determined $T_0$-topologies
papers.abstract: We answer four questions on irreducible determined $T_0$-topologies and a related question on monotone determined topologies posed by Xu, Yang and Luo (Topology Appl.\ 382 (2026), 109762). For every $T_0$ topology $τ$, the family $τ_r$ used to define its irreducible-derived topology is already a topology and preserves all nonempty irreducible subsets and their closures. Consequently, the least irreducible determined refinement is obtained in one step: $τ_r=\rd(τ)=\Rd(τ)$. For an arbitrary poset $P$, we describe the weakest order-compatible irreducible determined topology $ρ(P)$ using Dedekind--MacNeille cuts and a finite-cover condition involving principal lower sets. The Scott space of the binary-prefix domain provides a common counterexample to saturated heredity for irreducible determined spaces and monotone determined spaces: its maximal-point subspace is Cantor space. We also describe $ρ(P)$-closure by iterating an irreducible-cut operator, characterize Scott continuity of this operator, and give an example requiring two applications of the cut operator. A finite-decomposition condition extends the topology and closure-preservation results to general subset systems. For the Rudin and well-filtered determined systems, we exhibit a common $T_1$ example whose first and second derived topologies are the co-countable and discrete topologies, respectively. Thus the first derived topology need not be determined by the same subset system.

papers.title: Asymptotic Optimality of $cμ$-Rule for LLM Inference Scheduling under Memory Constraint
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) inference, the process by which a pre-trained model receives an input prompt and generates output tokens sequentially, has become increasingly important with the widespread deployment of LLM-based applications. As inference workloads continue to scale, GPU memory has emerged as a critical bottleneck: the long input prompts and generation sequences common in agentic and reasoning workloads lead to substantial key-value (KV) cache usage. In this paper, we study the resulting online scheduling problem from a queueing perspective. Requests arrive stochastically with heterogeneous prompt and output lengths, undergo prefill and autoregressive decode, and compete for a finite KV-cache capacity. Unlike classical queueing models, the duration of a processing step depends on both prefill computation and KV-cache I/O, so service capacity is jointly determined by computation, memory access, and memory occupancy. We develop a fluid model that reduces the system to a multiclass single-server queue with effective service rates capturing computation, memory access, and memory capacity. This fluid analysis yields a $cμ$ priority rule, where the effective service rate $μ$ is jointly determined by computational speed, memory bandwidth, and memory capacity. We prove that this rule minimizes cumulative holding cost in the fluid model and, for a finite workload, also minimizes completion time and maximizes full-run output-token throughput. We then construct a feasible scheduling policy for the original finite system and prove that its scaled dynamics converge to the optimal fluid policy. Finally, experiments on a real LLM serving engine using an NVIDIA H800 show that practical implementations of the proposed priority rule substantially reduce average latency while maintaining high throughput relative to existing scheduling policies.

papers.title: Pushforwards of lc pairs under morphisms to abelian varieties
papers.abstract: Let $f$ be a morphism from a log canonical pair $(X,Δ)$ to an abelian variety $A$ and $D\sim_{\mathbb Q}m(K_X+Δ)$ a Cartier divisor on $X$ with $m>1$ a rational number. We prove that $f_*\mathcal{O}_X(D)$ is globally generated after pullback by an isogeny. Our methods involve birational geometry, mixed Hodge modules and singular Hermitian metrics with the minimal extension property. Moreover, we provide simple counterexamples where the above result fails for plt pairs when $m=1$ and where the existence of Chen--Jiang decompositions fails for plt pairs for any $m\ge1$.

papers.title: Generic factorizations and alternating direction method for fixed-rank approximation of matrix polynomials
papers.abstract: We present an algorithm for approximating a given matrix polynomial of degree $d$ by a matrix polynomial of prescribed rank and degree at most $d$. The method builds on recent advances in the theory of generic eigenstructures and factorizations of matrix polynomials with bounded rank and degree. We also give a specialized treatment of the case of matrix pencils (degree one matrix polynomials), motivated by its particular theoretical and practical importance. Lastly, numerical experiments are reported to assess the performance of the proposed approach and to compare it with existing methods.

papers.title: Regularity of geodesics in the spaces of convex and plurisubharmonic functions III
papers.abstract: In this note, we study the regularity of solutions to the geodesic equation in the space of plurisubharmonic functions in a general Reinhardt domain. Our findings resolve a problem left open from our previous note [AD26].

papers.title: Hidden Symmetries of the Kepler Problem and Jacobi's Theorem
papers.abstract: We present a geometric derivation of the hidden symmetries of the Kepler problem, combining a duality for central-force systems, obtained by interchanging positions and velocities, with a generalized form of Jacobi's theorem. Applied to the dual Kepler problem, this theorem identifies Kepler hodographs of prescribed energy with geodesics of a metric of constant curvature. After adjoining one point at infinity, the resulting geometry is complete. Its Killing vector fields induce a finite-dimensional Lie algebra of infinitesimal symmetries on the corresponding energy hypersurface. The distinguished point at infinity determines a canonical decomposition of the Killing algebra into two vector subspaces, whose associated Noether invariants recover angular momentum and the Runge-Lenz vector.

papers.title: Space--time Runge approximation for weakly viscous nonlocal waves and identification of coefficients
papers.abstract: We study very weak solutions and Runge approximation for weakly viscous nonlocal wave equations with elastic term $(-Δ)^su$ and dissipative term $(-Δ)^r\partial_tu$, where $0\leq r<s$. For time-dependent potentials satisfying a smallness condition, we establish a transposition theory for sources in the dual of the natural space--time energy space. Under explicit nonlocality and nonresonance assumptions, we prove Runge approximation in $L^2(0,T;\widetilde H^s(Ω))$ and in $L^2(0,T;\widetilde H^s(Ω)) \cap H^1_0(0,T;\widetilde H^r(Ω))$. As an application, partial exterior Dirichlet-to-Neumann measurements uniquely determine a bounded, nonnegative, time-dependent coefficient in the nonlinear velocity damping term $q|\partial_tu|^{p-2}\partial_tu$ for $0<r<s$ and $2<p\leq 2+4r/n$. The proof establishes the small-amplitude response by energy estimates, weighted $L^p$ monotonicity convergence, and a linear Green identity, then applies adjoint Runge approximation followed by a forward velocity approximation in $L^2$. No smallness or positive lower bound is imposed on the nonlinear damping coefficient.

papers.title: On the Onsager--Machlup functional of the infinite-dimensional angular central Gaussian distribution and related measures
papers.abstract: The Onsager--Machlup functional of a probability measure is a generalisation of the negative logarithm of the probability density function, defined precisely using the ratios of masses of balls in the limit of vanishing radius. It plays an important role in several areas of applied mathematics because its minimisers can be understood as modes of the measure. We show that the Onsager--Machlup functional of the angular central Gaussian measure on the unit sphere of an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space---i.e., the radial projection of a centred Gaussian measure with covariance operator $C$---is constant on the finite-dimensional sphere spanned by the eigenvectors of leading eigenvalue under $C$, and takes the value $+\infty$ elsewhere. We discuss the consequences of this extreme concentration of mass for maximum a posteriori estimation in Bayesian inverse problems with an angular central Gaussian prior.

papers.title: On the Haagerup Vertex Operator Algebras
papers.abstract: Three constructions of vertex operator algebras realizing the Haagerup center were announced independently and almost simultaneously. The relations between these constructions are studied in this paper. The generators are expressed in a common lattice basis for $E_6\oplus A_2$. It is proved that the constructions of Riesen and Huang give isomorphic vertex operator algebras, and that this algebra and the algebra constructed by Jiao have isomorphic fixed point subalgebras under automorphisms of order two. The isomorphisms are given explicitly on generators. The common fixed point subalgebra contains the parafermion vertex operator algebras $K(\mathfrak{sl}_2,3)$ and $K(\mathfrak{sl}_2,13)$. A general rationality criterion for unitary vertex operator algebras is given in terms of positive linear combinations of conformal vectors and is applied to these constructions. The two vertex operator algebras are simple current extensions of the common fixed point subalgebra and have equivalent module categories as ribbon categories. The equivalence follows from decomposition with respect to a nondegenerate pointed subcategory with four simple objects in the module category of the common fixed point subalgebra. It is also proved that the conformal nets associated with these unitary vertex operator algebras are completely rational.

papers.title: Relative Tate-Shafarevich kernel of a reductive group over a global field
papers.abstract: We describe an algorithm and a computer program computing the relative Tate-Shafarevich kernel $Sha^S(K,G)$ of a reductive group $G$ over a global field $K$ with respect to a finite set $S$ of places of $K$ containing no archimedean places. We assume that we know the algebraic fundamental group $Λ=π_1^{alg}(G)$ together with the action on it of the Galois group $Θ=Gal(L/K)$, where $L/K$ is a finite Galois extension with no real places such that $Gal(K^s/L)$ acts trivially on $Λ$. We also assume that we know the decomposition subgroups $Θ_v\subseteq Θ$ for all places $v$ in $S$, and all non-cyclic decomposition subgroups $Θ_v$ for $v$ outside $S$. Under certain conditions, we compute the set $Sha^S(K,G)$ also when $S$ contains archimedean places.

papers.title: Temporal stretching of single-photon pulses by intra-cavity frequency conversion
papers.abstract: Spectral bandwidth and frequency mismatch between quantum light emitters and quantum components is a common problem in the realization of hybrid quantum information networks. Here we propose a simultaneous solution to both of these problems by using a free-space cavity with an embedded nonlinear crystal that, through frequency conversion, facilitates perfect coupling into a cavity mode. The slow leakage of the cavity effectively stretches the photon pulse, resulting in a much longer photon pulse at a different wavelength. We show that the amount of stretching is strictly limited by the finesse and length of the cavity. Including realistic internal losses in the cavity, we show that it is possible to stretch a photon by at least two orders of magnitude with high efficiency. The proposed setup can thus constitute a valuable addition to the toolbox of quantum information technologies.

papers.title: Counting irreducible skew polynomials $x^{2n}+ax^n+1$
papers.abstract: We give a counting formula for the coefficients $a\in\F_{p^h}$ for which $x^{2n}+ax^n+1$ is irreducible in $\F_{p^h}[x;σ]$, for arbitrary positive integers $n$ and $h$, where $σ(a)=a^p$ and $p$ is an arbitrary prime power. The proof reduces the problem to quadratic reduced norms, establishes a uniformity statement for every Frobenius generator, and counts the remaining coefficients by Möbius inversion.

papers.title: Unbounded total mean curvature with prescribed boundary metric
papers.abstract: Bär has shown that a fixed boundary metric and a scalar-curvature lower bound do not generally bound total mean curvature from above. We extend this unboundedness to every smooth compact connected manifold of dimension $n\ge3$ with nonempty boundary and every prescribed boundary metric, using scalar-flat metrics. While Bär's examples use warped products, our construction uses a nonzero cubic variation of total mean curvature near a flat product, followed by localization and conformal correction. We also construct arbitrarily $C^k$-small perturbations of the flat torical half-cylinder with nonnegative scalar curvature, unchanged boundary metric, an exact product end, and positive total boundary mean curvature.

papers.title: Real-analytic functional calculus and strictly real Banach algebras
papers.abstract: We use real-analytic functional calculus to show that the envelope of the algebra of $m$-variable polynomials with real coefficients, with respect to the class of strictly real Banach algebras, is isomorphic to the algebra of real-valued analytic functions on $\mathbb{R}^m$.

papers.title: Nonlinearity-Induced Suppression of Dissipation in Bath-Coupled Floquet Topological Insulators
papers.abstract: Topological insulators can host chiral, disorder-robust edge states that dissipate energy when coupled to an external bath. We show that nonlinear interactions enable all-optical control over edge-state dissipation in a laser-written Floquet topological insulator periodically coupled to a photonic bath. Although moderate nonlinearity enhances dissipation due to mode mixing, increasing the nonlinear strength to an optimal value dramatically suppresses dissipation by forming highly localized traveling edge solitons. These results establish engineered system-bath coupling and nonlinear interactions as a route to suppress dissipation of chiral topological edge transport.

papers.title: Increasing stability for the inverse potential problem of the fractional Helmholtz equation
papers.abstract: This paper is concerned with the inverse potential scattering problem for the three-dimensional fractional Helmholtz equation. For every $0<α<1$, we establish an increasing stability of determining the potential function from multifrequency exterior measurements of the scattered field. The stability consists of a Lipschitz data discrepancy and a logarithmic remainder that decreases when the upper measured wavenumber increases. The key ingredient in the analysis is to construct appropriate geometric optics solutions, which relate the X-ray transform of the potential to the measured fields. As a consequence, the stability is derived by applying analytic continuation. Two-dimensional numerical examples with noisy near-field data illustrate the benefit of enlarging the measured frequency band for three representative fractional orders.

papers.title: Analytical properties of the principal clamped transmission eigenpair for a planar region
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the analytical properties of the principal eigenpair for the clamped transmission eigenvalue problem, which arises in the context of biharmonic (i.e. flexural wave) scattering by a clamped planar obstacle. By deriving a suitable Rayleigh quotient, we provide rigorous proofs for several fundamental properties that were previously only observed through numerical experiments. One of the results we have shown here is that the first eigenvalue is monotone decreasing with respect to the domain. Furthermore, we prove that the corresponding eigenfunction is of a single sign, a property analogous to the principal eigenfunction of the Dirichlet eigenvalues of the Laplacian. Another key result is a Faber--Krahn type inequality, establishing that the disk minimizes the principal eigenvalue among all domains of a given measure. The theoretical results are supported by a comprehensive numerical investigation.

papers.title: Stochastic interpretation of the Water Waves equations
papers.abstract: The aim of this article is to derive a stochastic interpretation of the Water Waves equations, based on the location uncertainty principle (LU). Next, these equations are used to infer simpler models from scaling limits, such as the Saint-Venant, Boussinesq and Serre-Green-Naghdi ones. Once adapted to the stochastic setting, these models have been successfully implemented numerically, and we show several experiments to assess their properties -- for example the breaking of the wave symmetry, and the influence of time correlated noises.

papers.title: An oscillation result for slightly perturbed trigonometric series
papers.abstract: We establish that any nontrivial anharmonic Fourier series with exponents quadratically close to the positive integers changes sign on each interval of length 2$π$.

papers.title: Profinite approach to S-adic shift spaces II: Invertible directive sequences
papers.abstract: This paper is the second in a series about (relatively) free profinite semigroups and S-adic representations of minimal shifts. The first installment introduced the key notions of profinite images and saturating properties. The present paper examines the relationship between relative invertibility conditions (on a directive sequence) and charging properties (of a shift). The main result shows that the two properties are equivalent under mild conditions. Moreover, charging properties are shown to be equivalent to density of subgroups generated by return words in relatively free profinite groups. The main result can then be used to deduce purely discrete statements about subgroups generated by return words in relatively free groups. We also highlight applications of the main result to the study of maximal bifix decoding, following earlier work by the second author. Finally, we establish some results on the effect of direct images on charging properties and explain how to apply these results to the case of episturmian shifts.

papers.title: Finding Integer Roots of Polynomials in Nearly Optimal Time
papers.abstract: Let $f\in\mathbb Z[x]$ be a polynomial of degree $n$ with integer coefficients of absolute value less than $2^b$. Using Pan's approximate factorization theorem, we give a deterministic algorithm that finds all distinct integer roots of $f$ in $\widetilde O(nb)$ bit operations. This matches the bit size of the input up to logarithmic factors and does not require $f$ to be square-free. Since we were unable to verify parts of the running time analysis of Pan's theorem, we also give a self-contained deterministic algorithm with running time $\widetilde O(nb+\min(n,b)^3b^2)$, which is $\widetilde O(nb)$ whenever $b\leq n^{1/4}$. This answers a question of Harvey and Hittmeir (2022), who asked whether integer roots can be found deterministically in quasilinear time, conditionally on Pan's theorem, and unconditionally for $b\leq n^{1/4}$. The fastest previous deterministic algorithm, due to Nir, takes $\widetilde O(n^{3/2}b)$ bit operations and works only for square-free polynomials. Instead of $p$-adic lifting, we combine approximate complex root finding with exact polynomial evaluation. We first approximate the complex roots of the polynomial formed by the top $\min(n,b)+1$ coefficients of $f$. Every integer root $r$ of $f$ with $|r|\geq 2$ lies within distance $2$ of some complex root of this truncated polynomial. Rounding the real parts of the approximate roots therefore gives a list of $O(\min(n,b))$ candidate integers that is guaranteed to contain all integer roots of $f$. Although a single candidate can have up to $b$ bits, a bound via the Mahler measure shows that the bit lengths of all candidates sum to $O(b)$. This allows us to test all candidates by exact multipoint evaluation in $\widetilde O(nb)$ bit operations.

papers.title: Local resolution of the second log-Fitting ideal
papers.abstract: Logarithmic Fitting ideals encode the complexity of the corresponding morphisms in a natural and intrinsic way, and their principalisation offers a new perspective on problems such as the resolution of cotangent sheaves and the monomialisation of morphisms. In this paper, we give a local resolution theorem for log-rank adapted morphisms: after finite sequences of smooth local blow-ups, the first two log-Fitting ideals \mathcal{F}\_{n--1}(σ) and \mathcal{F}\_{n--2}(σ) become principal monomial ideals.

papers.title: Bayesian optimization enhanced magnetic field gradient detection based on spin-orbit coupled Bose-Einstein condensates
papers.abstract: Magnetic field detection is of great significance in modern fields such as medical diagnostics, geological exploration, inertial navigation, and space physics. We have previously investigated the expansion dynamics of a spin-orbit-coupled Bose-Einstein condensate. Building on these results, here we propose a scheme for magnetic-field-gradient detection by establishing a quantitative relationship between the condensate's rotational deflection angle and the magnetic-field gradient. In this work, we present the parameter dependence of this scheme and perform a systematic optimization. We introduce a Bayesian optimization algorithm to automatically and efficiently search for the optimal combination of key parameters, thereby significantly enhancing the sensitivity of the magnetic field gradient measurement. The results show that the optimized gradiometer improves the sensitivity by a factor of five. This work not only provides a new approach for magnetic field gradient measurement but also serves as a reference for machine learning-empowered quantum precision measurement.

papers.title: A Discontinuous Galerkin Framework for Efficient Simulation of Cyclic Voltammetry Models
papers.abstract: We develop a numerical framework to efficiently simulate the cyclic voltammetry models based on discontinuous Galerkin (DG) spatial discretization combined with linearly implicit Euler time integration. The method is applied to two electrochemical mechanisms: a heterogeneous electron-transfer (ET) reaction and an electron-transfer reaction coupled with a catalytic chemical step (EC'). The governing time-dependent reaction-diffusion equations are expressed in dimensionless form and discretized in space using locally defined orthonormal Legendre polynomial basis functions. This discretization leads to a system of ordinary differential equations that is subsequently advanced in time using the linearly implicit Euler method. The resulting solver, denoted $\text{DG}_{\text{Impl}}$, is evaluated through numerical experiments and compared with MATLAB's $pdepe$ solver in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency. The numerical results demonstrate the convergence of $\text{DG}_{\text{Impl}}$ with respect to spatial and temporal discretizations and show that the method accurately reproduces the voltammetric responses of both ET and EC' mechanisms. For a prescribed relative error, $\text{DG}_{\text{Impl}}$ requires less computational time than $pdepe$ in the numerical experiments considered. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed DG formulation for the forward simulation of cyclic voltammetry models and provide a numerical foundation for subsequent adjoint-based parameter-estimation and inverse-problem formulations.

papers.title: Approximating Distributions on Vertex Degrees in Random Hypergraphs via Stein's Method
papers.abstract: Complex data are increasingly represented as hypergraphs. We establish bounds for approximating joint vertex-degree distributions by independent multivariate Poisson and correlated normal distributions in hypergraph models with independent hyperedges. We discuss the approximation of the distribution under different density regimes which are further supported by simulation studies.

papers.title: Glauber Dynamics for Sampling Colorings: Rapid Mixing above $(1+1/\mathrm{e})Δ$ via Hidden Hard-Core Models
papers.abstract: We show that for every $γ>0$ and every sufficiently large $Δ$, the Glauber dynamics for proper $q$-colorings of any $n$-vertex graph of maximum degree $Δ$ has spectral gap $Ω_γ(1/n)$, and hence mixing time $O_γ(n^2\log q)$, whenever $q\ge(1+1/\mathrm{e}+γ)Δ$. Our proof establishes a Bochner-type inequality by exploiting the spectral gaps of hard-core models hidden in the color classes. The constant $1+1/\mathrm{e}\approx1.368$ comes from the uniqueness threshold $\approx\mathrm{e}/Δ$ of the hard-core model on the infinite $Δ$-regular tree.

papers.title: Characterization of Integral Transforms for Hilbert Space-Valued Functions
papers.abstract: The aim of this paper is to characterize the Fourier transform of functions taking values in a separable Hilbert space $\Hi$ and defined on locally compact abelian groups. Inspired by Krukowskis characterization of integral transforms on locally compact abelian groups, we establish characterizations of the Fourier, Laplace, and cosine transforms for separable Hilbert space-valued functions on locally compact abelian groups. Furthermore, we obtain a characterization of the group Fourier transform on the Heisenberg group.

papers.title: Two-block paths in oriented graphs under the Ore-type condition
papers.abstract: Stein conjectured that for every positive integer $k$, every oriented graph with minimum semi-degree greater than $k/2$ contains every oriented path of length $k$ [Springer Optim.Appl. 165 (2020), 459--486]. For directed paths this is a classical result of Jackson (1981). The two-block case of the conjecture was established by Chen, Hou and Zhou (2025). In this paper we prove the two-block analogue of Jackson's theorem. For all positive integers $s$ and $r$, let $P(s,r)$ be the oriented path consisting of two directed paths of lengths $s$ and $r$ with a common terminal vertex, and let $Q(s,r)$ be its reverse. We show that for all $K\ge3$ and all $s,r\ge1$ with $s+r\le K$, every oriented graph $D$ with $δ(D)\ge K$ and $d_D^+(u)+d_D^-(v)\ge K-1$ for every ordered pair of distinct vertices $(u,v)\notin A(D)$ contains both $P(s,r)$ and $Q(s,r)$. Our result is the two-block analogue of Jackson's theorem, and it extends the two-block result of Chen, Hou and Zhou. The proof iterates a shift of the terminal vertex of a longest path.

papers.title: A Relative Telescope-Type Conjecture: Support and Generation in Half-Bounded Derived Categories
papers.abstract: Let $R$ be a commutative noetherian ring. We ask whether complexes with finitely generated cohomology and a fixed support can be generated by relatively compact objects, using coproducts which exist in the half-bounded derived category. We prove that $\mathbf D^+_{\mathrm{fg},W}(R)=\operatorname{Loc}_{\mathrm{ex}}(\mathbf D^b_{\mathrm{fg},W}(R))$ whenever $W\subseteq\operatorname{Spec} R$ is specialization closed and has finite dimension. The same equality holds for every specialization-closed subset of $\operatorname{Spec} B$ when $B$ is a finite-type algebra over a noetherian domain $A$ of finite character and either $A$ or $B$ is regular. These equalities classify the thick Hom-submodules closed under existing coproducts. We also prove the corresponding bounded-above statement from the support results of Matsui--Takahashi. For an arbitrary noetherian ring, the bounded-below generation conjecture reduces to torsion complexes over quotient domains, with their support unchanged. Finally, over a regular noetherian domain of infinite dimension, we give a bounded-below object which is generated by bounded objects with the same support but has no bounded-below representative by finitely generated modules. The comparison functor from the bounded-below derived category of finite modules is therefore neither full nor essentially surjective.

papers.title: Resolvent comparison for Hermitian block matrices and Kelmans transformations
papers.abstract: A Kelmans transformation increases or preserves the largest eigenvalue of a symmetric nonnegative matrix. We determine when this comparison holds for Hermitian block extensions with a fixed coupling and an arbitrary common complementary block. An orthogonal change of basis and Schur complementation give an exact formula for the compressed resolvent difference as a difference of two rank-one matrices. This formula characterizes admissible coupling subspaces by proportionality of projected resolvent vectors. Polynomial coefficient kernels describe all such subspaces, and cyclic subspaces give dimension bounds and a maximum-dimension result for a two-block family. We also prove a general block comparison theorem and give monotonicity and equality criteria for nonnegative rank-one couplings. Applications concern graph joins, complex attachments, and Hermitian adjacency matrices.

papers.title: Online packing of the three largest trees
papers.abstract: For every $n\ge4$, arbitrary trees of orders $n,n-1,n-2$ can be packed into $K_n$ online, in decreasing order of size: each tree must be embedded before the next is revealed, and earlier embeddings cannot be changed. This strengthens the classical three-tree packing theorem of Hobbs, Bourgeois and Kasiraj (1987). In particular, the second tree is embedded without knowing the third, and the resulting pair of copies can be extended to accommodate every possible third tree. Our strategy is to embed the first two trees so that their union is $2$-degenerate. We prove that the complement of every $2$-degenerate graph on $n$ vertices contains every tree of order $n-2$, which guarantees the final move. The main ingredient is an embedding lemma for spiders whose center must occupy a prescribed vertex having degree at most two in the forbidden graph. We then extend this lemma to arbitrary trees by induction.

papers.title: Uniform boundary observability for periodic wave equations with low frequency exponent $4/3$
papers.abstract: We study boundary observability for Dirichlet wave equations with symmetric, periodic coefficients in bounded $C^{2,1}$ domains of dimension $d\ge2$. We establish two-sided observability estimates, uniform in the oscillation scale $\varepsilon$, for initial data generated by eigenfunctions with eigenvalues at most $δ\varepsilon^{-4/3}$ with some small factor $δ$. The proof reduces wave observability to boundary gradient estimates for narrow spectral clusters. These estimates are obtained using a second-order expansion and a uniform commutator estimate for harmonic extension in boundary layers.

papers.title: Effective results in representation theory of reductive groups over local fields
papers.abstract: We prove effective versions of several classical results in representation theory of reductive groups over non-Archimedean local fields of arbitrary characteristic. More specifically, we deal with the support of matrix coefficients of cuspidal representations and the recursions satisfied by matrix coefficients of representations of finite length. We provide effective generation results for irreducible representations. Finally, we study the effective smoothness of characters on the set of regular semi-simple elements.

papers.title: Co-Decompositions and FO Model Checking
papers.abstract: Tree decompositions describe large graphs as gluings of smaller component parts. Here we study their categorical duals, tree co-decompositions, which construct large graphs via fibered products of small constituent parts. Co-decompositions are compressed representations of graphs or relational structures: the decomposed object can be exponentially larger than the space required to specify the co-decomposition. Our main contribution is an algorithmic meta-theorem for first order logic: given only a co-decomposition of a $σ$-structure $G$ with $b$ bags, each of size at most $w$ and an FO sentence $φ$, there is an algorithm which, without ever constructing or inspecting $G$, operates on the co-decomposition and determines whether $G \models φ$ in time $f_σ(w,|\varphi|)\cdot b$. We pair this algorithm with structural results on tree co-width, including its relationship to tree-width and a separation from twin-width. Furthermore, we characterize bounded path co-width using a graph grammar. In contrast to our logical meta-theorem, we prove that $(s,t)$-Path becomes NP-hard on co-decomposition inputs. These results demonstrate how categorical constructions can enable efficient computation on exponentially compressed structures.

papers.title: Breakdown of Linearized Dispersion in Waveguide QED
papers.abstract: Exploring interactions between quantum emitters and guided photons, waveguide quantum electrodynamics (wQED) offers a versatile platform for quantum simulation and quantum interconnect. To simplify the quantized light-matter interactions, a linearized dispersion approximation (LDA) was widely used in wQED under the conditions of weak coupling and narrow photonic bandwidth. However, a growing number of strong-coupling wQED experiments have called the validity of LDA into question. Here, by investigating giant atoms coupled to a semi-infinite waveguide, we propose a principle to judge the validity of LDA. We find that the decoherence of the atoms exhibits rich dynamical behaviors determined by different numbers of bound states in and out of the continuum (BICs and BOCs) formed in the energy spectrum of the total atom-photon system. Based on this, we show that despite the LDA can partially preserve some of BICs, it completely erases BOCs. This causes the dominant role of LDA in the atomic dynamics to break down. Providing a physical insight into the validity of LDA, our results lay a firm foundation for exploring fundamental physics and its application frontier in strong-coupling wQED platforms.

papers.title: Long-time behaviour and bifurcation analysis of a non-reciprocal two-species aggregation-diffusion system on the torus
papers.abstract: A two-species aggregation-diffusion system on the one-dimensional torus with antisymmetric cross-interactions modeling pursuit-evasion dynamics is studied. The self-interaction strength is used as a bifurcation parameter, and the linear stability of the homogeneous state is characterized by Fourier analysis. It is shown that non-reciprocal coupling enlarges the stability region. In a symmetric diffusion setting, exponential convergence to the homogeneous state is established for sufficiently weak self-interactions by means of an entropy argument, with a decay condition independent of the cross-interaction strength. Under suitable nondegeneracy and spectral assumptions, the first loss of stability is shown to occur through a Hopf bifurcation associated with a single spatial Fourier mode. A branch of time-periodic patterns is thereby obtained, along which the two species oscillate with a fixed phase difference. An explicit formula for the cubic Hopf coefficient is derived, and an essential dependence of the direction and stability of the bifurcating branch on the second spatial harmonic is identified. In the case of matching diffusion coefficients and interaction kernels, sufficiently strong non-reciprocity is shown to transform a subcritical stationary instability of the corresponding reciprocal system into a supercritical Hopf bifurcation with stable periodic solutions. An exchange-of-stability result is proved, and the theory is illustrated for Kuramoto, two-mode cosine, and top-hat interaction kernels.

papers.title: Local convexity obstructions for bounded realizations of Teichmüller space
papers.abstract: Let $D\subset\mathbb{C}^n$, $n\ge2$, be a bounded domain that is biholomorphic to a finite-dimensional Teichmüller space. We prove that $\partial D$ has no locally convex boundary patch containing a complex $(n-1)$-dimensional manifold through each of its points. Note that in complex dimension two this excludes every locally convex boundary point, without any boundary regularity assumption. In every dimension, we also exclude locally convex $C^2$ boundary patches.

papers.title: Every classifiable simple C*-algebra has a C*-diagonal
papers.abstract: We construct C*-diagonals in all UCT Kirchberg algebras. Together with known constructions of C*-diagonals in the stably finite setting by Xin Li, this shows that every classifiable C*-algebra (in the sense of the Elliott classification programme) has a C*-diagonal. In fact, we show that every UCT Kirchberg algebra admits an untwisted principal étale groupoid model with a finite-dimensional unit space.

papers.title: Additive energy, Freiman's lemma, and an edge-isoperimetric problem on the boolean cube
papers.abstract: Let $d \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ be a finite, non-empty set not contained in any translate of a hyperplane. We show that there exists a subset $S \subseteq A$ such that $d \ll |S| \ll d$ and \[E(A,S) := |\{(a_1,a_2,s_1,s_2)\in A\times A\times S\times S:a_1+s_1=a_2+s_2\}|\ll\lvert A\rvert\lvert S\rvert.\] This can be interpreted as a robust, analytic generalisation of the classical Freiman's lemma, and recovers Freiman's lemma up to a constant multiplicative factor. In the process of proving this result, we also show that for any integer $1 \leq m \leq d$ and any set $A \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ with $|A| \leq \binom{d}{m}$, one has \[ E(A, B) \leq 4(m + 1/m) |A||B|,\] where $B$ is the canonical basis of $\mathbb{Z}^d$. This gives new estimates for multiplicative energies between finite sets of primes and arbitrary subsets of positive integers, improving a previous result of Shkredov. Using related ideas, we also prove new bounds for an edge-isoperimetric problem for certain graphs on the boolean cube, improving an earlier result of Kirshner and Samorodnitsky. We give two different proofs of the first result described in this abstract and three different proofs of the second one.

papers.title: The Sharp Interface Limit of the Two-Dimensional Navier--Stokes/Allen--Cahn System as a Brakke Flow
papers.abstract: We study the sharp-interface limit of the two-dimensional incompressible Navier--Stokes/Allen--Cahn system with constant mobility and prove the existence of global integral varifold solutions to the coupled Navier--Stokes/mean curvature flow system. The limiting interface measure satisfies Brakke's inequality, and its normal velocity equals the sum of its mean curvature and the normal projection of the fluid velocity.

papers.title: Isolated symplectic singularities admitting symplectic resolutions

papers.title: Weighted orbits of hypercyclic vectors on F-spaces
papers.abstract: We study $\mathcal{F}$-hypercyclicity of weighted orbits $λ_nT^nx$ for continuous linear operators $T$ on complex F-spaces, where $\mathcal{F}$ is a Furstenberg family with the cut--shift--and--paste (CuSP) property. We characterize the scalar sequences for which weighted hypercyclicity always implies ordinary hypercyclicity: their nonzero values must be bounded and bounded away from zero. The same condition removes weights for every such family. For the converse inclusion, we prove that a bounded scalar sequence preserves all $\mathcal{F}$-hypercyclic vectors if its backward-shift $ω$-limit system is distal and does not contain the zero sequence. For chaotic operators, minimality of this system suffices. In particular, every complex nilsequence which is not identically zero preserves $\mathcal{F}$-hypercyclicity, and equality holds when its nonzero values are bounded away from zero. We also obtain simultaneous weighted return results and stability under unimodular weights with asymptotically trivial multiplicative differences.

papers.title: Cooperative Suppression of Two-Particle Excitation by Kerr Nonlinearity and Cavity Loss ion a Driven Holstein-Tavis-Cumming System
papers.abstract: We apply the numerically accurate multiple Davydov Ansatz (multi-$\rm D_2$) method to investigate the nonequilibrium dynamics of an open molecular cavity system using an extended driven-dissipative Holstein-Tavis-Cummings model incorporating Kerr nonlinearity. Our results reveal that the synergy between Kerr nonlinearity and exciton-phonon coupling induces an anharmonic level structure, imposing a stringent energy penalty that isolates the one-excitation manifold. This establishes a robust single-excitation-dominated regime that dynamically manifests photon blockade, characterized by suppression of the pure two-photon state and isolation of the one-excitation manifold. While strong coherent driving induces power broadening that overcomes the nonlinear barrier and opens multiphoton channels, cavity dissipation counteracts this process by acting as a highly selective manifold filter. By preferentially depleting fragile multi-photon states while sheltering single excitations within dissipation-free dark states, the cavity mode decay rate actively cooperates with Kerr nonlinearity to restore and reinforce the photon blockade effect. These findings elucidate the intricate interplay among nonlinearity, driving, and dissipation, offering a theoretical blueprint for engineering robust single-photon sources in open molecular cavity platforms.

papers.title: An Excursion into Grassmannian Spectra
papers.abstract: We revisit the classical spectral problem for the Laplace-Beltrami and Laplace-Bochner operators on complex Grassmannians. After reviewing the standard approach based on non-commutative harmonic analysis, we develop two complementary methods originating from the quantization of the corresponding one-dimensional sigma model, both with and without a magnetic monopole field. The first is based on $\mathbf{SU}(n)$-equivariant first-order GLSM formulation and gives explicit eigenfunctions in terms of projectors and Plücker coordinates. The second uses a spin-chain realization of free particles on manifolds and describes the space of square-integrable functions, or sections in the magnetic case, through limiting tensor products of long rectangular $\mathbf{SU}(n)$ representations. Together, these approaches provide a more explicit picture of the spectral geometry of Grassmannians and clarify the relation between harmonics, Young diagrams, magnetic bundles, and Laplacian spectra.

papers.title: Decentralized Sparse Quantile Regression
papers.abstract: Distributed statistical learning has recently attracted significant attention owing to its computational efficiency and scalability in large-scale systems. However, the non-smooth quantile loss poses substantial challenges to the development of efficient decentralized algorithms for quantile regression. Existing methods may either suffer from slow convergence or rely on smoothing-based approximations that require additional stringent assumptions, particularly in high-dimensional settings. To address these issues, we propose a decentralized framework that integrates gradient tracking with iterative hard thresholding for sparse quantile estimation. The proposed method avoids smoothing approximations and relaxes the initialization requirement. Theoretically, we show that the proposed algorithm achieves linear convergence under stated regularity conditions and that the resulting estimator attains the same order of statistical accuracy as its centralized counterpart. We further develop a decentralized information criterion for selecting the working sparsity level and establish support screening guarantees. Numerical experiments and a real-data study illustrate the finite-sample performance of the proposed method.

papers.title: K3 Categories and Mukai Homomorphisms for Debarre-Voisin Varieties
papers.abstract: Let $M=X_6^σ$ be a smooth Debarre-Voisin hyperkähler fourfold and $X=X_3^σ$ the associated smooth hyperplane section of $\operatorname{Gr}(3,10)$. Using the incidence correspondence between $X$ and $M$, we construct a family $\mathcal E$ of objects in the Kuznetsov component $\operatorname{Ku}(X)$. We write $v$ for the common Mukai vector of its fibers. We prove that the associated Mukai homomorphism \[ Θ_{\mathcal E}|_{v^\perp}\colon v^\perp\xrightarrow{\sim}H^2(M,\mathbb Z) \] is an integral Hodge isometry and explicitly determine the inverse image of the Plücker polarization. For a very general point of the trivector divisor corresponding to discriminant $24$, we also construct an integral Hodge isometry between the full Mukai lattices of $\operatorname{Ku}(X)$ and the associated twisted K3 surface.

papers.title: Discontinuous Galerkin Approximation to a Class of Strongly Damped Wave Equations with Uniform Exponential Decay
papers.abstract: This paper proposes and examines a completely discrete discontinuous Galerkin finite element scheme to approximate the solution of a class of strongly damped wave equations with uniform exponential decay property. In the first part, a semidiscrete discontinuous Galerkin approximation is employed in the spatial variable, while keeping time variable continuous and optimal error estimates are established while preserving the exponential decay property of the original system. Subsequently, a fully discrete scheme is developed and analyzed. Using suitable energy techniques, the consistency between the decay properties of the continuous and discrete systems is demonstrated. In particular, the constants appearing in various estimates remain uniformly bounded even as the damping parameters approach zero. Moreover, error estimates that preserve the uniform decay property are highlights of this paper. Further extension of our analysis includes a class of strongly damped fourth order evolution equations using SIPG as well as $C^0$-IP methods. Finally, several numerical experiments are performed to confirm the theoretical convergence results, verify the predicted decay behavior, and investigate the influence of model parameters on stability and computational accuracy.

papers.title: Kaplansky's conjectures fail for torsion-free hyperbolic groups in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: Do Kaplansky's group-ring conjectures hold for torsion-free word-hyperbolic groups? We show that all four fail in positive characteristic. For every prime $p$ there is a finitely presented, torsion-free, word-hyperbolic group $G$ with a finite two-dimensional classifying space and $a,b\in\mathbb{F}_p[G]$ with $ab=1\neq ba$. So, over every field of characteristic $p$, the group algebra of $G$ is not directly finite and has a non-trivial idempotent, zero divisor and unit, and $G$ is neither sofic nor surjunctive. For $p=2$, $G$, $a$ and $b$ come from OpenAI's random construction, and we add that $G$ is hyperbolic with probability $1-o(1)$, as are OpenAI's zero-divisor groups. For odd $p$ the groups are new: they adapt OpenAI's direct-finiteness construction with a signed cancellation, found first by S. V. Ivanov and independently by us, via an exact solution of a colour-balance problem and a Perron certificate. As far as we know, they are the first torsion-free counterexamples to direct finiteness and to the idempotent conjecture in odd characteristic. Hyperbolicity comes from one deterministic criterion: if a labelled graph is pattern-free, the group obtained by coning off its components is aspherical and has a linear isoperimetric inequality. We prove it by running OpenAI's exclusion of reduced spheres on van Kampen discs, an accounting OpenAI used for another complex. For every prime $p$, the existence of $G$, $a$ and $b$ and the failure of all four conjectures are formalized in Lean 4, including existence forms of the random-graph estimates used. In characteristic zero, where the idempotent and direct-finiteness conjectures hold for torsion-free hyperbolic groups, we show that no cancellation built into the vertex types survives the decay estimate that makes the groups torsion-free. OpenAI's characteristic-two counterexample with torsion is a CAT(0) group.

papers.title: Estimating "Realized" Skewness using Convolutional Neural Network
papers.abstract: We propose a new estimator of low-frequency skewness (monthly) that exploits high-frequency data (5 min) through a direct functional mapping consisting of layers of Convolutional Neural Networks followed by Multi Layer Perceptrons. Monte Carlo experiments involving stochastic volatility models, with and without jumps, show that the estimator reduces finite-sample bias relative to existing realized-skewness estimators and remains accurate under model misspecification. Empirically, our estimator exhibits temporal stability and delivers cross-sectional performance in actual skewness-sorted portfolios. We characterize the finite-sample bias of conventional plug-in skewness estimators and establish risk consistency properties of the proposed NN estimator under standard regularity conditions.

papers.title: Continuized Quasar-Convex Acceleration via an Unbiased Finite-Mixing Network Oracle
papers.abstract: We study decentralized minimization of a smooth network average that is globally quasar-convex with respect to a fixed minimizer; the node functions may be nonconvex and need not share a minimizer. A unit-rate Poisson clock drives an exactly simulable continuized process: between events the state follows a closed-form accelerated flow, and each event uses one oracle vector. One master theorem covers oracles with a predictable bias and a state-dependent variance and keeps the inverse-quadratic term $\mathcal{O}(LR_0^2/(γ^2T^2))$; one selected-row lemma supplies the oracle moments of three network implementations. CQA-Net keeps a common state, mixes local rows for finitely many rounds, and disseminates one uniformly selected row; its oracle is unbiased at every mixing depth, so incomplete averaging affects only the variance. A walking token removes dissemination, the shared clock, and the shared root, and an importance weight keeps it unbiased on fixed graphs. D-CQA keeps local states and mixes them; under bounded heterogeneity it needs $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\sqrtχ\sqrt{L}R_0/(γθ\sqrt{\varepsilon}))$ communication rounds and no dissemination. Changing graphs enter through certified operator norms. Experiments on a certified nonconvex regression on static and changing graphs compare the three implementations.

papers.title: On the IQC and SRG Frameworks: Equivalences and Converse Results
papers.abstract: Integral quadratic constraints (IQCs) and scaled relative graphs (SRGs) are two prominent frameworks for analyzing feedback systems. Although both frameworks are rooted in the same graph separation principle, a general characterization of their relationship has remained unavailable. This paper establishes conditions under which the IQC- and SRG frameworks are equivalent. To this end, we introduce two new classes of systems, termed disjunctive and conjunctive systems, which are respectively characterized by unions and intersections of quadratic input-output constraints. Under structural assumptions, we prove equivalence between the IQC and SRG frameworks for these system classes. By exploiting this equivalence, we develop novel IQC- and SRG-based converse stability results for linear and nonlinear systems. Our results accommodate multiple quadratic constraints, extending well-known converse results in robust control beyond the single-constraint setting.

papers.title: Adaptive Self-Optimization of Polarization Efficiency for Low-Power NV Center Thermometers Based on PAS-Q
papers.abstract: Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond have attracted considerable attention for micro- and nanoscale thermometry owing to their high precision and spatial resolution. However, achieving sufficient electron spin polarization and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) typically requires high-power or long-duration laser excitation, which introduces heating and degrades measurement accuracy and stability. To address this trade-off, a reinforcement learning (RL)-based approach is proposed to optimize spin polarization under low-heating constraints. First, a physical model integrating five-level optical pumping rates and NV spin polarization dynamics is established. A temperature-rise constraint model is then developed based on pulsed optically detected magnetic resonance (P-ODMR) measurements under varying laser powers and pulse widths in an external magnetic field. Subsequently, a Progressive Action-Space Q-learning (PAS-Q) algorithm is employed to explore the parameter space and identify optimal laser power and pulse-width combinations. The agent is trained through numerical simulations and the resulting strategy is implemented in a hardware system. Experimental results demonstrate a 44% reduction in laser-induced heating, a 33% increase in spin polarization rate based on T1 relaxation analysis, and a 71% reduction in optimization time compared with traditional methods. This approach enables efficient spin polarization with reduced laser heating and improved optimization efficiency, and may be extended to other heat-sensitive quantum spin sensors, including silicon-vacancy centers in diamond and divacancy defects in silicon carbide.

papers.title: Nonlinear Darcy Laws for Generalized Newtonian Fluids with Orlicz Growth and Oscillating Navier Slip in Periodic Porous Media
papers.abstract: We study the periodic homogenization of a stationary generalized Navier--Stokes system in a periodically perforated domain $Ω\subset\mathbb R^N$, $N\in\{2,3\}$, with a heterogeneous bulk stress of general Orlicz growth and an oscillating nonlinear Navier friction law on the pore walls, both at the Darcy scale. If the lower growth exponent at infinity satisfies $p^-_\infty>3N/(N+2)$ and the inertial exponent exceeds $κ_c:=1+N(2/p^-_\infty-1)_+$, inertia vanishes and, under strict monotonicity of the bulk stress, the whole family converges to the nonlinear Darcy law $U=\mathcal K(f-\nabla p_0)$, $\operatorname{div}U=0$, $U\cdotν=0$. The permeability map $\mathcal K$ is continuous, strictly monotone, obeys two-sided Orlicz bounds and incorporates the wall slip through a nonlinear cell problem, and the extended microscopic pressure converges strongly to $p_0$. The proof relies on a uniform Orlicz--Korn inequality, a Darcy-scaled two-scale trace theorem and a coupled bulk--surface Minty argument.

papers.title: Derivation of a bending model for rods from finite viscoelasticity
papers.abstract: Starting from a fully three dimensional model of finite viscoelasticity in the Kelvin-Voigt rheology, we derive a bending model for thin, viscoelastic rods. For this, we utilize a formulation of the model as a time-dependent metric gradient flow and pass to the limit by establishing convergence of curves of maximal slope using $Γ$-convergence. A posteriori, we relate the metric gradient flow limits to gradient flows in Hilbert spaces and discuss their properties. In contrast to previous results, where limit deformations are infinitesimal, in the bending regime, we deal with large rotations. This prevents us from using an additive ansatz for the construction of recovery sequences. Instead, we adapt from a previous result by the authors a multiplicative ansatz for elastoplastic Cosserat rods to the viscoelastic setting. For regularization purposes, we consider strain gradient terms in the three dimensional model that vanish in the limit.

papers.title: Finiteness properties of centralisers in $\mathrm{Out}(F_N)$ and automorphisms of free-by-cyclic groups
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a finitely generated free group. We prove that the centraliser of any element of $\mathrm{Out}(F)$ or $\mathrm{Aut}(F)$ is of type $\rm{VF}$. We also prove that the (outer) automorphism group of any free-by-cyclic group $M=F\rtimes_\varphi\mathbb{Z}$ is of type $\rm{VF}$, and so are the McCool subgroups of $\mathrm{Out}(M)$. This relies on the construction of a new $\mathrm{Out}(M)$-invariant splitting of $M$, that enables us to reduce the proof of the above statements to the case where the outer class of $\varphi$ has finite order.

papers.title: The Lovász Local Lemma Is Sharp for the Hat Guessing Number
papers.abstract: In the hat guessing game on a graph $G$, each vertex is occupied by a player wearing a hat whose color is chosen from a set of $q$ colors. Each player knows the graph and their position in it and sees only the hat colors of their neighbors. The players may agree on a strategy beforehand but must simultaneously try to guess their own hat colors without communicating. They win if at least one player guesses their own hat color correctly. The hat guessing number of $G$, denoted by $\textrm{HG}(G)$, is the largest integer $q$ for which the players have a strategy that guarantees a win for every assignment of hat colors. A direct application of the symmetric Lovász Local Lemma shows that $\textrm{HG}(G) < eΔ$ for every graph $G$ of maximum degree at most $Δ\ge 1$. We prove that this bound is asymptotically sharp: for every $\varepsilon > 0$ and every sufficiently large $Δ$, there exists a graph $G$ of maximum degree at most $Δ$ with $\textrm{HG}(G) \ge (e - \varepsilon)Δ$. This answers a question of Alon et al., disproves the conjecture $\textrm{HG}(G) \le 2Δ(G)$ of Bosek et al., and improves on the construction of Latyshev and Kokhas, which achieves $\textrm{HG}(G) = 4Δ(G)/3$. The hat guessing number thus provides a natural combinatorial problem in which the Lovász Local Lemma is asymptotically tight.

papers.title: Polynomial configurations and pointwise averages along Piatetski--Shapiro primes
papers.abstract: For every \(c>1\) sufficiently close to \(1\), we prove that there is \(κ>0\) such that every sufficiently large \(A\subset[N]\) of density at least \((\log N)^{-κ}\) contains \[ x,\ x+(p-1),\ x+(p-1)^2,\ldots,\ x+(p-1)^k, \qquad p=\lfloor n^c\rfloor\in\mathbb P. \] We also prove pointwise almost-everywhere convergence of the corresponding multiple ergodic averages.

papers.title: Spectral Quantum Memory for Implicit Neural Representations
papers.abstract: Implicit neural representations (INRs) model signals as continuous functions from coordinates to values, but their performance depends strongly on how spectral capacity is allocated. Yet most Quantum INR (QINR) architectures treat spectral components as independent outputs of separate quantum blocks. We introduce the Spectral Quantum Memory Model (SQMM), a memory coupled quantum INR in which sequential hybrid data reuploading layers (bands) communicate through a shared coherent quantum memory register. Each band reads the memory, computes on its own coordinate upload, and writes part of its state back, so later bands can build on the computation of earlier ones. When memory read and write layers are input independent, we prove that the memory state forms an operator valued Fourier series whose support is contained in the Minkowski sum of the initial memory spectrum and the local band spectra. Downstream bands then condition their Fourier coefficients on the spectral content stored by earlier bands, and the memory coupling creates no new primitive frequencies. This theory motivates a spectral memory alignment loss that encourages memory to encode the spectrum expressed by the deployed prefix of the model. Across audio and image reconstruction benchmarks, SQMM improves over compact QINR and INR baselines.

papers.title: On Random Purifications of Isometries and Channels
papers.abstract: Acorn tricks turn weak quantum resources into stronger "randomized" ones. A recent example is the random purification channel, which turns $t$ copies of a mixed state into $t$ copies of a random purification. We ask whether analogous techniques can turn queries to an isometry into queries to a random unitary completion, or queries to a quantum channel into queries to a random isometry dilation. For an isometry from dimension $N$ to dimension $M$, we give an efficient, stateful simulator for $T$ sequential, forward queries to a fixed Haar random unitary completion. It uses at most one forward isometry query per simulated call, with total trace-distance error $O(T\sqrt{N/(M-T)})$. This lifts isometry query lower bounds to arbitrary unitary completions, and copy complexity lower bounds to forward access to state preparation unitaries, with dimension-dependent loss that can be made arbitrarily small for most applications. Conversely, we construct two distributions on quantum channels distinguishable exactly with two queries to an arbitrary dilation, but requiring exponentially many channel queries for nonnegligible advantage. This rules out efficient simulation of random channel dilations. Our technique also shows that approximating the quantum switch to any constant error below $1/2$ requires exponentially many channel queries, even for identical channels, giving an exponential query advantage for indefinite causal order and improving on Bavaresco et al. (2025). Finally, we show how to "decontrol" controlled forward access to an isometry: any algorithm making controlled queries to $φV$ for a random phase $φ$ can be transformed into one using the same number of uncontrolled forward queries to $V$, generalizing the analogous result for unitaries.

papers.title: Fat base schemes and unexpected hypersurfaces of type $(d+k,d)$
papers.abstract: We study hypersurfaces of degree $d+k$ containing a prescribed zero-dimensional fat point scheme $Z\subset\mathbb{P}^n$ and having multiplicity at least $d$ along a general codimension-two linear subspace. We associate with this interpolation problem a vector bundle on $\mathbb{P}^1$ whose splitting type determines the dimensions of all linear systems of type $(d+k,d)$. For a fat point of multiplicity $m$, we determine the exact number of conditions detected by this bundle and introduce the corresponding effective length. This leads to an excess formula separating the contributions of the splitting type, the part of the fat structure invisible to degree-$k$ fibrewise sections, and the Hilbert-function defect of the fixed scheme. We also prove a truncation theorem showing that multiplicities larger than $k$ contribute only a uniform twist of the bundle and, geometrically, fixed hyperplane components. Finally, we exhibit explicit planar and three-dimensional examples showing that genuinely unexpected phenomena persist for nonreduced fixed base schemes, including geometrically irreducible unexpected hypersurfaces.

papers.title: Tensor preduals, positive homogeneity and harmonicity in two-Lipschitz spaces
papers.abstract: We study subspaces of two-Lipschitz mappings using group actions and tensor preduals. We first show that the ambient spaces contain large classical sequence spaces. We then use similarity actions to select smaller subspaces. Character-equivariant mappings form weak$^*$-closed fixed-point spaces and admit quotient tensor preduals. We give two applications. For mappings on Banach spaces, we describe positive homogeneity in each variable and construct bounded projections. For mappings on finitely generated groups, we characterize harmonicity in each variable. We show that the harmonic predual is the projective tensor product of the corresponding one-variable quotient preduals.

papers.title: Morse homology of nonsingular Morse-Smale foliations and its duality theorem
papers.abstract: We define a Morse homology of the foliation which is defined by a general nonsingular Morse-Smale flow, applying the framework of the Conley index theory. In fact, we define a chain and a boundary homomorphism, therefore, a cochain and a cohomology are obtained as well. Furthermore, we prove a duality theorem on the homology and the cohomology.

papers.title: Good slopes, congruence preservation, and gaps over residue rings
papers.abstract: For $n\ge2$, a good slope of a permutation $f$ of $\mathbb{Z}_n=\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ is an element $m\in\mathbb{Z}_n$ for which $x\mapsto f(x)+mx$ is a permutation. We call $f$ congruence-preserving if it preserves congruences modulo every divisor of $n$. For odd prime powers $n$, we classify all permutations with more than $n/2$ good slopes. Among permutations that are not congruence-preserving, we determine the maximum number of good slopes for $n=3^e$ with $e\ge2$, and for $n=25$, $125$ and $625$. Every permutation of $\mathbb{Z}_n$ has at most $\varphi(n)$ good slopes, where $\varphi$ is Euler's totient function. For several families of moduli with at least two distinct prime divisors, we prove a sharp upper bound for the number of good slopes of the permutations with fewer than $\varphi(n)$ good slopes. These families include $9q$ and $3q^e$ for every prime $q\ge5$ and every $e\ge1$. Together with a companion paper, this settles the bound for every odd composite modulus below $105$.

papers.title: Bilinear Korányi spherical maximal function on the Heisenberg group
papers.abstract: We introduce the bilinear Korányi spherical means on the Heisenberg group $\mathbb{H}^n,$ and derive $L^{p_1}(\mathbb{H}^n) \times L^{p_2}(\mathbb{H}^n) \to L^{p}(\mathbb{H}^n)$ estimates for the associated bilinear Korányi spherical maximal function on $\mathbb{H}^n.$ We also address multilinear extensions of our results.

papers.title: Exotic Dehn twists on sums of 4-manifolds, nuclei, and exotic structures
papers.abstract: For closed 4-manifolds $X_1, X_2$, we give a sufficient condition, in terms of the Seiberg-Witten invariants of $X_i$, for the Dehn twist on $X_1\#X_2$ along the neck to be smoothly nontrivial. This provides a broad generalization of the result of Kronheimer-Mrowka for $K3\#K3$. We also show that the boundary Dehn twists on the punctured connected sums of many pairs of elliptic surfaces are smoothly nontrivial. We also detect new examples of exotic Dehn twists along Seifert fibered 3-manifolds in elliptic surfaces. As a consequence, we exhibit a new phenomenon in which "exotic diffeomorphisms detect exotic smooth structures on 4-manifolds": the triviality of the boundary Dehn twist characterizes the standard nucleus $N(n)$ among the nuclei $N(n)_{p,q}$ homeomorphic to it, provided that $n\equiv0 \bmod 4$. These results are proved by computing the families Bauer-Furuta invariant for a new framing of the families Dirac index.

papers.title: A sharp Mittag-Leffler bound for series with separated exponents
papers.abstract: Let $η\geq 0$ and $δ>0$, and let $(r_j)_{j\geq 0}$ be a sequence of real numbers satisfying $η\leq r_0 < r_1 < r_2 < \cdots$ and $r_{j+1}-r_j \geq δ$ for every $j\geq 0$. We prove that, for $δ\leq 1$ and every $x>0$, \[ \sum_{j=0}^\infty \frac{x^{r_j}}{\G(1+r_j)} \leq \sum_{j=0}^\infty \frac{x^{η+jδ}}{\G(1+η+jδ)} = x^ηE_{δ,1+η}(x^δ), \] where $E_{δ,1+η}$ denotes the two-parameter Mittag-Leffler function. Moreover, equality holds for some $x>0$ if and only if $r_j = η+ jδ$ for every $j$. The proof combines a finite compression argument for unimodal functions with a shift inequality for the Mittag-Leffler function. The upper bound $δ\leq 1$ is sharp, since counterexamples exist for every $1 < δ< 2$.

papers.title: Decoy-state quantum key distribution with a leaky Mach-Zehnder receiver
papers.abstract: We prove the security of phase-encoded decoy-state BB84 quantum key distribution for a Mach-Zehnder receiver with imbalanced beam splitters and two threshold detectors that leak fine-grained information about the detection patterns. For this, we derive a lower bound on Bob's single-photon contributions and combine it with the decoy-state method and a recent phase-error framework for leaky receivers. The leakage-induced correction to the phase-error rate is independent of channel loss, providing a loss-tolerant treatment of receiver leakage even in the presence of beam-splitter imbalance. Our results provide a practical route toward loss-tolerant security proofs for imperfect QKD receivers in the presence of receiver leakage.

papers.title: Wavefront engineering with atomic Huygens' surfaces made simple
papers.abstract: Atomic arrays provide a cooperative platform for light-mediated interactions in nonlocal metasurfaces which can operate in the quantum regime without nanofabricated optical elements or intrinsic material absorption. We present a minimal atomic implementation to harness wavefront engineering and create a near-ideal intrinsic atomic Huygens' surface. A simple bilayer square lattice with a two-atom unit cell, not limited to small lattice spacings, provides near-unity reflectionless transmission and a full $2π$ phase control of transmitted light without the localized site-dependent level shifts of previous proposals. This simplification is achieved through nonlocal radiative excitations that provide the familiar electric-dipole response with even radiation parity as well as an odd-parity radiation channel whose leading multipolar interpretation combines magnetic-dipole and electric-quadrupole contributions in atoms exhibiting only electric dipole transitions. This eliminates the need to simultaneously excite pure electric-dipole and magnetic-dipole responses with exactly matched radiation. We derive a two-mode model for this response and show that it accurately captures full coupled-dipole simulations near the optimal lattice spacings. Because of the wide applicability of coupled-dipole models, the relevance of our microscopic analysis extends beyond atomic physics to nanostructured metasurfaces. Moreover, the same platform also connects directly to established subradiance-protected single-photon storage protocols, suggesting a route toward combining wavefront engineering, storage, and retrieval in a simple atomic bilayer.

papers.title: The Extension groups of one $\rm K$-type representations of graded Hecke algebra
papers.abstract: We study the extension groups between one $\rm K$-type representations of the graded Hecke algebra $\mathbb H$. A one $\rm K$-type representation is a Hermitian representation of $\mbb H$ whose restriction to the Weyl group is irreducible. Using a Koszul-type resolution of $\mathbb H$-modules, we reduce the computation of $\operatorname{Ext}_{\mathbb H}^j(X,Y)$ to a combinatorial count, yielding explicit formulas for the classical types and a computer computation for the exceptional types.

papers.title: Extremal even-cycle-free subgraphs of the $k$-ary $n$-cube
papers.abstract: A graph is said to be $H$-free if it contains no subgraph isomorphic to $H$. The generalized Turán number $\mathrm{ex}(G, H)$, a natural extension of the classical Turán number, is defined as the maximum number of edges in an $H$-free spanning subgraph of $G$. For any integer $\ell\geq 2$, let $C_{2\ell}$ denote the even cycle of length $2\ell$. So far, extensive studies of the generalized Turán number for the hypercube $Q_{n}$ have been conducted. The $k$-ary $n$-cube is an important family of graphs with many favorable properties, such as regularity and vertex-transitivity. It generalizes the hypercube and reduces to the hypercube when $k=2$. In this paper, we investigate the generalized Turán number $\mathrm{ex}(Q^{k}_{n}, C_{2\ell})$ of $Q^{k}_{n}$ for all even integers $k\geq 4$ and integers $\ell\geq 2$, generalizing the result for $Q_{n}$ [J. Graph Theory 16 (1992) 273-286] from $k=2$ to $k\geq 4$.

papers.title: Star-shaped periodic solutions of a system of delay differential equations: A computer-assisted proof
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider a planar system of nonlinear delay differential equations and prove the existence of the star-shaped periodic solutions conjectured by Hara (Nonlinear Analysis: Theory, Methods \& Applications, 30:4555--4563 (1997)) for seven parameter values. These solutions cannot be obtained by a direct application of the standard Fourier spectral method, since the corresponding linearized operator is degenerate. From numerical observations of the Fourier coefficients, we derive an ansatz that writes a star-shaped periodic solution as a periodic profile in a rotating frame. Restricting the profile to real Fourier coefficients, we show that the resonance between the delay and the period of the profile fixes the rotation frequency exactly. We then validate a zero of the resulting real system with the radii polynomial approach and interval arithmetic, with bounds that cover all Fourier modes. For each parameter value, we also determine the fundamental period and the winding number of the solution.

papers.title: Unstable Stokes waves in constant vorticity flows of infinite depth
papers.abstract: We study the spectral stability of small-amplitude Stokes waves with constant vorticity in infinite depth. We describe the spectrum near the origin and near the first nonzero double eigenvalue. For nonzero vorticity $ω<2\sqrt{g/3}$, where $g$ is the gravitational constant, the eigenvalues near the origin form a figure eight, whereas for $ω>2\sqrt{g/3}$ the local spectrum remains purely imaginary. Away from the origin, the interaction of two Fourier modes whose indices differ by two produces an unstable isola when $ω>-\sqrt{g/6}$, $ω\ne0$, and the resonant wave numbers are noninteger. This curve is a real analytic oval with an explicit leading ellipse and maximal growth of quadratic order in the amplitude. We also prove instability at the integer resonances needed to cover the remaining vorticities. Together with the classical irrotational result, these two mechanisms show that sufficiently small nonzero Stokes waves are spectrally unstable for every fixed constant vorticity. The proof uses finite-dimensional spectral reductions of the full Euler linearization. Near the origin, the finite-dimensional linearized operator has a one-sided limit as the Floquet exponent vanishes, which differs from the periodic linearization. We use the Kato transformation to construct a three-dimensional reduction with biorthogonal bases and use all three eigenvectors of the reference operator to calculate the Benjamin--Feir coefficient. At the nonzero collision, a real two-dimensional reduction and an explicit second-order calculation determine the unstable curve.

papers.title: Long-lived quantum memories with rare-earth ions doped in crystals
papers.abstract: Quantum memory is a core enabling device for large-scale quantum networks, serving as the fundamental building block for quantum repeaters and transportable quantum memories. Among various physical platforms, rare-earth-ion-doped crystals stand out as one of the most promising solid-state candidates for long-lived photonic quantum memories, owing to their exceptionally long spin coherence time and their compatibility with integration. In this review, we first introduce the physical mechanisms underlying long-lived spin coherence in rare-earth systems, with particular emphasis on the zero-first-order-Zeeman transition and dynamical decoupling techniques. We then review the experimental progress in this field, highlighting three distinct lifetimes--the spin coherence time, the light storage time, and the quantum storage time--and covering experiments that have achieved hour-scale spin coherence, minute- to hour-scale light storage, and minute-scale single-photon-level quantum storage. Finally, we discuss the remaining challenges that hinder the realization of practical long-lived quantum memories, explore potential strategies to overcome these obstacles, and outline the prospects for their future applications in quantum networks.

papers.title: Binary Codes with a Forbidden Distance
papers.abstract: The maximum size of a t-intersecting code in the set of words of length n over an alphabet of size m, a problem posed by Frankl and Füredi, was determined independently by Ahlswede and Khachatrian and by Frankl and Tokushige. Extending this result to the forbidden-intersection setting, Keevash, Lifshitz, Long and Minzer proved that, for m greater than two and n sufficiently large in terms of t, (t minus one)-avoiding codes have the same maximum size and the same extremal ball constructions as t-intersecting codes. They also raised the binary case. Here, t-intersecting requires every two distinct words to agree in at least t coordinates, while (t minus one)-avoiding forbids agreement in exactly t minus one coordinates. We solve the binary case for all t at least three and n at least the square of the sum of t and one. If the forbidden Hamming distance n minus t plus one is odd, the maximum size of a (t minus one)-avoiding code strictly exceeds the maximum t-intersecting size. If it is even, the two maxima coincide, but their extremal families differ: some maximum (t minus one)-avoiding codes are not t-intersecting.
