The conservative response, which vanishes analytically, is constrained by the numerical error floor. These results demonstrate that PINNs can accurately compute black-hole tidal response and establish a validated framework for future extensions to frequency-dependent and non-separable perturbation problems.

papers.title: Koszul duality for boundary categories
papers.abstract: We study how Koszul duality relates two kinds of boundary constructions associated with a smooth category and a proper category. For a smooth category with a proper Koszul-dualizing subcategory, we construct a fully faithful functor from its categorical neighborhood of infinity to the singularity category associated to the proper category. We prove that this functor is an equivalence precisely when the smooth category is reflexive, meaning that it can be reconstructed from its finite-dimensional module theory. Under a Gorenstein condition, satisfied in the Calabi--Yau setting, the functor is induced by restriction of modules. We give algebraic criteria that ensure equivalence and obtain an identification of Hochschild cohomology.

papers.title: $M$-subgroups and normal-subgroup lattices of finite groups
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a group. A normal subgroup $E$ is an $M$-subgroup if $E\cap N_1\cap N_2\neq1$ whenever $N_1\cap N_2$, $E\cap N_1$, and $E\cap N_2$ are non-trivial for normal subgroups $N_1,N_2$. We characterise these subgroups as the essential or relatively uniform normal subgroups. For finite $G$, an $M$-subgroup is either trivial, contains exactly one minimal normal subgroup, or contains the socle. Consequently, every normal subgroup is an $M$-subgroup precisely when the socle has $G$-chief length at most two. We obtain an explicit $M$-closure operation and describe the minimal normal subgroups of finite direct products. For crown-based powers, we use the known comparability of normal subgroups with the socle to describe the normal lattice in terms of Boolean or subspace lattices and the quotient above the socle. We then determine when the $M$-lattice retains the normal lattice, classify normal quotients and their automorphism orbits, and characterise quotient maps compatible with $M$-closure. Finally, we compute the maximal length of chains of $M$-subgroups in terms of the chief length and socle length of $G$.

papers.title: Enumeration of $k$-convex polyominoes by semi-perimeter
papers.abstract: We prove the Conway--Guttmann formula for the generating function of $k$-convex polyominoes by semi-perimeter, for every $k\ge2$. A decomposition according to the two diagonal directions reduces the enumeration to convex polyominoes satisfying a one-bend condition in one diagonal direction. Splitting these polyominoes at the right endpoint of the top row leaves an initial part followed by columns whose vertical intervals decrease by inclusion. Ordered forests describe the initial part and retain the row information needed to determine when column extensions first exceed the prescribed bound. A first-passage calculation, together with a sum over initial parts already above the bound, gives the required generating function. The argument includes the case $k=2$.

papers.title: Functoriality probes over number fields by mixed zero correlations
papers.abstract: We use an automorphic L-function over one number field as a probe for the functorial structure of another automorphic L-function over a possibly different field. No automorphic induction is assumed. We first determine the mixed Euler factors arising from the explicit formula, including the residue-degree multiplicities that occur when local traces are grouped by absolute norm. This local analysis gives four probe constructions. Rational-field probes with known base change detect constituent multiplicities and, in equal rank, exact Satake equalities. Probes over a common Galois field detect conjugacy and stabilizers. Dirichlet-character probes give congruence-weighted combinations of Satake traces even when the leading overlap vanishes. A tensor-product construction realizes general different-field probes whenever the required base changes exist. We then separate the pair calculation from the higher connected calculations and work out the cubic and quartic arithmetic explicitly. In an explicit small Fourier box these expressions yield all finite secondary orders of the centered statistics; the required pair prime number theorems also give raw and distinct-index correlations. The main analytic tools are an independent fixed-data proof of Hypothesis H over number fields, a positive-margin estimate for rationally grouped coefficients, and the theorem of Harcos-Thorner for the realized Rankin-Selberg factors. This expanded version includes the full computations, local examples, and an appendix explaining the character-extension issue avoided by the proof of Hypothesis H. The resulting probes give concrete tests of functorial relationships, while recovery of automorphic induction remains a longer-term goal.

papers.title: Classical and Quantum Logics with Multiple Non-Equivalent and Non-Isomorphic Models
papers.abstract: Both quantum and classical logics have several mutually non-equivalent and non-isomorphic models as has repeatedly been proved in the literature. Yet, several authors have recently come with criticisms of this result. In this paper, we show that the criticisms are either unfounded or wrong.

papers.title: Asymptotic behavior of some strongly critical decomposable multi-type Galton-Watson processes with immigration
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotic behavior of a critical decomposable multi-type Galton-Watson process with immigration whose offspring mean matrix is triangular with diagonal entries 1. Under second-order moment conditions on the offspring and immigration distributions, we establish a functional limit theorem for the sequence of appropriately scaled processes, and describe the limit process as independent squared Bessel processes and some linear combinations of their iterated integral processes. Our work completes and extends some results of Foster and Ney (1978) for some strongly critical decomposable multi-type Galton-Watson processes with immigration.

papers.title: The local-to-global minimum problem of Calvert and Vamanamurthy: a quartic counterexample in three variables and the cubic case in all dimensions
papers.abstract: In 1980 Calvert and Vamanamurthy asked whether a polynomial whose only critical point is a local minimum must attain its global minimum there. They gave counterexamples of every degree at least five in two or more variables and settled cubics in two and three variables and quartics in two variables, leaving open quartics in three or more variables and cubics in four or more variables. We resolve both remaining cases. First, we give an explicit quartic in three variables whose unique critical point is a nondegenerate strict local minimum, although the polynomial is unbounded below; the example extends to every dimension at least three, and its critical locus is a single point even over the complex numbers. Second, we prove that in every dimension a polynomial of exact degree three with a local minimum has another critical point, so that the cubic case holds vacuously; the proof is elementary and avoids the topological degree arguments used previously in two and three variables. Together with the results of Calvert and Vamanamurthy, this gives the complete classification of the local-to-global property by degree and dimension.

papers.title: Uniqueness of scalar-flat ALE Kähler metrics
papers.abstract: We study uniqueness of scalar-flat Kähler metrics in a fixed Kähler class on an asymptotically locally Euclidean (ALE) Kähler manifold, assuming only differentiated $o(1)$ decay to a fixed Euclidean metric on the end. In complex dimension $n\geq2$, under suitable polynomial decay of the reference metric, we prove that the relative Mabuchi functional is finite, continuous, and convex along weak geodesics whose endpoint potentials satisfy $u=O(r^{-γ})$, $γ>2n-4$, together with the corresponding derivative estimates. Combining this convexity with the analysis of the Lichnerowicz operator in weighted spaces, we obtain uniqueness by a perturbation argument. Decay improvement and comparison of the asymptotic charts produce a global potential with the required decay for the difference of the two cohomologous scalar-flat Kähler forms. The argument also extends to asymptotically conical Kähler metrics approaching a fixed Ricci-flat Kähler cone under prescribed decay assumptions.

papers.title: Extremal zero-sum sequences without elements of maximal order
papers.abstract: Let $\mathsf D(G)$ denote the Davenport constant of a finite abelian group $G$, the maximal length of a minimal zero-sum sequence over $G$. Gao and Geroldinger conjectured that every minimal zero-sum sequence of length $\mathsf D(G)$~\cite[Conjecture~6.1]{GG99} and every zero-sumfree sequence of length $\mathsf D(G)-1$~\cite[Conjecture~4.1]{GG06} contains an element of order $\exp(G)$. We disprove both conjectures by proving a density-one theorem: for every fixed finite abelian group $H$ of exponent $M=2^ap^b$, where $a\ge2$, $b\ge1$, and $p$ is an odd prime, the set of integers $r\ge0$ for which $G_r=C_2^r\oplus H$ admits a minimal zero-sum sequence of length $\mathsf D(G_r)$ with no term of order $M$ has natural density one.

papers.title: Generalized Ricci Solitons on Heisenberg and Oscillator Algebras
papers.abstract: We prove that on a connected, simply-connected nilpotent Lie group, the notions of left-invariant generalized Ricci soliton, semi-algebraic and algebraic generalized Ricci soliton coincide. Moreover, every such soliton has harmonic torsion. We classify all algebraic solitons with positive definite metric on the five-dimensional Heisenberg algebra, the four-dimensional oscillator algebra and the four-dimensional split-oscillator algebra up to automorphisms and rescalings. We find that there is only a finite number of algebraic solitons, all of which have harmonic torsion.

papers.title: Tensor Products and the Isomorphic Theory of Daugavet Spaces
papers.abstract: We construct two separable Banach spaces with the Daugavet property whose injective and projective tensor squares, respectively, fail the Daugavet property. Both examples arise from one sequence of finite-dimensional extensions. The first space is the completion of the increasing union of the extensions, whereas the second is the closed span of their coordinate functionals. We will also investigate the operator Daugavet properties of these spaces later in the paper, also highlighting natural examples of metric spaces \(M\) for which \(\operatorname{Lip}_0(M)\) has the Daugavet property but fails to have the weak operator Daugavet property. Independently of this, we will also prove that every Banach space admits a linear isometric embedding into a Banach space which is not isomorphic to any Banach space with the Daugavet property.

papers.title: Adaptive Preference Elicitation in Preference Robust CPT-Based Shortfall
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the cumulative prospect theory (CPT)-based shortfall risk measure where the value (utility) function and the distortion (probability weighting) functions are ambiguous. We propose a worst-case CPT-based shortfall risk measure where the capital requirement is based on the worst-case value function and distortion functions from an ambiguity set constructed with user-specific information (e.g., preference between risky and certain lotteries) and well-known general information such as the S-shape of the value functions. When the underlying random loss is discretely distributed and parameters in pairs of lotteries remain undetermined, we demonstrate that the worst-case value function and the distortion functions have a piecewise linear structure. Based on this observation, we develop an adaptive preference elicitation approach extended from the well-known polyhedral method to simultaneously elicit the distortion functions and the positive and negative parts of the value function by solving a sequence of mixed-integer linear programs. Based on the elicited distortions, we design new queries to construct a feasible set of the holistic value functions. The proposed framework iteratively shrinks the ambiguity set through designed queries, yielding a computationally implementable robust CPT-based shortfall risk measure. To examine the in-sample and out-of-sample performance of the elicited CPT-based preference functions and the resulting preference robust shortfall risk measure, we conduct numerical experiments under an S-shaped value function and inverse S-shaped distortion functions and report the corresponding results.

papers.title: Probing automorphic induction through zero correlations and secondary arithmetic terms
papers.abstract: Zero correlations offer a way to test the cuspidal structure of an automorphic L-function, but their leading self statistics retain only coarse degree and multiplicity data. We therefore adjoin a specified cuspidal L-function as a probe and study the resulting raw mixed correlations. Assuming a factorization into cuspidal L-functions over Q, we show that a mixed pair statistic detects the probe's occurrence and recovers its multiplicity. A suitable Gevrey-order-two test eliminates the smooth-density terms and gives a subexponential error. For arbitrary smooth plateau tests, the prime number theorem of Harcos and Thorner gives an error smaller than every fixed inverse power of log T, without a self-contragredience assumption. The stronger prime number theorem of Liu and Ye gives a subexponential remainder under its stated structural assumptions, with the possible norm-twist terms made explicit. To obtain arithmetic information beyond this overlap, we compute the correlation expansion at every fixed level and inverse-logarithmic order within the original strict small-support range. We treat the pair and higher correlations separately, using Jiang's rational-field fixed-data estimates to justify the required prime-power convergence. The pair calculation identifies the mixed arithmetic finite parts and gives detailed error estimates, including the contribution of norm twists. The higher-level calculation retains connected prime-power invariants, whose first cubic contribution appears at order (log T)^{-3}. Explicit third- and fourth-level formulas and examples explain the arithmetic content of these coefficients and the limitations of self-correlations. Varying powers of the probe separates their mixed components. These formulas, together with the distinct-index sieve, provide a collection of arithmetic probe responses toward the further problem of recovering automorphic induction structure.

papers.title: Rare Event Constrained Reinforcement Learning with Large Deviations
papers.abstract: We study finite-horizon reinforcement learning with a safety constraint on the probability of reaching a failure set. In contrast to the well-studied safe reinforcement learning literature, we consider problems where the probability of reaching the failure set is vanishingly small, but the consequences of reaching the failure set are catastrophic. Direct simulation and estimation of the optimal policy is naturally ineffective when the failure probability is extremely small. Moreover, on a real system the controller can only choose actions, and this is not enough to make failures frequent. In contrast to the rare event simulation literature, our goal is not to estimate the probability of the rare event occurrence, but to upper bound it such that the failure constraint is satisfied. Thus, instead of sampling failures, we use the large deviations principle. We define a damage variable that on exceeding a certain threshold indicates failure. We study the cumulant generating function (CGF) as its positive root provides an upper bound on the failure probability via Cramer's theorem. We extend this approach to Markov decision processes with hitting times through state-action CGFs, and give finite-horizon and state-dependent versions of the bound. The state-action CGFs do not depend on the policy and can be estimated from regular transitions, so the bound can be checked for any policy a priori. This gives a policy improvement algorithm in which every policy satisfies the failure constraint with high probability.

papers.title: A Korselt Characterization of Carmichael Numbers of the Form $(aC_n+1)(aC_{n+1}+1)(aC_{n+2}+1)$
papers.abstract: We study products \[ N=(aC_n+1)(aC_{n+1}+1)(aC_{n+2}+1), \] where $(C_n)$ is the Lucas--balancing sequence. Under the assumption that all three factors are prime, we give a necessary and sufficient condition for $N$ to be a Carmichael number: this happens precisely when $n$ is even and $a=kC_{n+1}$ for a positive integer $k$ satisfying \[ 48k\equiv 7\pmod{C_nC_{n+2}}. \] We derive further congruence restrictions, an explicit parametrization of the integer solutions of the resulting congruence, a lower bound for $k$, and a divisibility relation involving the middle prime factor. The characterization is conditional on the primality of the three factors and does not assert that such prime triples exist for infinitely many parameters.

papers.title: Minimax-Optimal Static Estimators Under Interference
papers.abstract: We study the problem of estimating the global treatment effect in randomized experiments under interference, where a unit's outcome may depend on the treatment assignments of other units. We adopt a minimax framework, allowing an adversary to select an outcome function from a class of functions that satisfy bounded outcomes and bounded interference. We derive minimax-optimal static estimators that are robust to a wide range of interference structures, parameterized by a scalar $δ$ controlling the maximum influence of one unit's treatment on another's outcome. Under large interference, we observe two regimes. When the treatment and control groups are equally sized, the minimax-optimal static estimator is the zero estimator. When one of the two groups is larger, the minimax-optimal static estimator is a "half-zero" estimator, in which the outcomes of the smaller group are ignored, and the estimator only considers the outcomes of the larger group.

papers.title: On Guarding Line Arrangements
papers.abstract: We study the problem of guarding a set of straight lines in the plane by selecting a minimum-cardinality set of points such that every line contains at least one selected point. This problem is known to be strongly NP-hard \cite{megiddo}. We investigate approximation algorithms for the problem and analyze their performance guarantees under various structural assumptions on the underlying line arrangement. In particular, we present approximation schemes based on set-cover techniques, relaxation methods, and properties of maximal lines. We establish constant-factor bounds on the approximation ratio for several classes of arrangements and derive relationships between the guarding number and the incidence parameters of the arrangement. Connections with Dirac-type incidence results are also explored.

papers.title: A proof of the sharpness conjectures for all saturated fusion systems
papers.abstract: We prove the Díaz$\unicode[Arial]{x2013}$Park conjecture for sharpness of saturated fusion systems. More generally, for every saturated fusion system $\mathcal F$ over a finite $p$-group and every Mackey functor for $\mathcal F$ over the localisation $\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$ of the integers at $p$, the higher limits of its contravariant part over the centric orbit category vanish in all positive degrees. In particular, the subgroup and normaliser decompositions of every $p$-local finite group $(S,\mathcal F,\mathcal L)$ over the $\mathcal F$-centric subgroups are sharp. This answers in the affirmative a question in the list of important open problems in [M. Aschbacher, R. Kessar and B. Oliver, Fusion Systems in Algebra and Topology, Cambridge Univ. Press (2011)], and proves the sharpness conjecture stated in [M. Aschbacher and B. Oliver, Fusion systems, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. (2016)] and Conjecture 1.2 of [E. Yalç$\unicode[Arial]{x131}$n, Higher limits over the fusion orbit category, Adv. Math. (2022)]. The proof is algebraic and does not rely on the classification of finite simple groups.

papers.title: An entropic barrier to equilibration in the discrete nonlinear Schrödinger equation: Rigorous bounds for the microcanonical Brownian motion
papers.abstract: The relaxation of the discrete nonlinear Schrödinger equation is known to slow down dramatically when the energy density $\varepsilon$ exceeds a critical value $\varepsilon_c$, where the system enters a condensed phase. Replacing the Hamiltonian dynamics by Brownian motion on the microcanonical surface of $N$ sites at fixed mass and energy, we prove rigorous upper and lower bounds on the equilibration time $τ_{\mathrm{eq}}$, which is governed by the first non-zero eigenvalue $λ_1$ of the Laplacian on this surface. In the condensed phase the equilibration time is stretched exponential, not exponential, in the system size. The upper bounds on $λ_1$ come from trial functions: of one occupation for $\varepsilon<\varepsilon_c$, where the problem reduces to a Sturm-Liouville equation, and of two occupations for $\varepsilon>\varepsilon_c$, where they cross the bottleneck through which the condensate moves between sites. The lower bounds on $λ_1$ come from a Bochner-Reilly argument, with a vector field that compensates the concavity of the boundary. As a result, $τ_{\mathrm{eq}}=O(1)$ for $\varepsilon<\varepsilon_c$, while for $\varepsilon>\varepsilon_c$, asymptotically in $N$, $(\sqrt{2}-1)\sqrt{\varepsilon-\varepsilon_c}\leq\lnτ_{\mathrm{eq}}/\sqrt{N}\leq\sqrt{\varepsilon-\varepsilon_c}$. We conjecture that the left-hand bound is sharp and the right-hand one is not.

papers.title: Reverse Transportation and Harnack Inequalities for Underdamped Langevin in the Non-convex Setting
papers.abstract: We establish a dimension-free long-time reverse transportation, respectively Harnack inequality for the underdamped Langevin dynamics with non-convex potential. Specifically, we prove that for any two initial points $z,z'$ and $P_t$ the underdamped Langevin semigroup, it holds \begin{equation} \mathrm{KL}(δ_z P_t|δ_{z'}P_t) \leq C\mathrm{e}^{-χt}|z-z'|(\mathcal{R}\vee|z-z'|) \end{equation} for all $t>δ$ where $δ>0$ is arbitrarily small and $C=C(δ),\mathcal{R},χ>0$ are dimension free constants. In particular, our proof extends recent results which are restricted to either the convex underdamped or the non-convex but overdamped setting.

papers.title: The Coxeter-Todd abelian sixfold, Gamma00, and big Schottky
papers.abstract: We recall the construction of the Coxeter-Todd principally polarized abelian sixfold, and study its special properties. We show that the base locus of the Gamma00 linear system on the Coxeter-Todd sixfold consists of 253 points, disproving the stronger version by Donagi and Beauville--Debarre of the Gamma00 conjecture of van Geemen and van der Geer. This also leads us to construct explicit indecomposable 7-dimensional principally polarized abelian varieties that are not Jacobians, but lie in the so-called Big Schottky locus, thus disproving the corresponding conjecture from the Schottky-Jung approach to the Schottky problem. We furthermore show that while no even theta constant vanishes for the Coxeter-Todd sixfold, its associated Scorza quartic is identically zero. Finally, we show that there exist two different theta level (2,4) structures on the Coxeter-Todd sixfold, for which the sets of second order theta constants are projectively equal. This disproves the expected injectivity of the second order theta constant map for all genera starting with 6.

papers.title: Randomized Adaptive Sequential Allocation and the Limits of Bounded Exposure to Inferior Treatments
papers.abstract: A clinical trial must learn which treatment is superior while sparing its participants from the inferior one. Kundu et al. 2025 recently showed that a purely deterministic rule, which always assigns the treatment with the larger current sample mean, achieves a strong form of this ethical goal. The smaller allocation count stays almost surely finite and has all moments bounded uniformly in the sample size. Deterministic allocation is, however, predictable, and predictability invites selection bias. We ask whether this bounded-exposure phenomenon survives once the deterministic rule is replaced by a smooth randomized one. We show that it does not. Under any fixed non-degenerate symmetric randomization, both treatments are sampled infinitely often, the adaptive sample means are strongly consistent, and the inferior treatment draws a strictly positive limiting allocation proportion. Consequently, the inferior allocation count grows linearly and its moments are unbounded. We then study annealed randomization, in which the randomization scale cools with the accumulated information, and obtain summability and divergence criteria that separate finite, sublinear, and linear exposure. A forced-exploration variant identifies the superior treatment with probability one while keeping the inferior exposure sublinear, and thereby frees the annealed guarantees from any correct-stabilization event. We also treat normalized multi-treatment rules, ties, indifference zones, unequal variances, general response distributions, and local alternatives. Finally, we develop the post-trial asymptotic inference that each exposure regime permits. The results delineate the trade-off between allocation concealment, persistent exploration, and ethical concentration on the superior treatment.

papers.title: Volume Doubling and Geometric Inequalities on Graphs with Bakry-Émery Curvature
papers.abstract: We consider irreducible reversible Markov chains whose nonzero off-diagonal transition probabilities are bounded below by $ε>0$ and whose reversible measure satisfies $m_-\le m(x)\leκm_-$. Under the Bakry--Émery curvature condition $\mathrm{CD}(K,\infty)$, with $K\in\mathbb{R}$, we establish Wang's log-Harnack inequality $$ P_t(\log f)(x)\le\log P_tf(y) +\frac{C\mathrm{dist}(x,y)^2}{\int_0^t e^{2Ks}\mathrm{d} s}, $$ for bounded positive $f$ bounded away from zero and all $x,y\in V$, where $C$ is a constant dependent only on $\varepsilon$. Building upon this inequality, we further prove volume doubling property: let $K_-:=\max\{-K,0\}$ $$ \mathrm{Vol}(B(o,2R))\le C_0\exp\!\bigl(C_1\sqrt{K_-}\,R\bigr) \mathrm{Vol}(B(o,R)),\qquad R>0, $$ where $C_0,C_1$ depend only on $ε,κ$. If $d$ is the maximum combinatorial degree of the support graph, we further prove under $\mathrm{CD}(0,\infty)$ the sharp volume growth bound $\mathrm{Vol}(B(o,R))\le m_-CR^{\lfloor d/2\rfloor}$ for all $o$ and $R\geq 1$.

papers.title: The Carpenter property for subfactors of uniform infinite index
papers.abstract: We show that if $N\subset M$ is an inclusion of $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors of uniform infinite index, for instance an irreducible inclusion of infinite index, then every positive contraction $b\in N$ is of the form $E_N(p)$ for a projection $p\in M$. This gives the exact version of Popa's asymptotic result in the ultrapower, and it is a subfactor analogue of the Carpenter problem for masas. In particular, Popa's relative dimension set of such an inclusion is $[0,1]$, so the set of expectations of projections does not distinguish inclusions without corners of finite index. As applications, the Carpenter property holds for $N\subset N\rtimes G$ whenever an infinite group $G$ acts outerly on a $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor $N$, and for ICC groups $H\le G$ the inclusion $L(H)\subset L(G)$ has it exactly when $[G:H]=\infty$, confirming a recent conjecture. We also give examples showing that the Carpenter property does not imply uniform infinite index, and that infinite index does not imply the Carpenter property.

papers.title: A complete characterization of graphs with second largest eigenvalue at most $(\sqrt5-1)/2$
papers.abstract: In 1993, Cao and Hong posed the problem of characterizing graphs whose second largest adjacency eigenvalue is greater than $1/3$ and less than $(\sqrt5-1)/2$. Subsequent work extended the question to the non-strict bound. We give a complete structural characterization of connected graphs $G$ with $|V(G)|\ge2$ satisfying $λ_2(G)\le(\sqrt5-1)/2$. Their complements are described by disjoint unions of graphs from an explicit family with least adjacency eigenvalue at least $-(1+\sqrt5)/2$, possibly together with a cone or a thin or thick spider constructed from disjoint unions of members of the same family, subject to explicit numerical inequalities. This provides a positive characterization of the class, going beyond the classical result of Cvetković and Simić that the bound $λ_2\le(\sqrt5-1)/2$ admits only finitely many minimal forbidden induced subgraphs.

papers.title: Polynomial convexity and non-polynomial convexity of totally real discs in $\mathbb{C}^2$
papers.abstract: We study the polynomial convexity of smooth totally real discs contained in the boundaries of strongly pseudoconvex domains in $\mathbb{C}^2$. Using Wermer's classical example, we construct a bounded domain with smooth strongly pseudoconvex boundary containing a non-polynomially convex totally real disc. We also construct a nonsingular Levi-flat hypersurface in a non-Runge domain containing such a disc. This provides a partial negative answer, to a conjecture proposed in an earlier work. Furthermore, we prove that the Wermer graph over the closed disc of radius $R$ is polynomially convex for every $R\in (0,1)$. Finally, we establish a sufficient condition for the polynomial convexity of totally real discs contained in the smoothly bounded strongly pseudoconvex domains in $\mathbb{C}^2$.

papers.title: A Reider-type theorem for syzygies of cyclic covers of anticanonical rational surfaces
papers.abstract: Let $π\colon X\to S$ be a smooth ramified cyclic cover of an anticanonical rational surface, with $κ(X)\geq0$, and let $A$ be a divisor on $S$. We prove a Reider-type theorem for syzygies: for every integer $p\ge 0$, the adjoint divisor $K_X+π^*A$ satisfies Property $\mathrm{N}_p$ provided that $A\cdot C\geq p+3$ for every curve $C\subseteq S$ with $C^2\le 1$. One ingredient is a syzygy criterion for finite covers that reduces the weight-two Koszul vanishing on $X$ to weight-one vanishing for the nontrivial character modules on $S$. The most delicate case, in which $\dim|-K_S|=0$ and $K_S^2<0$, is handled by a separate geometric argument.

papers.title: Convergence properties of nonlinear RLC electrical networks
papers.abstract: Convergence properties of general electrical networks with grounded nonlinear capacitors at the nodes and nonlinear inductors and resistors at the edges are studied. It is shown how, under appropriate conditions, for every initial condition there exists a unique equilibrium to which the system converges asymptotically. Partial extensions to networks with terminals or current sources are also provided. For RC networks this is compared with the use of an alternative storage function based on the co-content functions of the resistors.

papers.title: Rule-based hardware-configurable static analysis for quantum programs
papers.abstract: The rapid evolution of quantum hardware necessitates an adaptable static analysis framework for validating quantum programs. In this work, we introduce SHARP, a rule-based static analysis framework designed for OpenQASM that decouples hardware-specific constraints from the validation engine. By employing a rule-based approach, SHARP allows quantum computing services to validate programs against evolving instruction set architectures (ISAs) without having to modify the core analysis engine. SHARP achieves this by ingesting ISA descriptions as standalone data, making the validation engine resilient to hardware updates. Furthermore, the framework employs an analysis-driven validation mechanism that enables multi-stage validation, simplifying rule construction and enhancing extensibility. We demonstrate how SHARP supports hardware-specific validation tasks and discuss its impact on quantum software development, including language decoupling, program-level constraint validation, and feature access control. Our findings suggest that SHARP provides a path toward a scalable and maintainable programming interface for quantum computing.

papers.title: Unfolding of symmetric monoidal $(\infty,n)$-categories
papers.abstract: We prove Lurie's proposed description of left rigid symmetric monoidal $(\infty,n)$-categories in terms of purely $\infty$-categorical data. More precisely, unfolding gives an equivalence between left rigid symmetric monoidal $(\infty,n)$-categories and complete categorical chain complexes of rigid symmetric monoidal $\infty$-categories. More generally, unfolding identifies skeletal sequences with categorical chain complexes without the completeness condition. We extend these equivalences to $(\infty,\infty)$-categories and, stably, obtain an equivalence between complete unbounded categorical chain complexes and left rigid categorical spectra. We also analyze their groupoid completion and express the homotopy groups of the associated spaces and spectra in terms of categorical cycles and boundaries. As examples, we construct the categorical chain complexes associated to geometric and algebraic bordism categories, including their equivariant variants, and to iterated span categories. Their localizations recover classical bordism and $L$-groups, while the span examples are related to algebraic $K$-theory.

papers.title: Seeing Why: Exact Evidence Maps for Quantum and Optical Image Classifiers
papers.abstract: When an image classifier decides, we can usually only estimate why. For quantum and all-optical classifiers that act linearly on amplitude-encoded pictures up to the measurement, with no trained classical network before or after them, each class's Born probability above its no-information share, $P_g - b_g$, splits exactly into contributions of the encoded amplitudes, shown as Born evidence maps (BEM). The split itself follows from known results on quadratic forms: with the transmitted light held fixed, it is what Integrated Gradients from a zero baseline and the Shapley value give. What we add is a way to measure it on the hardware that classifies, from class probabilities on a quantum chip or, in simulation, from camera frames on a lens bench, with no gradient circuit and no light sent backwards; a $g\times g$ map takes $1 + 2g^2$ runs. Deleting the 5% of pixels with the highest evidence drops accuracy from 73% to 9% (one seed), as occlusion and gradient $\times$ input do, while plain gradients remove much less. The classifiers share one architecture, a Fourier-plane mask followed by a brickwall circuit on qubits or by phase plates on a lens bench, read by a fixed Born headroom readout with no trained parameter; centring each picture on its own mean lets dark features count as much as bright ones. In simulation, four phase plates at one wavelength reach 72.3% on Caltech-10 colour photographs. On IBM's ibm_kingston, with the mask computed classically before approximate loading, 300 test pictures were classified at 37.7% against 10% chance (56.3% in exact simulation), and $2\times2$ maps of the filtered input of 30 test pictures drawn at random in advance, measured on the chip, agreed with the exact ones ($r = 0.88$; standard estimator 0.82). The maps also revealed a shortcut in the data; as the trim that removed it was chosen on test pictures, the Caltech-10 results are exploratory.

papers.title: Fixed points via tilting
papers.abstract: In this article we initiate the study of perfect commutative $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebras in the non-connective setting. As an application we show that given a finite $C_p$-space $X$ the $\mathbb{F}_p$-cochains on $X^{C_p}$ can be recovered as a base-change of the tilt of the Tate construction on cochains on $X^e$.

papers.title: Quantum Path Finder: Navigating Constraint Space via Non-Abelian Gauge Dynamics
papers.abstract: Quantum algorithms are commonly designed within the circuit paradigm or through adiabatic evolution. Here we introduce \emph{Quantum Path Finder} (QPF), a distinct algorithm-design paradigm based on non-Abelian gauge dynamics in a constraint-protected degenerate manifold. Each Boolean variable is promoted to a qutrit whose additional state represents an unassigned variable. The problem Hamiltonian then defines a connected manifold of feasible partial assignments, and time-dependent local qutrit rotations generate coherent transport on this manifold. Unlike conventional adiabatic quantum computation, QPF does not require the state to follow an instantaneous eigenstate along a prescribed interpolation: adiabaticity with respect to the constraint gap protects the feasible manifold, while adiabatic following within that manifold is optional. The algorithmic task is therefore to design paths and interference in constraint space rather than only to engineer a sequence of gates or a ground-state interpolation. We illustrate the framework with three applications. For unstructured search, a two-level analysis and numerical evolution recover Grover-type scaling under explicitly stated assumptions. For complete $3$-XORSAT, the accessible gauge sector has a size-independent gap, in contrast to the exponentially closing gap of a conventional transverse-field adiabatic path. For satisfiable $3$-SAT instances, finite-size benchmarks demonstrate high satisfied-clause fractions at short classical comparison budgets, without claiming an equal-cost quantum advantage. We also outline a superconducting-qutrit implementation and discuss the conceptual relationship between QPF and nondeterministic Turing machine.

papers.title: Finite-Regularity Counterexamples to Katok's Periodic-Point Conjecture
papers.abstract: For any $r>1$ and any nonnegative sequence $ω(n)=o(n)$, we construct a $C^r$ sphere diffeomorphism $f$ with $h=h_{\mathrm{top}}(f)>0$ such that $\displaystyle \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{n}\log\#\operatorname{Fix}(f^n)=h$ and $\displaystyle \sum_{n\geqslant 1}e^{-hn+ω(n)}\#\operatorname{Fix}(f^n) < \infty$. Every ergodic invariant probability measure is hyperbolic, and, apart from finitely many fixed points, all periodic points lie in a single topologically mixing homoclinic class of entropy $h$. This shows that the logarithmic periodic-point lower bound is optimal in finite regularity. In particular, we answer the finite-regularity case of Katok's periodic-point question in the negative.ative.

papers.title: Covariant Calculus and Hamiltonian Flows for Nonlocal Wasserstein Metrics
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study nonlocal metrics on smooth positive probability densities on a closed manifold, induced by symmetric jump kernels and density-dependent mobilities. First, we introduce the density-variation operator to express the density derivatives of the Dirichlet form and kinetic energy. Second, we construct density and velocity-field representations of the tangent space and prove their isometric equivalence. We use the generator's pseudoinverse to derive Levi-Civita connections and covariant differentials in both representations. Third, we establish mechanical Hamiltonian dynamics in both tangent representations; an action principle and Legendre duality identify the Hamilton--Jacobi and covariant Newton equations; smooth negative gradient flows admit a zero-energy Hamiltonian lift. Entropy diffusion, nonlocal mean-field equations, Keller--Segel dynamics, and a nonlocal Vlasov equation illustrate the resulting calculus. For geometric-mean mobility, the Hopf--Cole transformation of the nonlocal Schrödinger bridge system and the Madelung transformation of the nonlocal Schrödinger equation yield hyperbolic and trigonometric phase energies, respectively. At zero momentum, both recover the metric kinetic energy to second order.

papers.title: Generic point processes are intermittently hyperuniform and maximally rigid
papers.abstract: We study the prevalence of hyperuniformity and spatial rigidity among translation- invariant ergodic simple point processes of fixed intensity, in a topology controlling local second moments. Hyperuniform processes are dense but meagre. We prove that intermittent hyperuniformity is residual: the number variance exhibits hyperuniform behavior along some sequences of radii and hyperfluctuating behavior along others. Maximal rigidity is also residual. Thus generic processes are maximally rigid but not hyperuniform. A local-to-global principle reduces the proofs to cross-section constructions for an arbitrary fixed essentially free ergodic $\mathbb{R}^d$-action. We also prove that processes admitting revival sequences form a residual set and exhibit near-quadratic variance along suitable van Hove sequences.

papers.title: The equality $s(G)=η(G)+\exp(G)-1$ fails for $G=C_2^7\oplus C_6$
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group. The Erdős-Ginzburg-Ziv constant $\mathsf{s}(G)$ is the smallest positive integer $\ell$ such that every sequence over $G$ of length at least $\ell$ contains a zero-sum subsequence of length $\exp(G)$. The short zero-sum constant $η(G)$ is defined similarly, with the requirement that the zero-sum subsequence is nonempty and has length at most $\exp(G)$. It is known that $\mathsf{s}(G)\ge η(G)+\exp(G)-1.$ A conjecture proposed by W. Gao in 2003, which has been widely studied in zero-sum theory, predicts that $$ \mathsf{s}(G)=η(G)+\exp(G)-1 $$ for every nontrivial finite abelian group $G$. In this paper, we prove that this conjecture fails for the group $C_2^7\oplus C_6$.

papers.title: On Bykov Cycles in Filippov Systems
papers.abstract: We introduce two types of Bykov cycles for Filippov systems: crossing Bykov cycles, which retain the main dynamical features of their smooth counterparts, and sliding Bykov cycles, whose dynamics intrinsically involves the switching manifold. We construct explicit piecewise linear examples of both configurations. For crossing Bykov cycles, we prove the existence of hyperbolic invariant sets carrying symbolic dynamics, as in the classical smooth setting. For sliding Bykov cycles, under suitable open conditions, we obtain a countable symbolic dynamics on an invariant set; we prove that this invariant set has several interesting properties: the Hausdorff dimension of it and of its closure are equal, and it lies strictly between zero and one, and so both sets have zero Lebesgue measure; its closure is a Cantor set; and we also obtain conformal and invariant ergodic measures for the associated return dynamics. Finally, we show that convolution regularization of a suitable piecewise constant vector field produces a spatial cusp whose versal unfolding contains classical Bykov cycles. Thus, Bykov-type dynamics arises in the non-smooth setting both intrinsically, through crossing and sliding mechanisms, and through smooth regularization.

papers.title: Finite tests and low-rank excluded minors for matroid path-width two
papers.abstract: The path-width of a matroid is the minimum, over all orderings of its ground set, of the maximum value of its connectivity function on an initial segment. For any two connected rooted matroids whose roots are neither loops nor coloops, we form the 2-sum of each with a third such rooted matroid by identifying their roots and deleting the common element. The two original rooted matroids are equivalent when these sums agree on whether their path-width is at most two for every choice of the third rooted matroid. We prove that the two rooted matroids are equivalent if and only if this agreement holds for thirteen fixed graphic or cographic rooted matroids. They distinguish exactly twenty equivalence classes, and, moreover, there exists no family of twelve fixed connected rooted matroids that can guarantee this. Using these classes, we show that the tree in the canonical tree decomposition of an excluded minor for path-width at most two has diameter at most ten edges. For a connected matroid given by a tree decomposition using 2-sums, we give an exact recurrence to decide whether its path-width is at most two and to construct an ordering of width at most two when possible. Moreover, we derive a formula for the path-width of parallel extensions that gives complete binary excluded-minor lists in ranks three, four and five, containing two, four and eleven isomorphism classes, respectively.

papers.title: Calabi flow on polarized Kähler surfaces
papers.abstract: We study global smooth Calabi flows on polarized Kähler surfaces $(M,L)$, assuming uniformly bounded Sobolev constants and the algebraic conditions $χ(\mathcal O_M)=1$ and $c_1(M)\cdot c_1(L)>0$. Using the orbifold compactness theorem, we prove a uniform Bergman estimate, construct a normal test configuration for each geometric limit, and establish uniqueness of the extremal orbifold limit up to polarized holomorphic isometry. K-polystability then identifies the limit with the original surface and gives a constant scalar curvature Kähler metric. We also prove finite-group equivariant versions of these results. Independently of the flow, we obtain a uniform Bergman lower bound for polarized cscK surfaces with bounded volume and Sobolev constants and $|S|\leq1$. We illustrate the hypotheses with nonstationary flows near a product cscK metric on $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$ and near Calabi's non-cscK extremal metric on the first Hirzebruch surface. Their controlled-cone energy inequalities follow from elementary calculations and continuity.

papers.title: OC-OPD: Observation-coordinated Supervision for On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: Reverse and forward Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergences provide complementary supervision in on-policy distillation: reverse KL refines the student's active token rankings, and forward KL allocates mass to teacher-supported candidates. At student-generated prefixes, we form a four-observation matrix by treating the student and teacher as both candidate sources and evaluators. The diagonal self-observations measure uncertainty, while source-centered cross-observations recover the two KL objectives. We establish an exact identity equating the Fisher inverse-metric coupling of their logit gradients with the sum of these contrasts, yielding a common local descent direction for distinct positive distributions. Observation-coordinated on-policy distillation (OC-OPD) uses observations to set preferences, closed-form bargaining to coordinate gradients, and distributional discrepancy to scale the update. Across three heterogeneous student settings (non-thinking generation, thinking generation, and base-model initialization), OC-OPD achieves strong gains in mathematical reasoning and transfers effectively to out-of-distribution scientific question answering and code generation. Our code is publicly available at: https://github.com/RuoranXu/OC-OPD.

papers.title: Chain Conditions for Abelian Normal Subgroups
papers.abstract: We investigate various chain conditions for abelian normal subgroups of groups, following Robinson (1968). We focus on the maximal condition for abelian normal subgroups, an exceptional case excluded from his results except for some counterexamples. In particular we show that a hypercentral group satisfies the maximal condition for abelian normal subgroups if and only if it is is finitely generated nilpotent.

papers.title: The Erdős--Hajnal property for paths
papers.abstract: The well-known Erdős-Hajnal conjecture states that for any graph $H$, there is a constant $c=c(H)>0$ such that every $n$-vertex graph $G$ with no induced copies of $H$ contains a clique or an independent set of size at least $n^{c}$. In this paper, we prove that the Erdős-Hajnal conjecture holds for every path.

papers.title: Moduli spaces of rank 2 sheaves on $\mathbb P^3$ via Quot schemes
papers.abstract: We study the Gieseker--Maruyama moduli space $M_{c_3}$ of stable rank 2 torsion-free sheaves on $\mathbb{P}^3$ with Chern classes $c_1=-1$, $c_2=1$, and odd $c_3 \le 1$. Every such sheaf $E$ has reflexive hull $E^{\ast\ast}$ parametrised by $M_1$, and the quotient $E^{\ast\ast}/E$ is a 0-dimensional sheaf of length $n = (1-c_3)/2$. We prove that $M_{c_3}$ is isomorphic to the relative Quot scheme $\mathsf{Quot}_{\mathbb{P}^3 \times M_1/M_1}(\mathscr{R},n)$, where $\mathscr{R}$ is the universal reflexive sheaf over $M_1$. Our technique combines (i) Bridgeland-type wall-crossing in Donaldson--Thomas theory, (ii) the theory of good moduli spaces, (iii) deformation theory in dgla and Ext-quiver language. We deduce that $M_{c_3}$ is connected, and we analyse its \emph{smoothable component} $M_{c_3}^{\mathsf{main}}$, proving it is rational and generically smooth of dimension $4n+3$. We further prove that $\dim \mathrm{Sing} M_{c_3} \geq 4n-2$ for all $n \geq 2$. Finally, we provide a geometric characterisation for the cases $n\leq 2$. We show that $M_{-1}$ is a smooth rational projective variety of dimension 7 and compute its motive in the Grothendieck ring of varieties, while $M_{-3}$ is shown to be an integral, normal variety of dimension 11 that is regular in codimension 4.

papers.title: Carleson Measures and Integral Operators on Fock--Sobolev Spaces
papers.abstract: For integers $n\ge1$ and $N\ge0$, let $\mathbf g=(g_0,\ldots,g_N)$ be a vector of entire functions. We consider the generalized integral operator \ [T_{\mathbf g}^{(n,N)}f =I^n\!\left(\sum_{j=0}^N g_jf^{(j)}\right), \qquad (Ih)(z)=\int_0^z h(w)\dd w. \] We characterize its boundedness and compactness between Fock--Sobolev spaces $\F_m^p$ and $\F_\ell^q$, where $0<p,q<\infty$ and $m,\ell\ge0$ are integers. The coefficients of critical total degree determine the operator modulo compact operators and yield essential-norm estimates. In the Hilbert case, a Laurent Toeplitz representation gives the exact essential norm, a Fredholm criterion and an index formula. As an application, we obtain conditions for solutions of linear differential equations to belong to Fock--Sobolev spaces, including a necessary and sufficient polynomial zero condition in the Hilbert case. For entire functions $u_0,\ldots,u_N$ and $\varphi$, we also characterize boundedness, compactness and essential norms of the operators \[ L_{\mathbf u,\varphi}^{(N)}f =\sum_{j=0}^N u_j\,f^{(j)}\circ\varphi. \] The proofs use Carleson measure characterizations for finite sums of weighted differentiation operators on Fock--Sobolev spaces.

papers.title: Asymptotic Stability and $L^p$ Time-Decay Rates of Rarefaction Waves for Systems of Viscous Conservation Laws
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotic stability and quantitative time-decay rates of rarefaction waves for one-dimensional $n\times n$ strictly hyperbolic systems of viscous conservation laws. While the nonlinear stability of rarefaction waves for $2\times 2$ systems was established by Xin \cite{Xin1988,Xin1989}, extending such results to general $n\times n$ systems presents additional difficulties arising from the possible coexistence of positive and negative transverse relative characteristic speeds and nonlinear interactions between distinct characteristic families. Moreover, establishing standalone $L^p$ energy estimates and explicit algebraic decay rates for general viscous systems without $L^1$ localization remains a significant challenge. In this paper, we establish both the global $H^2(\R)$ asymptotic stability and, for the first time, standalone physical-space $L^p$ energy estimates and explicit algebraic $L^p$ time-decay rates for weak rarefaction waves. Specifically, for every integer $p\ge 3$, we prove that the perturbation $U(t)-\bar{U}(t)$ around the smooth Burgers rarefaction profile $\bar{U}$ decays in $L^p(\R)$ at the rate \[ \|U(t)-\bar{U}(t)\|_{L^p}\le C_p\bigl(\|U_0-\bar{U}(0)\|_{H^2}^2+δ^3\bigr)^{1/2}(1+t)^{-\frac{1}{2}(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{p})}, \] where $δ$ denotes the wave strength. Our proof combines a diagonal characteristic weight matrix that yields coercive rarefaction damping in all characteristic modes with directed wave-interaction functionals that exploit the strict separation of characteristic speeds to control nonlinear coupling between distinct characteristic families. These estimates lead to a closed $L^p$ Lyapunov inequality, from which the algebraic time-decay rates follow by the one-dimensional Nash inequality.

papers.title: Theoretical relations between basic centrality measures in real-world networks
papers.abstract: We establish new relationships among several fundamental measures of real-world networks, including the average clustering coefficient, the global clustering coefficient, the average shortest-path length and degree centrality, closeness centrality, betweenness centrality and ksi-centrality. We further develop the theory of $j$-neighborhood centrality, which encompasses degree centrality and ksi-centrality as special cases.

papers.title: Time-Decay Rates toward Rarefaction Waves for the One-Dimensional Isentropic Compressible Navier--Stokes Equations
papers.abstract: While the asymptotic stability of rarefaction waves for the compressible Navier--Stokes equations has been well established since the pioneering works of Matsumura--Nishihara \cite{MatsumuraNishihara1986} and Liu--Xin \cite{LiuXin1988}, the classical $L^2$ energy method yields only qualitative convergence in $L^\infty(\R)$ as $t\to\infty$ without any explicit decay rate. In this paper, we establish for the first time a standalone \(L^4\) energy estimate for perturbations of a weak rarefaction wave in the one-dimensional isentropic compressible Navier--Stokes system, thereby obtaining the first explicit algebraic time-decay rates for this model. Specifically, for small initial perturbations in $H^2(\R)$ and small wave strength $δ$, we prove that $(v-V,u-U)$ decays in $L^4(\R)$ at the rate \[ \|(v-V,u-U)(t)\|_{L^4}\le C\bigl(\|(v_0-V(0),u_0-U(0))\|_{H^2}+\sqrtδ\bigr)(1+t)^{-1/8}, \] where \((V,U)\) denotes the smooth rarefaction wave, while the relative Riemann invariants \(z_\pm\) of the perturbed system decay in \(L^\infty(\R)\) at the rate \((1+t)^{-1/6}\). The proof relies on a new local quartic energy estimate for \(z_\pm\) and \(z_\pm-Q\), where \(Q=μ(v)v_x-μ(V)V_x\), as well as a nonlocal half-space wave-interaction functional for corrected characteristic modes and a weighted higher-order derivative energy estimate coupled at the scale of the one-dimensional Nash inequality.

papers.title: The signed error-sum function of tent-map expansions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the signed error-sum function of tent map base series introduced by Dai and Tang in 2011. We show that the function is discontinuous at every dyadic rational in the open unit interval, although it was asserted to be continuous. We determine its values at these points and analyze its range, differentiability, and variation. We also obtain sharp covering estimates for its graph and calculate the Hausdorff, box-counting, and covering dimensions of the graph, which are $1$, $1$, and $0$, respectively. Moreover, we show that the signed error sum agrees with Lévy's function away from dyadic rationals and that the unsigned error sum is the Takagi function.

papers.title: Multi-Period Donation Allocation for Food Banks under Stochastic Capacity and Supply
papers.abstract: Each food bank within the national Feeding America network faces the challenge of distributing donated food equitably across the food-insecure population it serves while minimizing food storage and waste over a multi-period planning horizon. Donated food supply is highly stochastic, and distribution to beneficiaries is done by autonomous local agencies whose capacities are uncertain and vary over time. Based on our long-standing partnership with a regional food bank in the southeastern United States, we address the equitable and effective distribution of food donations to charitable agencies over a finite planning horizon under uncertain capacity and supply. We derive structural properties of this problem and use them to develop efficient heuristics. An extensive numerical study evaluates the performance of the heuristics relative to a stochastic dynamic programming benchmark, which suffers from the curse of dimensionality. One heuristic consistently provides near-optimal solutions and can be easily implemented by food banks. Our results also apply to other problems involving the equitable and effective distribution of scarce resources under stochastic capacity and supply.

papers.title: Experimental demonstration of phase-conjugated twin-wave coherent reception over 100 km with injection locking assisted phase stabilization
papers.abstract: Recovering complex optical signals with high sensitivity is central to coherent communication and sensing. Beyond conventional homodyne and heterodyne reception, phase-conjugate twin-wave encoding and phase-sensitive joint detection offer an alternative strategy with enhanced sensitivity. Extending this approach to long-distance transmission of high-order-modulated signals is challenging because optical phase coherence must be maintained at the receiver. Here we experimentally demonstrate injection-locking-assisted phase-conjugated twin-wave reception of 200-MBaud signals with modulation formats up to 256-QAM over 100 km of optical fiber. Optical injection locking regenerates the local oscillator (LO) from a reference transmitted through the 16 dB-loss link, while pilot-assisted optical feedback stabilizes the relative signal-LO phase, enabling coherent combining of the phase-conjugated twin waves at a single balanced photodetector. At equal received signal-photon number per quadrature in each data-carrying optical mode, the measured PCTW signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) exceeds the ideal single-mode homodyne standard quantum limit (SQL) benchmark. The SNR gains over the measured homodyne and conventional heterodyne results are about 3 dB and 6 dB, respectively. Constellation and bit-error-rate measurements show that this gain improves high-order data recovery relative to heterodyne reception. An ideal Gaussian-noise model predicts a photon information efficiency of 1.54 bits per received signal photon for uniform 16-QAM. These results establish an injection-locking-assisted coherent receiver architecture that implements joint detection of phase-conjugated twin waves over 100 km of fiber with enhanced sensitivity, providing a practical route for photon-efficient coherent communication.

papers.title: Asymptotic delta-like behavior of the weighted taper in Thomson's multitaper F-test
papers.abstract: We study the weighted taper arising in Thomson's multitaper F test, which is constructed from pre-plunge discrete prolate spheroidal wave functions (DPSWF). Numerical evidence suggests that, in the asymptotic regime, the Fourier transform of this taper converges to a delta measure supported at the origin. We provide a rigorous theoretical justification for this behavior.

papers.title: Convergence Guarantees for the Broximal Point Method under Perturbations
papers.abstract: The Broximal Point Method (BPM) of Gruntkowska et al. (2025) comes with strong guarantees for convex optimization: under convexity alone, it terminates after finitely many steps and converges linearly in function value, with bounds that do not depend on the condition number or on any other regularity property of the objective. Each iteration, however, requires the exact minimization of the objective over a ball, which is generally intractable. As a first step toward implementable variants, we study the method when these subproblems are solved only approximately. We introduce and analyze Inexact BPM, which replaces the exact broximal point by an approximation and makes no assumption on how this approximation is obtained. Under summable or sufficiently small errors, we bound the number of iterations needed to reach a neighborhood of the set of minimizers, and these bounds remain independent of the regularity of the objective. Under the weaker requirement that the errors stay below the ball radius, we prove sublinear convergence in function value for the exact broximal points underlying the perturbed iterates, valid until the target neighborhood is reached, and we recover linear rates under bounded sublevel sets or strong convexity.

papers.title: Entire solutions of Fermat-Type Partial Differential-Difference equations in higher dimensions
papers.abstract: The purpose of this paper is to investigate the finite-order entire solutions of the following Fermat-type partial differential-difference equations: \begin{align*} (P_1(z)f(z+c))^{m_1}+\left(P_2(z)f(z)+\sideset{}{_{j=1}^m}{\sum} Q_j(z)\partial_{z_j}(f(z))\right)^{m_2}=P(z), \end{align*} \begin{align*} (P_1(z)f(z))^{m_1}+\left(P_2(z)f(z+c)+\sideset{}{_{j=1}^m}{\sum} Q_j(z)\partial_{z_j}(f(z))\right)^{m_2}=P(z) \end{align*} and \begin{align*} \left(\sideset{}{_{j=1}^m}{\sum} Q_j(z)\partial_{z_j}(f(z))\right)^{m_1}+\left(P_1(z)f(z+c)+P_2(z)f(z)\right)^{m_2}=P(z), \end{align*} in $\mathbb{C}^m$, where $m_1,m_2\in\mathbb{N}$ such that $m_1+m_2>2$, $c=(c_1,c_2,\ldots,c_m)\in\mathbb{C}^m$, $P(\not\equiv 0)$, $P_1$, $P_2$ and $Q_i\;(i=1,2,\ldots,m)$ are polynomials in $\mathbb{C}^m$ such that $P(z)$ is irreducible in $\mathbb{C}^m$. The results established in this paper generalize those of Xu et al. \cite{Xu-Luo-Cao-2025} from $\mathbb{C}$ to $\mathbb{C}^m$.

papers.title: Boundary fibers of the holonomy map for complex projective structures
papers.abstract: We study the Morgan--Shalen boundary of holonomy representations of complex projective structures on a compact Riemann surface of genus at least two. We prove that every direction defined by a holomorphic quadratic differential with a multiple zero admits distinct projective marked length limits. Together with Dumas's uniqueness theorem for simple zeros, this gives a complete characterization of directions with unique limits. We also establish that no nonzero abelian length function can occur in the holonomy boundary of any such fixed surface, regardless of the limiting quadratic differential. Finally, we characterize all directional boundary fibers by a necessary-and-sufficient analytic condition involving valued representations and the holomorphic jet bundle underlying an oper.

papers.title: Global existence and decay estimates of solutions for the compressible Prandtl type equations in Sobolev spaces
papers.abstract: This paper addresses the global existence and large-time decay of solutions to the two-dimensional compressible Prandtl equations in Sobolev spaces. We study small perturbations around a monotone shear flow and establish global weighted Sobolev estimates together with precise time-decay rates for the solutions. The main difficulties are that the normal velocity causes a loss of one tangential derivative, the variable density gives rise to nonstandard boundary and shear-flow coupling terms, and the global-in-time argument requires sufficiently strong decay to close the time-weighted energy estimates. To overcome these difficulties, we combine the cancellation method introduced by Masmoudi and Wong~\cite{MW2015} with the good-quantity approach developed by Paicu and Zhang~\cite{PZ2021}, together with weighted shear-flow estimates and a careful treatment of the natural boundary structure. Under suitable assumptions on the density perturbation, the shear flow, and the function $f(t)$ describing the outer tangential flow, we prove the global-in-time well-posedness of solutions in weighted Sobolev spaces. In this sense, the present result may be viewed as a Sobolev-space counterpart of the recent analytic-framework result obtained by Chen, Huang and Li (J. Funct. Anal. 286 (2024), 110322)~\cite{CHL2024} for the two-dimensional compressible Prandtl-type equations, while requiring a weaker time-decay assumption on the density perturbation.

papers.title: Parameter-robust preconditioners for a stabilized control-volume discretization of Biot's equations
papers.abstract: We develop and analyze parameter-robust block preconditioners for a stabilized control-volume discretization of the quasi-static Biot equations. Beginning with a five-field formulation, we eliminate the poroelastic stress and time-scaled Darcy velocity through independent vertex-local solves, obtaining a symmetric cell-centered displacement--rotation--pressure system. A macrocell rotation-jump term stabilizes the weak-symmetry constraint. We prove the well-posedness of the fully discrete scheme and show that the condensed, coupled displacement--rotation mechanics block is uniformly spectrally equivalent to its block-diagonal counterpart. For uncoupled preconditioners, we derive an exact discrete pressure-control criterion and a sufficient parameter condition that accommodates the scaling \(c_0\asymp K_{\rm dr}^{-1}\), thereby allowing the storage coefficient to vanish in the nearly incompressible limit. We then construct a Schur-consistent pressure block that approximates the mechanics-induced pressure correction and prove its uniform equivalence to the exact pressure Schur complement. These results yield parameter-independent spectral bounds for block-diagonal preconditioning and weighted field-of-values estimates for lower-triangular preconditioning. Practical realizations employ a macrocell mass-matrix approximation for the stabilized rotation block and tailored two-grid solvers for the displacement and pressure blocks. Numerical experiments verify the expected convergence behavior in two dimensions and demonstrate robust performance under mesh refinement and broad variations of the physical parameters in both two and three dimensions.

papers.title: Alternating Sums in Compositions
papers.abstract: Motivated by the recent asymptotic formula for the moment of the alternating sum of parts in partitions by Craig and Li, we study the moment of the alternating sum of parts in compositions. We establish closed formulas for this moment using techniques involving generating functions, matrix diagonalization, Krawtchouk polynomials, differential equations, and Faà di Bruno's formula. Our result is connected with some known integer sequences in the OEIS and admits a combinatorial interpretation by coin flipping.

papers.title: On closed symmetric monoidal enriched $\infty$-categories
papers.abstract: We show that a closed symmetric monoidal V-enriched $\infty$-category can be described by a lax symmetric monoidal functor to V from its underlying $\infty$-category.

papers.title: Quadratic bounds for intersecting hypergraphs: An affirmative answer to a question of Duke and Erdős
papers.abstract: Let $m(k,b)$ denote the minimum number of edges in an intersecting $k$-uniform hypergraph in which every $(k-1)$-set of vertices is disjoint from at least $b$ edges, with $m(k,b)=+\infty$ if no such hypergraph exists. Duke and Erdős [Congressus Numerantium (1980)] asked whether $m(k,k)=o(k^4)$ is possible. In this paper, we answer this question affirmatively and determine the order of growth of $m(k,k)$ by proving that $k^2+1\leq m(k,k)\leq Ck^2$ for all sufficiently large $k$, where $C$ is an absolute constant. More generally, we show that $m(k,b)=Θ(kb)$ for all sufficiently large odd $k$ and every integer $b$ with $k\leq b\leq (k-1)(k-3)/2$, where the implied constants are independent of $k$ and $b$.

papers.title: On cylindrical directions of regular surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ derived from contact with spherical cylinders
papers.abstract: We investigate the contact of regular surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ with spherical cylinders $S^2(r) \times \mathbb{R}$. We introduce cylindrical directions of these surfaces, defined by the axes of spherical cylinders having degenerate contact with the surfaces, and show that these directions capture the ridge condition of projected regular surfaces under orthogonal projection along these directions.

papers.title: Generalized Hamiltonian gradient flow of contact type II: singularities, cut locus, and controllability
papers.abstract: We study singularities, cut loci and controllability for time-dependent contact Hamilton--Jacobi equations. A contact version of Arnaud's theorem identifies the superdifferential graph of an evolved profile with the contact Hamiltonian image of the differential graph of its positive Lax--Oleinik regularization. This representation defines intrinsic singular characteristics and determines their initial velocity through a minimum-energy selection on the space-time superdifferential. The curves are continuous and locally $1/2$-Hölder, but they need not be locally Lipschitz. The exponent $1/2$ is optimal even for a quadratic Hamiltonian. The intrinsic characteristic issued from a cut point is singular at every later time in the short-time interval. We also establish the contact Lax--Oleinik commutator identities, which identify the superlevel and sublevel sets of the cut time with the corresponding terminal momentum graphs through bi-Lipschitz maps. For reachable terminal data we characterize the associated calibrated sets, and we describe all continuous initial data that reach a prescribed semiconcave profile. The proofs use Herglotz' variational principle and short-time estimates for contact fundamental solutions.

papers.title: Improved lower bounds for the kissing number in dimensions 49 to 61
papers.abstract: We give explicit kissing configurations in R^d for every d = 49, ..., 61. The lower bound is improved over the best previously published value in all thirteen dimensions, by margins from 232 to 159,220 points and by 506,461 points in total. The configurations are obtained from the antipodal block lift of Yang et al. applied to the 52,416,000-point minimal shell of the extremal even unimodular lattice P_48p, using a class of 7,193 minimal lines and, in each dimension, a kissing configuration of R^k (k <= 15) with the largest available number of antipodal pairs. Two ingredients are new. The published class of 7,077 lines is grown to 7,193 by local search in three stages, as a sequence of exchanges between candidate lines and class lines; and the point count, which equals 52,416,000 + 2S + 2t with t the number of antipodal pairs and S the size of the union of t isometric images of the class, is maximised as a maximum-coverage problem by greedy search with iterated local search over pools of 4,000 automorphic images, reaching 92-100% of the trivial bound 7,193t. All results are verified in exact integer arithmetic, and the certificates are distributed with the code. Code and data: https://github.com/dimkadimon/KissingNumbers

papers.title: Convergence in law of the maximum of the Riemann zeta function on expanding intervals near the critical line
papers.abstract: Let $T \to \infty$, let $τ$ be uniformly distributed on $[T,2T]$, and let $σ= σ(T)$ be a deterministic real part approaching $1/2$ from the right. We establish the convergence in law of the recentered maximum of $\log|ζ(σ+ \mathrm{i}τ+ \mathrm{i} h)|$ over $I_θ = \smash{[ - (\log T)^θ,(\log T)^θ]}$, for every fixed $θ> 0$. Under explicit conditions on the displacement $σ- 1/2$, the recentered maximum converges to a Gumbel distribution with scale parameter $1/(2\sqrt{1 + θ})$. The recentering is an exact upper quantile of the one-point law of the associated Haar field $F_{h}^{\mathrm{H}} = \Re\sum_{p^{j}\leq X}U_{p}^{j}/(jp^{j(σ+ \mathrm{i} h)})$, where the $U_{p}$ are independent and uniformly distributed on the complex unit circle. The positive constant in the limiting distribution is characterized by a Gaussian process describing the limiting microscopic increments of the Haar field around a high point. The result is established without the Riemann hypothesis.

papers.title: Federated Estimation of Loading Spaces in Tensor Factor Models under Differential Privacy
papers.abstract: Tensor factor models provide low-dimensional representations of tensor-valued observations while preserving their multiway structure. When these observations are held by different clients, privacy constraints may prevent them from being pooled for centralized analysis. We study estimation of common loading spaces in Tucker tensor factor models under federated differential privacy, allowing heterogeneous sample sizes, privacy budgets, and factor strengths. The proposed method combines private stability testing, Huber aggregation, and Gaussian perturbation at each client with weighted aggregation at the server. We establish non-asymptotic upper bounds governed by a scaled harmonic mean of the squared local error rates, and prove minimax optimality up to logarithmic factors under strong factors, fixed factor ranks, and fixed noise variance. We further develop a private calibration procedure that selects the local tuning parameters and aggregation weights without knowledge of the noise level or client-specific factor strengths. The resulting adaptive estimator preserves the privacy guarantee and attains the error rate obtained with oracle tuning. We illustrate the finite-sample performance of the proposed estimators through simulation experiments and an application to a Meditation Traits EEG dataset.

papers.title: The Brin-Katok local entropy formula for non-compact random dynamical systems and an application
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish the classical Brin-Katok local entropy formula for $C^1$ random dynamical systems on a complete Riemannian manifold (possibly non-compact) under a mild integrability condition. The proof depends on the constructions of measurable partitions adapted to asymptotically varying radii and finite measurable partitions with null-boundaries. As an application, under additional integrability assumptions, we obtain the Margulis-Ruelle inequality for $C^2$ random dynamical systems on complete non-compact Riemannian manifolds. Furthermore, we also construct a counterexample showing that the integrability condition above cannot in general be omitted.

papers.title: Optimal asymptotic bounds for design curves on manifolds
papers.abstract: A spherical $t$-design is a finite set of points on the $d$-dimensional unit sphere such that averaging any polynomial of degree at most $t$ over these points gives its exact spherical average. We study the corresponding notion for curves, where point averages are replaced by normalized arclength integration. For fixed $d\ge 2$, the length of such curves is known to be bounded below by a positive multiple of $t^{d-1}$ as $t\to\infty$. We show that this asymptotic order is attained: for every $d\ge 2$, there exists a constant $C_d>0$ such that, for every positive integer $t$ and every prescribed length $L\ge C_dt^{d-1}$, there is a simple spherical $t$-design curve of length $L$. This establishes the analogue for curves of the theorem of Bondarenko, Radchenko, and Viazovska, which resolved the Korevaar-Meyers conjecture for spherical design points. More generally, we prove the corresponding result on closed, connected Riemannian manifolds of dimension $d\ge 2$, where eigenfunctions of the Laplace-Beltrami operator substitute for polynomials. The proof combines a geometric construction of curves with continuously adjustable local lengths and an application of Brouwer's degree theorem.

papers.title: Well-posedness and Quantitative Stability for Degenerate Fokker--Planck Equations with Rough Coefficients
papers.abstract: We establish quantitative stability and well-posedness for degenerate Fokker--Planck equations with Sobolev-regular and possibly fully degenerate diffusion coefficient. For two classes of rough drifts, stability estimates imply uniqueness, and existence is proved under suitable conditions. First, for anisotropic drifts with partial fractional Sobolev regularity, we prove both existence (as probability densities, essential for the probabilistic interpretation via superposition) and quantitative stability without imposing any growth conditions, covering the full range of fractional exponents and extending previous Lagrangian-flow results. Second, for drifts whose distributional gradients are given by singular integrals (e.g., Biot--Savart velocity fields from $L^1$ vorticity), we obtain stability estimates that allow the diffusion matrix to be time-space dependent and possibly degenerate, removing the prior restrictions of identity diffusion or bounded coefficients. Our results also recover the pure transport regime as a limiting case.

papers.title: Reduction of the integro-differential equation to an ordinary differential equation in ruin models with investment in a risky asset
papers.abstract: We study ruin models with the surplus invested in a risky asset and Erlang-distributed claims: non-life insurance, annuity payments and the mixed model. Assuming that the integro-differential equation for the survival probability has a classical twice continuously differentiable solution, we prove that this solution satisfies a linear ordinary differential equation. We construct explicit annihilating operators and write the coefficients of the reduced equation in closed form through binomial coefficients (for the mixed model with equal shape parameters). A converse criterion is obtained: a bounded solution of the reduced equation satisfies the integro-differential equation if and only if the residual vanishes at zero initial capital together with its derivatives of order below that of the annihilator. The exponent of the power branch at infinity is determined by the parameters of the risky asset alone and does not depend on the shape parameter. For the mixed model we classify the fundamental set of solutions: the exponentially growing modes are excluded by boundedness. The connection coefficient of the power branch is nonzero by a known power-law lower bound for the ruin probability, and in the annuity model by the reduced equation and the boundary condition at zero. Hence the ruin probability has power-law asymptotics with a positive constant for all shape parameters and all positive exponents, and a complete asymptotic expansion up to a multiplicative constant in all three models. For non-life insurance with Erlang claims of order two the expansion coefficients are computed by an explicit recurrence.

papers.title: Tensor Contraction with ZX Calculus, a Graph-Theoretic Approach
papers.abstract: Tensors are higher dimensional generalisations of vectors and matrices. Tensor networks are a diagrammatic representation of complicated relations between tensors, and tensor contraction is the evaluation of a tensor network analogous to matrix multiplication. Tensor networks and tensor contraction are ubiquitous in computer science, physics, and applied mathematics. Most existing tensor contraction algorithms are focused on finding an optimal contraction order of the tensors' bonds. However, finding the optimal order is an NP-hard problem. It is equivalent to another possibly more straightforward but still NP-hard problem of finding the treewidth of the line graph of the tensor network. While in general finding the optimal bond-by-bond contraction order is hard, in many practical cases there is no need to find an optimal order. This observation leads to the core innovation of this thesis, which is a new tensor contraction paradigm that uses graph theoretic operations to produce an equivalent tensor network whose line graph has lower treewidth than the original tensor network, before applying the bond-by-bond contraction algorithm.
