papers.abstract: A semi-Lagrangian discontinuous finite element scheme based on the characteristic Galerkin method (CSLDG) is investigated.The scheme directly discretizes an integral invariant model derived from the coupling of the transport equation and its adjoint equation.we have established, for the first time, error estimates for the fully discrete CSLDG scheme over a general domain Ωin \mathbb{R}^d.The error is decomposed into three parts: the ideal numerical solution error (the difference between the exact solution and the spatial discretization), the time-dependent test function error (the deviation of the test function caused by the numerical characteristic backtracking via an ODE solver), and the upstream region approximation error (the integration region deviation induced by numerical characteristic backtracking and spline boundary reconstruction).Under either compact-support boundary conditions or periodic boundary conditions with the velocity field and the solution sharing the same spatial periodicity, without requiring incompressibility,and assuming the standard CFL condition (Δt=O(h)) linking the time step and the mesh size, the following results are proved:Using piecewise P^K polynomial spaces, the L^2 error of the ideal numerical solution attains a suboptimal order O(h^K); If the ODE solver order satisfies D \ge 2K+2+d, the overall error retains the suboptimal order even after incorporating the time-dependent test function error;When the upstream region approximation error is further taken into account, for d \ge 2 the overall error remains suboptimal O(h^K) provided the spline reconstruction degree satisfies r \ge \max(K+1+d, d+2);

papers.title: Irreducibility of Full Multivariate Partial-Twuality Polynomials
papers.abstract: For each nonempty finite simple graph, we study five full multivariate partial-twuality polynomials defined using matrix ranks and coranks over $\mathbb{F}_2$. Over an arbitrary coefficient field $K$, we give a necessary and sufficient criterion for nontrivial factorization in the Laurent polynomial ring by additive separation of the exponent function across a nontrivial vertex partition. For $\bullet\in\{τ,δτ,τδ,δτδ\}$, the full multivariate partial-$\langle\bullet\rangle$ polynomial is irreducible in $K[z^{\pm1},\mathbf{u},\mathbf{v}]$ if and only if the graph is connected. For $δ$, we characterize the connected graphs whose polynomials are reducible by a condition on the parities of vertex degrees and of the numbers of common neighbors, and determine their irreducible factors. For each operation, the corresponding polynomial is irreducible in $K[z,\mathbf{u},\mathbf{v}]$ if and only if the graph is connected and at least one state has zero $z$-exponent. In particular, the full multivariate partial-$\langleδ\rangle$ polynomial is irreducible in $K[z,\mathbf{u},\mathbf{v}]$ if and only if the graph is connected and bipartite.

papers.title: Generating the liftable outer automorphism groups of regular cyclic covers
papers.abstract: Let $R_n = \bigvee_{i=1}^{n} S^1$ be a finite connected one-dimensional CW complex with $n \geq 2$, and let $\mathrm{Out}(F_n)$ be the outer automorphism group of the free group $F_n$, where $π_1(R_n)\cong F_n$. Let $p_k:\tilde{R}_n\rightarrow R_n$ be the standard $k$-sheeted regular cyclic cover of $R_n$ induced by a $\mathbb{Z}_k$-action on $\tilde{R}_n$ (which is homotopy equivalent to $R_{n_k}$, where $n_k=k(n-1)+1$) generated by a free rotation through $2π/k$ of $\tilde{R}_n$. Let $\mathrm{Out}_{F_{n_k}}(F_n)$ be the liftable outer automorphism group associated with a standard $k$-sheeted normal cover $p_k$. For $n\geq3$, we show that $\{\mathrm{Out}_{F_{n_k}}(F_n)\}_{k\geq2}$ forms an infinite family of self-normalizing subgroups of $\mathrm{Out}(F_n)$. For $n\geq2$, these groups are maximal if and only if $k$ is prime. Furthermore, we derive explicit finite generating sets for $\mathrm{Out}_{F_{n_k}}(F_n)$ for $k\geq 2$ and $n\geq 3$. Let $\mathcal{C}$ be the infinite chain of roses, and let $q_n:\mathcal{C}\longrightarrow R_n$ be the standard infinite-sheeted cover induced by $\langle τ\rangle$, where $τ$ is the unit translation on $\mathcal{C}$. As a final application, we obtain a finite generating set for $\mathrm{Out}_{F_\infty}(F_n)$ when $n\geq 3$.

papers.title: $p$-Wasserstein distance and Cramér-type moderate deviations for the multi-dimensional elephant random walk
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish $p$-Wasserstein bounds and Cramér-type moderate deviations for the multi-dimensional elephant random walk in the diffusive and critical regimes. Using a Gaussian convolution estimate with random covariance and the recursions for the conditional covariance, we obtain $W_{p,2}(\mathcal L(\widehat T_n),N(0,I_d))\le C_{a,d}pL_n$, where $\widehat T_n$ is normalized by its exact covariance and \[ L_n\asymp \begin{cases} n^{-1/2}\log n,&a\le1/3,\\ n^{-3(1/2-a)},&1/3<a<1/2,\\ (\log n)^{-3/2},&a=1/2. \end{cases} \] Consequently, we obtain radial Cramér-type moderate deviations for $x=o(L_n^{-1/3})$. We also determine the covariance bias under the uncorrected normalization and establish the corresponding Wasserstein bounds, lower bounds and moderate deviation estimates. The dimension and the model parameters are fixed.

papers.title: Dual Path Following for an Aerial Manipulator Under State and Input Constraints via Transverse Feedback Linearization
papers.abstract: This paper studies dual path following for a quadrotor carrying a three-degree-of-freedom arm. The center of mass of the combined system must follow a vehicle path and the end effector must follow a second path, while the arm respects its joint limits and avoids its singular postures. The vehicle and the arm are mechanically coupled, so one controller must handle both paths. With the center of mass and the end-effector path coordinates as outputs, and a dynamic extension of the thrust, the system admits a normal form without internal dynamics. We characterize the states where this normal form fails. We formulate the transverse feedback linearizing controller as a quadratic program that relaxes only the speed of the end effector along its path and imposes safety and actuator limits as inequality constraints. The program reduces to a scalar problem with a closed-form solution. If it remains strictly feasible for all time, the feedback is locally Lipschitz, both paths are invariant and attractive, and every constraint holds. In the physics engine Drake, the controller resolves a conflict between the two speed references by slowing the end effector while both paths remain invariant. By contrast, a cascade with a safety filter leaves both paths. Code and animations are available at https://gradslab.github.io/am_dual_pf-/

papers.title: Precise large deviations for the elephant random walk with Weibull-type and lognormal-type random step sizes
papers.abstract: We prove precise large deviations for the symmetric elephant random walk with random step sizes. When the distribution of $|Z_1-1|$ is subexponential, we first show that, for each fixed$p\in[0,1]$, there exists a positive number sequence $b_n\to\infty$ such that \[ \mathbb P(S_n>x)\sim \mathbb P(S_n<-x)\sim \frac n2\overline F(x) \] uniformly for $x\ge b_n$, where $\overline F(x)=\mathbb P(|Z_1-1|>x)$. This existence result requires no moment assumptions and does not specify the growth rate of $b_n$. For $p\in[0,3/4]$, we further give explicit sufficient conditions on $b_n$ under Weibull-type and lognormal-type tail conditions with a regularly varying factor $x^γL(x)$, where $γ\in\mathbf R$ and $L$ is a positive measurable slowly varying function. Analogous results hold with $\mathbb P(|Z_1|>x)$ and non-strict tails.

papers.title: Parameters and lim CM sequences: the Q-sequence conjecture and Lech's formula
papers.abstract: We prove that if a local ring has a weakly lim Cohen-Macaulay sequence of modules, then it satisfies the conjecture that every system of parameters is a Q-sequence. We also give a generalization of Lech's formula for the multiplicity of a local ring $(R,m)$ with respect to a system of parameters that allows a very large class of sequences of $m$-primary ideals generated by monomials in the parameters to be used in the calculation. The cases where the sequence of ideals consists of the powers of the ideal generated by parameters, or where the ideals in the sequence are generated by varying powers of the individual parameters all of which tend to infinity, which is Lech's original formula, are included.

papers.title: Transport for Conditional Sampling: Foundations and Applications
papers.abstract: Conditional sampling is central to Bayesian inference, generative modeling, and causal inference: given a joint law for random variables $X$ and $Y$ and an observation $Y=y$, one seeks to sample from the conditional law of $X\mid Y=y$. Even when the joint distribution is accurately represented, this task can be computationally difficult as it may require evaluating intractable normalizing constants or solving a new inference problem for each observation. Measure transport provides an approach to this problem by identifying a map with triangular structure that directly pushes forward a reference to the conditional of a joint distribution for any observation. This article reviews the theoretical, methodological, and algorithmic foundations of triangular transports, with the Knothe-Rosenblatt rearrangement as a canonical construction. We discuss methods for estimating triangular maps from finite samples, as well as their use in simulation-based inference and causal inference. While our primary aim is to review existing formulations, we also present new ideas and open questions for conditional sampling using transport.

papers.title: Boson sampling is fragile to loss
papers.abstract: Boson sampling experiments aim to demonstrate quantum computational advantage with increasing numbers of interfering photons. A central question is whether their computational hardness survives under photon loss. We show that even an arbitrarily small nonzero uniform loss rate permits efficient classical sampling in the average case when the rate remains fixed as the system grows. We exploit how loss suppresses correlations involving many photons to approximate the full output distribution using low correlation orders. The resulting samplers run in time polynomial in system size and inverse total variation error, with the error averaged over Haar random interferometers. The results apply to Fock state boson sampling with single-photon states in distinct input modes and arbitrary additional vacuum inputs, and to Gaussian boson sampling with equal squeezing of bounded strength in every input mode. Classical sampling is efficient even when the mean detected photon number grows linearly with system size, showing that large photon counts alone do not ensure computational hardness.

papers.title: $L^1$ amplification near a self-similar vortex collapse in 2D Navier-Stokes
papers.abstract: We establish quantitative $L^1$ instability for the two-dimensional Navier--Stokes equations near a self-similar three-vortex collapse as viscosity tends to zero. For every $0<γ<\frac12$ and $t_0\in(0,1)$, we construct solutions that are $O(ν^{1-γ})$-close in $L^1(\mathbb{R}^2)$ at $t_0$ but exhibit order-one $L^1$ separation in a shrinking neighborhood of the collapse point at times approaching collapse as $ν\to0$. By time translation, we also obtain pairs of solutions with initial $L^1$ distance $O(ν^{1-γ})$ that develop order-one separation at a fixed positive time. In both constructions, the solutions have the same viscosity and total circulation and are uniformly bounded in $L^1(\mathbb{R}^2)$. The proof exploits the amplification of small time delays, the fast speed of the vortex centers near collapse, together with sharp inviscid approximation estimates for the Navier--Stokes equations established in~\cite{Ga11,NguyenCollapse}.

papers.title: Variational learning of energy-stable macroscopic flow equations from microscopic laws
papers.abstract: We present a generalized variational approach for constructing energy-stable macroscopic partial differential equations (PDEs) directly from microscopic physical laws. Rather than fitting the PDE evolution for prescribed variables from macroscopic trajectories, we construct an extendable variational structure by adjoining auxiliary variables to seek autonomous reduced dynamics in an enlarged state space. By defining these variables as micro--macro encoders with explicit microscopic counterparts, we cast the learning problem as the sample-wise joint identification of the reduced state representation and the variational ingredients from time-discrete data, enabling systematic law-level transfer across scales. The resulting PDEs preserve frame indifference, physical constraints, and energy stability by construction, and admit a fluctuation--dissipation-consistent stochastic extension. Numerical results for the non-Newtonian hydrodynamics of polymeric fluids show that the learned models capture the viscoelastic responses induced by nonlinear and heterogeneous molecular interactions beyond empirical closures.

papers.title: Longest-Queue Policies in Dynamic Matching with Abandonments
papers.abstract: We study a dynamic two-way matching market in which agents of heterogeneous types arrive over time, wait to be matched according to a compatibility network, and abandon the system if their random patience expires. The decision maker collects match rewards and pays holding and abandonment costs, and seeks to maximize the expected net value over a finite horizon. We evaluate policies by their approximation ratio against a fluid benchmark, the optimal value of a linear-programming relaxation that upper bounds the expected net value of every policy. Under a general position gap (GPG) condition, which requires the unique optimal dual solution of this linear program to remain optimal under small perturbations of the arrival rates, we propose a longest-queue policy. The policy first uses this dual solution to identify a set of good match types and a set of critical agent types. Upon each arrival, it considers only good matches and matches the arrival to the critical partner with the longest queue subject to availabilities. In the high-volume regime, in which arrival rates are scaled by s, we prove that the policy attains an approximation ratio of at least 1-O(1/s) at every scale s >= 1 and every horizon T >= 1, so the ratio tends to 1 as s goes to infinity.

papers.title: Whittaker modules for the principal $W$-algebra $\mathcal W^k(\mathfrak{sl}_3)$ via free field realizations
papers.abstract: We study Whittaker and generalized Whittaker modules for the universal principal $W$-algebra $\mathcal W^k(\mathfrak{sl}_3)$, using two free field realizations: one in the Heisenberg vertex algebra of rank two and the other in the tensor product of the universal Virasoro vertex algebra with the Heisenberg vertex algebra of rank one. Under explicit conditions on the parameters, we construct universal Whittaker modules, establish their ordered bases, and obtain explicit irreducibility criteria. Under an explicit nondegeneracy condition, we also show that the submodules of these tensor products correspond to the submodules of the Virasoro factor. We prove irreducibility of the universal Whittaker modules constructed in this paper.

papers.title: The classification of Fano contact manifolds revisited
papers.abstract: We present an account of the classification of Fano contact manifolds based on the proof of OpenAI and the solution of LeBrun-Salamon conjecture by Hu, Liu and Wan. The proof combines their constructions with earlier results on contact lines, with some simplifications.

papers.title: The Marvelous Meixner Polynomials: Second Kind, First Class
papers.abstract: Meixner's classification asks which exponential generating functions can generate orthogonal polynomials. We follow the continuous Meixner family from this question to its moments, measures, and continued fractions. A beta integral and a bilinear identity establish positivity and orthogonality; Carlitz's Bernoulli and Euler constructions reveal further connections. Turning the parameter into a variable leads to rational orthogonality and Wall's fraction. We derive its Nevanlinna measure and unite the two spectral directions in a joint law with Cauchy marginals. Even finite pencils produce couplings with these exact marginals. Laguerre limits explain the gamma law governing joint extremes. Along the way, Meixner's scientific life, combinatorics, tangent numbers, and even zeta values illuminate the same structure.

papers.title: Effective Hausdorff dimension one is cofinal in the K-degrees
papers.abstract: Every K-degree has an upper bound of effective Hausdorff dimension one and Kurtz random sequences are cofinal in the K-degrees.

papers.title: Some variants of function domination
papers.abstract: We investigate whether classical recursion-theoretic notions defined by function domination remain unchanged when success is required only on sets of prescribed asymptotic density. We establish robustness for many such notions and uncover unexpected connections between familiar degree properties by comparing upper and lower density. In contrast, pdomination, as defined by Chong, Hoi, Stephan and Turetsky, is not robust under density weakenings. We also answer a question of Kjos-Hanssen and Nies by characterizing superhighness as domination with a threshold boundedly limit recursive in the oracle. As an application, we introduce supermaximal sets, a strengthening of maximality whose degrees are exactly the superhigh r.e. degrees.

papers.title: Degenerate neckpinches at the first $N$ singular times
papers.abstract: For every integer $N\ge1$, we construct a smooth closed connected strictly mean-convex rotationally symmetric surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose level set flow remains connected until extinction and has exactly one singular point at each of its first $N$ singular times. These singularities are degenerate neckpinches with the Angenent--Velázquez asymptotics: the leading deviation from the cylinder under parabolic rescaling is a cubic Hermite term.

papers.title: Topological transcendence degree and the dimension problem for perfectoid spaces
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a perfectoid field of characteristic $p$ with countable value group (for example, $K=\mathbb{C}_{p}^{\flat}$). We study Zariski-closed subsets \begin{equation*}Z\subseteq \mathbb{B}_{K}^{n,\mathrm{perfd}}\end{equation*}of the $n$-dimensional perfectoid closed unit ball $\mathbb{B}_{K}^{n,\mathrm{perfd}}$ over $K$. We use an example of Gleason, and its generalization obtained in the authors' previous work, to show that two natural notions of dimension for such Zariski-closed subsets, the Krull dimension $\dim(Z)$ and Huber's iterated transcendence degree $\mathrm{dim.tr}(Z)$, do not coincide, and that the gap between them can be arbitrarily large.

papers.title: A short proof of the complete Crouzeix inequality in dimension three
papers.abstract: We give a short proof of the complete Crouzeix inequality with sharp constant $2$ for matrices of dimension at most three.

papers.title: The Yangian associated with the binary tree
papers.abstract: In this article, we give three candidates for a definition of the Yangian associated with the binary tree $X^*$ and the group $Aut(X^*)$ consisting of automorphisms of $X^*$ which preserve the tree structure. The first candidate has the Schur-Weyl duality with one kind of an extension of the degenerate affine Hecke algebra. The second and third ones have a homomorphism corresponding to the wreath recursion.

papers.title: The MZ-property for three-term differences
papers.abstract: We study the Marcinkiewicz--Zygmund property for finite differences. A difference \[ D(f,h)=\sum_{k=1}^n a_k f(b_kh) \] is said to have the MZ-property if, for every measurable function $f$, \[ D(f,h)=o(h) \quad\text{and}\quad f(h)=o(1) \] imply \[ f(h)=o(h). \] In this paper, we characterize all three-node differences \[ D(f,h)=af(qh)+bf(rh)+cf(sh) \] having the MZ-property. In particular, for irrational differences with distinct nodes, we obtain explicit necessary and sufficient conditions in terms of the coefficients $a,b,c$ and the nodes $q,r,s$. As an application, our results resolve an open problem concerning a second-order Riemann difference.

papers.title: Log-Sobolev inequality for the sine-Gordon model in the subcritical regime
papers.abstract: We prove a logarithmic Sobolev inequality for the massive two-dimensional sine-Gordon model throughout the subcritical range $0<β<8π$. For fixed mass, volume and arbitrary real coupling, the constant has a positive lower bound independent of the lattice spacing. When the dimensionless coupling is small, the lower bound is also uniform in volume and approaches the Gaussian constant as the coupling tends to zero. This extends the known range $β<6π$ and gives a rate of entropy decay for the reversible Langevin dynamics that remains positive as the cutoff is removed. The proof follows the Polchinski flow to a positive physical scale, where the Hamiltonian is a bounded perturbation of a uniformly convex one. For interactions invariant under constant field shifts, spatial differences bound their curvature by the gradient energy. For the oscillating part, we compare Gaussian integration with an average in which the original cosine phase fluctuates independently of the remaining variables. We estimate the comparison error at an intermediate scale, then differentiate the remaining Gaussian density. This preserves both phase damping and spatial decay without assuming bounds on second derivatives of the incoming local terms. The resulting strict gain between scales closes the estimates for every fixed $β<8π$.

papers.title: Perfectness of partial Christoffel transforms of Nikishin systems
papers.abstract: We study multiple orthogonal polynomial systems obtained from a Nikishin system of two measures by applying a Christoffel transform to one of the measures at a point $x=x_0$. We show that if $x_0$ separates the supports of the generating measures, then the modified systems remain perfect. As an application, we prove that the type I multiple orthogonal polynomials of a Nikishin system have no zeros in the gap between the supports of its generating measures.

papers.title: A GPU-Accelerated and Geometry-Aware Quantum-Classical Framework for Optimized PES Scans with CUDA-Q
papers.abstract: Hybrid quantum-classical workloads, particularly Potential Energy Surface (PES) scans in quantum chemistry using batched VQE and QAOA, involve many structurally similar Hamiltonians differing only in coefficients. Existing warm-start and meta-optimization strategies reuse parameters between instances but still consume fixed quantum-classical resources, ignoring cross-instance structural similarities. We present OptiPESS, a GPU-accelerated runtime system for adaptive resource allocation in hybrid quantum-classical execution. OptiPESS introduces the Locality-Occupancy-Variance (LOV) metric, a lightweight, geometry-aware measure of Hamiltonian similarity, coupled with efficient alignment and Pauli-classification passes. Using LOV, OptiPESS performs distance-aware scheduling of iteration and shot budgets, predicting which instances can be skipped, quick-solved, or fully optimized. Implemented atop CUDA-Q with persistent multi-GPU execution and near-linear scaling, OptiPESS reduces classical and quantum evaluations by up to 78.3\% and wall-time by up to 74.8\% while maintaining baseline accuracy. This demonstrates how lightweight static analysis and adaptive scheduling can transform quantum-classical co-execution from fixed-budget loops into a predictive, resource-aware runtime.

papers.title: Continuity of Global Attractors under a Mass-Preserving Singular Memory Limit, with an Application to a Coupled Suspension Bridge System
papers.abstract: We study how the global attractor of a dissipative evolution equation with memory depends on the memory kernel when the kernel concentrates, while preserving its total mass, towards a Dirac mass at the origin. The mass-preserving rescaling is the structural feature that prevents the effective elastic coefficients from degenerating in the limit, so that the memory-dependent dynamics reduces formally to a memoryless damped system with unchanged elastic coefficients. For a coupled nonlinear suspension bridge system with past history, taken as a concrete model, we establish uniform-in-parameter dissipativity and uniform-in-parameter exponential stability of the associated linear semigroup. These uniform estimates yield uniform quasi-stability, uniform exponential attraction, finite-time convergence of the semigroups, and uniform Hölder continuity with respect to the perturbation parameter. We deduce upper semicontinuity of the global attractors, and, under an additional structural stability hypothesis on the limit attractor, lower semicontinuity as well. The analysis separates the general continuity mechanism, which applies to a broad class of memory kernels and dissipative systems, from the model-specific verification, which exploits the coupled bridge structure.

papers.title: Three-phase time minimization transportation problem with non-idle phases: a polynomial two-witness algorithm
papers.abstract: The three-phase time minimization transportation problem partitions the origin-terminal links into three sets used in consecutive phases and minimizes the sum of the phase shipment times. Optimal solutions may leave a phase idle, as in the main example of the original study. We require every phase to carry a positive integer quantity while leaving the split of the total requirement across phases free. Discarding idle solutions from the original algorithm does not, in general, solve this variant. We prove that the optimum is attained by fixing one witness link in each of two phases and deciding the third phase by a single network flow computation, with the optimal Phase-3 time of each witness pair located by binary search. The resulting exact algorithm is strongly polynomial. It extends to any fixed number of phases, whereas, when the number of phases is part of the input, even non-idle feasibility is strongly NP-complete; feasibility alone is fixed-parameter tractable in the number of phases via known rainbow-matching results. We also characterize the minimum time of each phase. On the main example, non-idleness raises the optimum from 38 to 41. On 3,650 random instances with up to $50\times50$ links the algorithm took at most 50.2 seconds, and non-idleness raised the optimal value in 41% of the 2,250 instances with equal phase sizes; on 90 sampled instances it was faster than a mixed integer programming solver on 80 with a direct formulation and on 65 with a tighter threshold formulation.

papers.title: Benign population landscapes do not transfer to empirical risk minimization in nonsmooth optimization
papers.abstract: Benign landscapes provide a geometric explanation for the success of iterative methods on nonconvex problems arising in data science. The landscape is benign if every local minimizer is global and every other critical point is a strict saddle. For methods that avoid strict saddles, convergence to a critical point therefore implies convergence to a global minimizer. For smooth stochastic optimization, a common strategy for establishing such landscapes proceeds in two steps: $(i)$ establish benign geometry for the population objective---which is often easier to analyze---and $(ii)$ transfer this geometry to the empirical objective using concentration of gradients and Hessians. Recent work has extended saddle-point avoidance guarantees to weakly convex nonsmooth optimization through the notion of active strict saddles. We show, however, that benign population geometry need not transfer to empirical objectives in this setting. Specifically, for robust phase retrieval with Gaussian measurements---a well-studied and highly structured problem---the population objective is benign. Nevertheless, the empirical objective has sharp spurious local minima with probability bounded away from zero as the sample size tends to infinity. This asymptotic probability lower bound is independent of the dimension.

papers.title: Exponential stability of the reduced Bresse--Gurtin--Pipkin system with one temperature
papers.abstract: We consider the reduced Bresse--Gurtin--Pipkin system with one temperature, obtained from the full Bresse--Gurtin--Pipkin thermoelastic beam system by neglecting one of the two temperature variables. This system was left essentially open in a recent work of Dell'Oro, where only a conjecture on its exponential stability condition was formulated. By combining the spectral analysis recently developed by Dell'Oro, Pata and Vasylyeva for the abstract Gurtin--Pipkin heat equation with the resolvent estimate framework of Dell'Oro for Bresse systems, we prove that the associated contraction semigroup is exponentially stable if and only if two explicit stability numbers, depending on the structural constants of the beam, both vanish. The proof is based on a spectral characterization of the infinitesimal generator in a half-plane containing the imaginary axis, an analysis of its spectrum on the imaginary axis, sharp upper bounds for the resolvent, and the Gearhart--Prüss theorem. In particular, we confirm the conjecture of Dell'Oro and provide a rigorous spectral analysis of the reduced system. The same method yields the exponential stability characterization of the corresponding reduced Bresse--Maxwell--Cattaneo system, and can be adapted to other reduced Bresse-type models.

papers.title: Decay of Correlations for Multiplicative Functionals of Determinantal Point Processes
papers.abstract: The main result of this paper is an upper bound on the correlations of multiplicative functionals of determinantal point processes. In particular, for the sine process, the correlations of a multiplicative functional associated with a rapidly decaying function decay quadratically. It follows that the spectral density of such functionals belongs to the Sobolev space $H_1$.

papers.title: Sharper Bounds for Graphical Two-Choice Allocation
papers.abstract: In graphical two-choice allocation, vertices are bins, and each arriving ball must be placed irrevocably at one endpoint of a uniformly random edge. The objective is to keep the maximum-minus-minimum load gap small at every time. On cycles, endpoint-local monotone rules incur polynomial gaps at long time horizons, whereas global rules can achieve polylogarithmic gaps. We prove a joint exponential-moment inequality for the orthogonal contrasts of a binary partition tree, controlling all contrasts along a root-to-leaf path simultaneously. Applied to the Bansal--Feldheim strategy, it improves the gap on every $κ$-edge-connected $d$-regular graph from $O((d/κ)\log^4 n\log\log n)$ to $O((d/κ)\log^3 n\log\log n)$. We give an explicit strategy on the $n$-cycle with expected gap $O(\log^2 n)$ uniformly over deterministic times and exponential tails at each such time. An Euler-tour projection yields $O(\bar d\log^2(2M))$ for every connected graph with $M$ edges and degree-proportional capacities. For lower bounds, we introduce a stochastic cut workload: the expected largest normalized overload forced by the requests, plus an indivisibility term. For every online integral strategy, the supremum over time of the expected gap is at least one sixth of this benchmark. Regular rings of cliques attain $Ω((d/κ)\log n)$ along an explicit family, improving the prior additive lower bound. With unequal capacities, the workload need not control the gap: one family has constant relative cut slack, bounded workload and gap $Ω(\log\log n)$; another has workload at most $20$ but forces gap $Ω(\log n)$ even for clairvoyant fractional allocations that remain irrevocable.

papers.title: An $\mathsf{FPRAS}$ for Mixed Volumes
papers.abstract: We design the first fully polynomial-time randomized approximation scheme ($\mathsf{FPRAS}$) to estimate the mixed volume of $n$ arbitrary compact convex sets in $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ specified by weak membership oracles. This disproves a longstanding conjecture of Gurvits (2009). $\textbf{AI Disclosure}$ The main ideas were generated entirely by GPT 6 Astra. The purpose of this paper is to provide a human-written exposition of the algorithm.

papers.title: Triple bubbles in the hyperbolic plane
papers.abstract: We prove that the standard triple bubble uniquely minimizes perimeter among clusters in the hyperbolic plane with three prescribed positive finite areas. The standard family admits global pressure coordinates, and its volume differential is the negative of a positive definite grounded weighted graph Laplacian. A normalized perimeter excess attains a comparison minimum under a perimeter bound and gives a strict comparison between actual and model pressures. Component relabeling reduces the possible topologies to an all-boundary network or a 4-daisy. Discrete comparisons exclude the 4-daisy; pressure-preserving face deletion reduces the remaining network to the standard tetrahedral configuration.

papers.title: Strict rearrangement inequalities for logarithmic p-Laplacians
papers.abstract: We establish cases of equality for the Polya-Szego inequality of the logarithmic p-Laplacian.

papers.title: A unified study of explosive processes with a root in the neighborhood of the unit circle
papers.abstract: This study is dedicated to autoregressive processes with stable and explosive time-varying coefficients, with a particular emphasis on a root located inside or outside the unit circle but converging towards the unit circle as the sample size increases (so that the limit process is integrated). Our objective is to develop a unified asymptotic theory that connects the classical stable, unstable and explosive regimes. By considering roots approaching the unit circle from both the stationary and explosive sides, we investigate how the corresponding asymptotic behaviors (of the process and the OLS) interact, and we try to build bridges between the rates associated with these regimes. This perspective provides a framework for understanding mixed autoregressive dynamics having a root in the neighborhood of the unit circle, provided a fairly general set of conditions.

papers.title: Unifying quantum smoothing theories with extended retrodiction
papers.abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 01 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41534-026-01379-9Unifying quantum smoothing theories with extended retrodiction

papers.title: Logical-Class Diagnostic Layer for Stabilizer Codes and Decoders via Supercharge Structures
papers.abstract: We develop a decoder-agnostic logical-class diagnostic layer for abelian Pauli stabilizer codes, motivated by fault-tolerant quantum computing. An ancilla fermionic register defines a nilpotent supercharge whose clean degree-zero harmonic sector is the code space. Projected-return blocks derived from graded commutators organize the recovery test of whether a decoder-selected correction preserves every encoded input for every error in a declared same-syndrome family; the passing syndromes form the certified faithful window. Demoting the supercharge to an exact binary diagnostic formulation classifies residuals modulo stabilizers, separating a check violation, a harmless stabilizer residual, and a syndrome-silent nontrivial logical action, with a two-sector form for CSS codes. Because the unknown fault cancels, the relative logical class of two record-compatible candidates is computable online. We verify the diagnostic formalisms on the Steane code and specify a static--circuit bridge audit protocol for the Gross bivariate-bicycle quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) code. The method supplements existing decoders without additional physical qubits for software use.

papers.title: An Introduction to Financial Derivatives: Open Lecture Notes
papers.abstract: These lecture notes give a broad introduction to financial derivatives at the level of a Masters program in quantitative finance. Topics include forward and futures contracts, no-arbitrage bounds and put-call parity, the binomial model, the fundamental theorems of asset pricing, Brownian motion and Itô calculus, the Black-Scholes model, the Greeks, variance swaps, local and stochastic volatility models including Heston, and static hedging of barrier options. Each chapter ends with exercises, and complete solutions, including Python code for the computational exercises, are provided in an appendix. The notes are open source: the LaTeX source is available at https://github.com/mattlorig/intro-financial-derivatives, and readers are invited to submit corrections and additions.

papers.title: Lehmer's number is not an orientable stretch factor in genus six
papers.abstract: Let $λ_L \approx 1.17628$ be Lehmer's number. We prove that no pseudo-Anosov homeomorphism of a closed orientable surface of genus six with orientable invariant foliations has stretch factor $λ_L$. This gives a negative answer to a question of Lanneau and Thiffeault on the minimal stretch factor in even genus. As a consequence, the minimal stretch factor $δ_6^{+}$ of such maps is the largest root of $x^{12}-x^{9}-x^{7}+x^{6}-x^{5}-x^{3}+1$, approximately $1.20189$. The proof combines the Lefschetz method of Lanneau and Thiffeault, the standardly embedded train tracks of Hironaka and Tsang, an elementary analysis of the transition digraph, and an obstruction from periodic conjugacy classes in the fundamental group.

papers.title: Stochastic Euler Products in the Paley-Wiener Space
papers.abstract: General sufficient conditions, in terms of stochastic Euler products, are given for a realization of a point process to have finite excess or finite deficiency in the Paley-Wiener space.

papers.title: Graceful supertrees with at most $2m-\mathrm{diam}(T)$ edges
papers.abstract: A graceful labeling of a tree with $m$ edges is a bijection from its vertices to $\{0,1,\ldots,m\}$ whose edge differences are pairwise distinct. The Graceful Tree Conjecture asserts that every tree admits such a labeling; equivalently, the smallest graceful tree containing a given $m$-edge tree has $m$ edges. For this embedding problem, Sethuraman, Ragukumar and Slater proved that fewer than $4m$ edges suffice, while Sethuraman and Ragukumar observed that in practice fewer than $2m$ appear to suffice. We prove the latter bound for every tree. For any root of height $h$ with $t_h$ vertices at maximum distance, we construct a graceful tree containing the original tree with exactly $M=2m-h-t_h+1$ edges; in particular, $2m-\operatorname{diam}(T)$ edges suffice. The construction completes a cyclic reflection of van Bussel's level labeling without increasing its span; each original edge difference $d$ is replaced by $M+1-d$. Unused vertex labels and missing edge differences are indexed by the same intermediate-level positions, allowing an explicit attachment rule that preserves the tree property. The best root for this construction is computable in linear time. Because every graceful supertree labeling restricts to a range-relaxed labeling, a uniform supertree bound of $(2-\varepsilon)m+O(1)$ would imply such a range-relaxed bound for all trees.

papers.title: Threshold existence for random NAE-$k$-SAT and random hypergraph $2$-colourability
papers.abstract: The existence of limiting threshold densities for random hypergraph $2$-colourability and random NAE-$k$-SAT was conjectured in earlier work, including Achlioptas and Moore [RANDOM 2002] and Coja-Oghlan and Panagiotou [STOC 2012]. We prove these conjectures for all $k\geq 3$. We also show that $α^{\mathrm{2-col}}_k \leq α^{\mathrm{NAE}}_k$ for each $k\geq 3$.

papers.title: Heat flow and the fundamental solution of the Baouendi-Grushin operator
papers.abstract: For the Baouendi-Grushin operator $\mathscr L_γ= Δ_x + |x|^{2γ}Δ_y$ in $\R^{m+k}$, with $γ>0$, we prove that the time integral of the heat kernel with pole at the origin equals $C_{γ,Q}\, N_γ^{2-Q}$, where $N_γ$ is the gauge and $Q$ the homogeneous dimension. When $γ\not=1$ no closed form of the heat kernel is known. After a partial Fourier transform in $y$, the time integral of the heat kernel becomes the Green function of an anharmonic oscillator, which solves a generalized modified Bessel equation, and the gauge appears when the inverse Fourier transform is computed as a Hankel transform. In particular, the heat flow provides a new proof that $C_{γ,Q}\, N_γ^{2-Q}$ is a fundamental solution of $-\mathscr L_γ$ with pole at the origin.

papers.title: Optimal Certified Multiple Testing with E-values
papers.abstract: We study randomized multiple testing with e-values under arbitrary dependence and introduce a conditional certification constraint: Given the observed evidence, each coordinate's expected rejection certificate must not exceed its e-value. Existing randomized e-BH improvements satisfy this constraint but have no established optimality guarantee. We prove that the maximum conditional inclusion probability for hypothesis $i$, given e-values~$x$, is $1 \wedge (α/ K) \sum_j \min(x_i, x_j)$, and construct one rule attaining these bounds simultaneously. The rule uses a single independent uniform variable, rejects a prefix of the ordered e-values, and has a unique conditional rejection-set law among rules attaining all the bounds. It therefore maximizes every nonnegative weighted sum of inclusion probabilities, including expected true discoveries under any truth configuration. Under a shared uniform draw, its rejection set contains those of e-BH and U-eBH. The construction extends to BY-calibrated p-values, and simulations under positive and negative dependence show power gains over existing randomized procedures.

papers.title: Theoretical estimation of nonlinear response function and ultrafast optical spectroscopy of nitrogen vacancy centers
papers.abstract: The theoretical description of the ultrafast optical response of nitrogen-vacancy centers has traditionally been developed using the nonlinear response function formalism based on a displaced harmonic oscillator model. However, restrictive defect geometries that lead to rich phonon mode distributions can limit the validity of this model. Here, we extend this framework by incorporating state-dependent oscillator modes characterized by different frequencies. We demonstrate that, as a consequence, the nonlinear response function is modified by a straightforward correction term that can be evaluated using operator algebraic techniques. These modifications directly impact two-dimensional correlation spectroscopy, which serves as a vital characterization tool for color centers by resolving ultrafast correlated electron-vibrational dynamics.

papers.title: Floquet engineering of quantum relaxation
papers.abstract: Dynamical decoupling suppresses decoherence by averaging selected interactions between a quantum system and its environment. Here, we extend this notion through a general Floquet formalism that maps periodic control onto relaxation and dephasing channels. Environmental fluctuations are decomposed into Floquet components that sample the noise spectrum at distinct frequencies, with coupling strengths determined by control-induced Floquet coefficients. We experimentally investigate this approach using a single nitrogen-vacancy center in diamond under multi-pulse control. By tuning the drive and detuning, we reshape the coupling to environmental fluctuations and create isolated operating points where the dominant decoherence channel vanishes, strongly suppressing Floquet dephasing. The resulting coherence enhancement follows the predicted Floquet coupling coefficients and can be shifted by modifying the control sequence. These results establish Floquet driving as a general framework for engineering transverse and longitudinal relaxation through the design of quantum control protocols.

papers.title: The sharp Stein-Tomas inequality on the circle
papers.abstract: We prove that constant functions are global maximizers for the endpoint Stein--Tomas inequality on $\mathbb{S}^1$, thereby determining its sharp constant. By the known characterization of the phases of maximizers, every nonzero maximizer then has the form $f(ω)=c e^{ix_0\cdotω}$, where $c\in\mathbb{C}\setminus\{0\}$ and $x_0\in\mathbb{R}^2$.

papers.title: Optimal lengths of commutators of idempotents and similarity of nilpotent operators to their negatives
papers.abstract: Let $\HH$ be a complex separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space. We prove that every operator in $\BH$ is a sum of three commutators of idempotents and a product of two such commutators. Both numbers are best possible. The same is true for differences of idempotents, for operators similar to their negatives, and for operators anticommuting with an involution. Each of these four classes therefore has additive length three and multiplicative length two. We also construct nilpotent operators of order three that are similar to their negatives but cannot be conjugated to their negatives by any bounded involution. These results answer Question~7.22(a)--(c), the question in Remark~7.17, and the question about involutions in Section~2.9 of Marcoux, Radjavi and Zhang, \emph{J. Funct. Anal.} \textbf{284} (2023), 109854.

papers.title: Hidden selection rules and amplitude ceilings in quantum Fourier models
papers.abstract: Quantum models with Pauli data encodings compute trigonometric polynomials whatever channels, ancillas and outcome-averaged measurements follow, so their expressivity depends on the Fourier coefficients a circuit can reach. We identify two kinds of structure that settle this before training. An antiunitary time-reversal rule and a unitary reflection rule remove frequencies. For gate-level circuits, deciding whether such a rule exists reduces to a linear system over GF(2), solvable in polynomial time, and the time-reversal rule holds in 17.6% of 6,120 configurations of standard templates. Single-upload encodings cap the top coefficient at $2^{-m}$ for every channel, and we compute the tight ceiling for every frequency and a depth-independent re-uploading bound. Frozen before training, these bounds were never violated on a non-linearity benchmark, and they predicted trained performance on real data. On IBM processors the rule held on a 65-qubit chain, and we switched rule-breaking relaxation noise on and off by design.

papers.title: How Does One Cut a 30-60-90 Triangle?
papers.abstract: We enumerate dissections of a 30-60-90 triangle into smaller triangles similar to itself, counting unlabeled arrangements up to similarity and reflection. There are 18 four-piece, 121 five-piece, and 844 six-piece arrangements, corresponding to 11, 47, and 235 distinct multisets of piece areas. We present illustrated catalogs organized by these area multisets and distinguish layouts obtained by subdivision and local rotations or reflections from independent layouts. A separately implemented computational search reproduces every arrangement up to nine pieces, finding 460404 arrangements. Counts through nine pieces for five other classes of triangles are included for comparison.

papers.title: Maximum purity of absolutely separable and absolutely PPT states in qutrit--qudit systems
papers.abstract: A bipartite state is absolutely positive partial transpose (APPT) if it remains PPT under every global unitary transformation, and absolutely separable if it remains separable. For every qutrit--qudit system $\mathbb{C}^3\otimes\mathbb{C}^n$, $n\ge3$, we prove that the maximum purity is the same for absolutely separable and APPT states and equals $\max\{(3n+8)/(3n+2)^2,\,3/(8n)\}$. The maximizing ordered spectrum is unique and contains exactly two distinct eigenvalues: the larger one has multiplicity one for $3\le n\le8$ and multiplicity $n$ for $n\ge9$. We also derive, in terms of the purity, an upper bound on the minimum partial-transpose eigenvalue achievable by global unitary transformations, and characterize all states for which the bound is attained. These results confirm the inscribed-polytope purity conjecture of Ahiable, Kothakonda, and Winter for all qutrit--qudit systems. They also give a lower bound, sharp over explicit purity ranges, on the global depolarizing noise needed for absolute separability or APPT.

papers.title: Two-scale estimates for limit-periodic Schrödinger operators
papers.abstract: We prove strong ballistic transport for one-dimensional continuum Schrödinger operators by comparing the spectral geometry at two consecutive periods. Enlarging a period decomposes each fiber into the eigenspaces of translation by the smaller cell. Away from the larger-period symmetry momenta, a simple ordered band remains in one translation sector and agrees with one translated smaller-period band. This permits us to combine large-period ordering and non-overlap with a smaller-period derivative bound. We obtain lower bounds for folded band widths and confine all near-collisions to a common neighborhood of the symmetry momenta, with the exponential cost at the smaller period. For nested periods $p_n$ with $p_{n+1}/p_n\in\mathbb{N}$ and $p_{n+1}\ge2p_n$, approximation errors $o(p_{n+1}^{-2}e^{-ηp_n})$, where $η>7\sqrt{2R}$ and $\|V\|_\infty\le R$, give a nonzero strong asymptotic velocity on a weighted $H^2$ class containing the Schwartz space. Every position moment of order $0<r\le4$ has two-sided ballistic growth. A period-uniform form estimate, ordered-gap summation, and a linear dynamical comparison complete the argument. No upper bound on successive period ratios is assumed, and the sufficient approximation exponents are not claimed to be optimal.

papers.title: Accelerating posterior sampling in Bayesian inverse problems with diffusion models: an online-offline perspective
papers.abstract: Bayesian inverse problems require both informative prior models and computationally feasible posterior inference. Score-based diffusion models provide expressive learned priors, but their use for inversion introduces a conditioning problem: the score of a noised posterior is generally unavailable from a prior score alone. This selective survey reviews the principal approaches to that problem, including likelihood guidance, spectral and projection methods, sequential Monte Carlo corrections, and amortized conditional training. We organize methods by how they split cost between offline preparation and online inference, and compare their assumptions, advantages and limitations, with emphasis on computational speedups. Some ongoing directions and open questions are gathered at the end.

papers.title: Similarity cancellation and primitive operator roots
papers.abstract: Kaplansky's second test problem for similarity asks whether $A\oplus A\sim B\oplus B$ implies $A\sim B$ for bounded operators on a separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space. We answer this question in the negative, even for compact operators whose singular values satisfy any prescribed positive upper bounds tending to zero. We also show that cancellation can fail under the stronger hypothesis $J_2(T)\sim J_2(S)$ considered by Marcoux, Radjavi, Troscheit, and Zhang \cite{MRTZ}. For these operators, finite amplifications and primitive roots are similar exactly at even multiplicities and even orders, respectively. In contrast, cancellation in fixed matrix size admits a uniform bound on the condition number. This extends the finite type~$I$ results of Jiang, Ma, Shi, and Zhang \cite{JMSZ}. The bound also holds for simultaneous similarity of arbitrary families of matrices and can be chosen to tend to one as the amplified bound tends to one. We conclude that, in a finite type~$I$ von Neumann algebra, cancellation of doubles and cancellation of primitive square roots are each equivalent to boundedness of the orders of its nonzero homogeneous summands.

papers.title: Exponential suppression of bit-flip errors in dissipative cat qubits
papers.abstract: We study the infinite-dimensional Lindblad generator $L_ε=D[a^2-α^2]+εD[a]$, describing a dissipative cat qubit subject to single-photon loss. For sufficiently large $α$ and sufficiently small $ε>0$, we identify a two-dimensional spectral subspace near zero and establish an upper bound on the slow decay rate that decreases exponentially with $α^2$, uniformly in $ε$. This proves exponential suppression of bit-flip errors.

papers.title: Counterexamples to uniqueness for a discrete X-ray transform under quadratic decay
papers.abstract: We show nonuniqueness for a discrete X-ray transform on $\mathbb Z^2$ under quadratic decay. We construct an explicit nonzero function in $\ell^1(\mathbb Z^2)$ with pointwise decay $O(|z|^{-2})$ whose sums over integer lines vanish. We also obtain an infinite-dimensional null space with the same decay assumption. Furthermore, we show a result which indicates that the decay rate $|z|^{-2}$ may be sharp and faster decay may imply uniqueness.

papers.title: Contact multiplicity and a sharp six-map bound for collinear self-similar dendrites
papers.abstract: Let $K\subset\mathbb{C}$ be the attractor of $n\ge2$ similarities $z\mapstoλz+b_k$, $0<|λ|<1$, whose fixed points are evenly spaced on a line, and suppose that $K$ does not lie in a line. We prove that $K$ can be a dendrite only if $n\le6$, and that such dendrites exist for every $2\le n\le6$; no separation or finite-intersection hypothesis is imposed. Hence, for $n\ge7$, every connected $K$ of this kind has interior points or separates the plane. Neighboring pieces of $K$ meet in similar copies of a single contact set. In a dendrite exactly one first-level piece meets this set, whereas for $n\ge7$ at least $n-\lceil2\sqrt{n-1}\rceil\ge2$ do, a bound attained by explicit quadratic parameters. The proof combines a planar translation obstruction for replicated contact arcs with an estimate based on Jensen's formula. After normalizing to $z\mapsto t+z/c$, $t\in\{-n+1,-n+3,\ldots,n-1\}$, the connectedness locus is the closure, outside the unit disk, of the roots of monic integer polynomials of height at most $n-1$. The same estimate shows that, for $n\ge7$, every such polynomial with a non-real root $c$ satisfying $|c|^2\ge\lceil2\sqrt{n-1}\rceil+1$ has subleading coefficient of absolute value at most $\lceil2\sqrt{n-1}\rceil$, and that this bound is sharp. Accordingly, for $n\ge7$, at every non-real boundary point $c$ of the locus with $|c|>1$, each expansion $c=\sum_{j\ge0}d_jc^{-j}$ with integer digits $|d_j|\le n-1$ has $|d_0|\le\lceil2\sqrt{n-1}\rceil$.

papers.title: Minimax estimation of linear functionals in the Darcy inverse problem
papers.abstract: We study estimation of linear functionals $\int fψ$ of the conductivity $f$ in the Darcy problem $\nabla\cdot(f\nabla u)=g$ from observations of $u$ in Gaussian white noise of level $N^{-1/2}$. When the potential has a single nondegenerate minimum, we determine the minimax rates over Sobolev balls in the linearised experiment. Unless a compatibility condition along the gradient flow holds, the rate is governed by an effective dimension $T$ of the Hessian at the minimum, not by the ambient dimension: it is $N^{-(2s+T)/(4s+8)}$ for $T<4$, has an elbow at $T=4$ with an extra logarithmic factor, and is parametric for $T>4$. In the nonlinear experiment we show that these lower bounds persist when compatibility fails at the reference and $T\le4$, and we prove the minimax rate on classes with isotropic critical Hessians, and the parametric rate near references with $T>4$. In dimension at most four, no nonzero linear functional is uniformly $\sqrt N$-estimable on a Sobolev neighbourhood of the constant conductivity, even when it is regular there.

papers.title: Sharp Critical Rates for Locally Private Distribution Estimation
papers.abstract: We determine sharp minimax rates for distribution estimation under pure local differential privacy at critical query smoothness. For the integral probability metric generated by the unit ball of $B^d_{2,q}$, $1\le q\le\infty$, over fixed periodic Sobolev density balls with positive smoothness and interior slack at the uniform density, the expected risk is of order $N^{-1/2}(\log N)^{3/2-1/q}$, where $N=n\varepsilon^2$; expected squared risk has the squared order. The fine index governs aggregation across resolutions that share one private information budget. A single noninteractive release with a measurable proper density output attains these rates, and matching lower bounds allow finite public blackboard interaction and repeated participation under each user's total privacy budget. A known $L^2$ radius permits the same rates without using density smoothness, with output in the $L^2$ density ball. Separately, for positive smooth densities on $[0,1]$, integrated squared CDF risk has minimax order $(\log N)^2/N$, with sharp quantile, Wasserstein, and transport map consequences. The rates hold uniformly for $0<\varepsilon\le1$ as $N\to\infty$, with class parameters fixed.

papers.title: Model-Based Fast Calibration for a Nitrogen Vacancy Center QPU
papers.abstract: We present a simulation-informed calibration workflow for NV quantum processing units that combines a digital twin, optimal control pulses, and a Fisher-information-guided experiment design into an iterative parameter estimation feedback loop. We find that using this framework, we obtain the same calibration precision as standard techniques with up to 4x reduction in measurement time.

papers.title: Small-LCM Distinct Covering Systems via Segmented Local Search
papers.abstract: We construct distinct covering systems with minimum moduli 8, 9, 10, 11 and least common multiples 20160, 75600, 302400, 3326400, respectively, and conjecture that these values are minimal. For minimum modulus 8, the exclusion computations leave only 10080 and 15120 unresolved below our construction. The constructions use segmented local search: moduli are introduced in increasing blocks, followed by joint reoptimization of selected blocks. We give complete residue lists and an independent integer-arithmetic verifier. Two computational studies, comprising 180 initial runs and 130 follow-up runs, compare initialization orders, revisit rules and seed-bank capacities under fixed scan limits.

papers.title: The Prodigal Elephant Returns: Last-Return Laws in the Superdiffusive Regime
papers.abstract: Let $(S_n)$ be the one-dimensional elephant random walk with memory parameter $p\in(3/4,1)$ and first-step probability $q=\mathbb{P}(S_1=1)\in[0,1]$. Set $a=2p-1$, and let $f_{q,a}$ denote the density of the almost-sure limit of $S_n/n^a$. We prove that the last return time $T_0=\sup\{m\geq0:S_m=0\}$ satisfies: $\mathbb{P}(T_0\geq n)\sim f_{q,a}(0)\sqrt{\frac{8}{π(2a-1)}}n^{-(a-1/2)}$. Reflection gives $f_{q,a}(0)=f_{1,a}(0)$, so the constant is independent of $q$. For future walks started from admissible states $(n,x_n)$ with $x_n/\sqrt n\to z$, we establish functional convergence of the centered martingale-normalized paths to a time-changed Brownian motion. Uniform control of late hitting times then gives the eventual-return kernel $2Φ(-\sqrt{2a-1}|z|)$, uniformly on bounded scaled windows, where $Φ$ is the standard normal distribution function. The same last-visit asymptotic holds uniformly for nonempty deterministic targets $F_n\subseteq[-r_n,r_n]\cap\mathbb{Z}$, $r_n=o(\sqrt n)$, held fixed during each trajectory. Conditionally on $T_0\geq n$, we identify the joint limit of $S_n/\sqrt n$, the next return divided by $n$, and the last return divided by the next return. The last ratio converges to $A^{-1/(2a-1)}$, independently of the other two limiting coordinates, where $A$ has the arcsine distribution on $(0,1)$.

papers.title: Artinian reduction applied to the Largest Intersection Problem
papers.abstract: Suppose we have $r$ hypersurfaces in $\mathbb{P}^m$ of degree $d$, whose defining polynomials are linearly independent and whose intersection is zero-dimensional. What is the maximum number of points in their intersection? This problem is motivated by computing the generalized Hamming weights of projective Reed-Muller codes, and a conjectured formula for this maximum was given in [21]. We prove the conjectured formula for arbitrary $m$ when $\binom{m+d}{d}-\binom{d+2}{2}<r\leq\binom{m+d}{d}$. We use the notion of Artinian reduction to reformulate the problem in terms of graded Artinian algebras and then apply combinatorial tools to bound their Hilbert functions.

papers.title: Mixed-Integer Programming for Causal Discovery with Unknown Hard-Intervention Targets
papers.abstract: When intervention targets are uncertain, learning causal relationships and identifying directly perturbed variables become a joint task. We develop an exact mixed-integer program based on optimized parent-set scores (PS-MIP) for joint graph and intervention-target estimation in linear Gaussian structural equation models under stochastic hard interventions. The method can incorporate candidate-edge restrictions and partial target knowledge when available. For each random variable, PS-MIP evaluates candidate sets of direct causes, or parent sets, by optimizing the likelihood parameters and compatible target patterns, retaining both the score and a minimizing target pattern. A global mixed-integer program then selects parent sets subject to acyclicity. Under stated conditions, this reduction preserves the joint objective and reconstructs the graph, targets, and likelihood parameters. Because the local scores are precomputed, PS-MIP replaces a direct large bilinear mixed-integer program with a linear selection problem; empirically it certifies global optimality on far more instances than the direct formulation (126 of 180 versus 34) and is often orders of magnitude faster. On synthetic data, PS-MIP achieves favorable false-discovery--true-discovery trade-offs relative to several benchmark algorithms for causal discovery with unknown intervention targets, along with strong intervention-target recovery in denser settings. An exploratory study on real data from a controlled physical system further demonstrates recovery beyond simulation.

papers.title: Singular Perturbations for Control Systems Safety
papers.abstract: Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) offer a powerful theory for enforcing safety in dynamical systems. Yet, applying this framework to complex systems is challenging when subsystems are feedback-interconnected and operate at different timescales. Such structures arise naturally in multiphysics systems and in control architectures where physical plants interact with optimization, estimation, and control algorithms. In many of these settings, safety involves only part of the system, motivating the design of reduced-order certificates. Inspired by singular perturbation theory, we establish sufficient conditions, involving separation between slow and fast dynamics, under which a reduced-order safety certificate can be lifted to the full interconnected system. Specifically, we construct a composite CBF ensuring forward invariance of a lifted subset of the original safe set. We also show that the certified safe set expands monotonically as the tuning parameter accelerating the fast dynamics is reduced. Numerical results validate the approach on two robotic systems: a planar 2-DoF manipulator with motor dynamics and a 6-DoF UR10e manipulator controlled by a suboptimal optimization algorithm.

papers.title: Gromov-Witten theory of the local model of the standard flop
papers.abstract: We conjecture that the generating series of equivariant Gromov-Witten invariants of the local Calabi-Yau $(2n-1)$-fold $\operatorname{Tot} \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{n-1}} (-1)^{\oplus n}$ at fixed genus can be presented as a linear combination of polylogarithms, generalising a well-known property of the resolved conifold. We prove this conjecture for two specialisations of the equivariant parameters. In the first, the parameters are specialised to roots of unity and the proof proceeds via Givental-Teleman reconstruction. In the second, we obtain a closed-form evaluation of the generating series from which the conjecture follows. For $n=3$, the resulting closed formula establishes a special case of a Gopakumar-Vafa-type conjecture for Calabi-Yau fivefolds.

papers.title: Clique counts under degree and matching constraints
papers.abstract: We study the maximum number of $t$-cliques in graphs with maximum degree at most $D$ and matching number at most $M$, with no restriction on the number of vertices. For $t\ge 3$, we determine this maximum whenever $D\ge 2M-1$ and characterize all extremal graphs when the maximum is positive. Up to isolated vertices, these are complete or complete split graphs for $D\ge 2M$, while $K_{2M}$ is uniquely extremal when $D=2M-1$. We also derive a general upper bound from the Chvátal-Hanson edge theorem and refine it for even $D$. For fixed even $D$ and $3\le t\le D+1$, every extremal graph consists, apart from isolated vertices, of copies of $K_{D+1}$ together with a remainder whose order is bounded independently of $M$. When $D/2$ divides $M$, this remainder is empty and the extremal graph is unique. This structure yields an eventual recurrence, reducing the determination of all extremal values and graphs to finitely many matching bounds.

papers.title: $a$-contraction applied to the time-asymptotic stability of weak shocks for a general 1-D viscous system
papers.abstract: The method of $a$-contraction with shifts builds on the relative entropy method of Dafermos and DiPerna and allows both viscous shocks and rarefaction waves to be studied directly at the level of the solution. This unified framework led to the resolution of Matsumura's long-standing conjecture on the time-asymptotic stability of a viscous shock in composition with a rarefaction. Kang, Vasseur, and Wang established this stability for the one-dimensional compressible barotropic Navier-Stokes system. Their result was subsequently extended to composite planar waves for general $n\times n$ viscous systems in arbitrary spatial dimensions. The present paper is a companion to that work. Here we prove the estimates on viscous shock profiles needed to apply $a$-contraction with shifts, including derivative estimates that go beyond the standard bounds. We also give a streamlined account of the main ideas of the method by focusing on a single viscous shock for a general one-dimensional system.

papers.title: Entropic Column Generation and Lehmer Branch-and-Price for Bin Packing Problem
papers.abstract: We introduce Lehmer branch-and-price, an exact algorithm for bin packing and cutting stock problems built on the Lehmer transform, the ratio of Mellin transforms of item weights at consecutive orders. The transform maps each bin, a finite multiset of item weights, to a smooth increasing curve, and so gives the discrete problem a continuous representation on which the tools of analysis, such as convexity, exponential families and smoothing, can act. Read along this curve, the problem yields an explicit dual solution, a monotone representation of the dominance order, a family of constructive heuristics with first fit decreasing as its limit, and an integer identity that tells when the linear relaxation can decide an instance and when only a perfect packing can improve the best solution known. Lifted from items to patterns, the transform gives entropic column generation, a new form of column generation that bounds the relaxation from both sides at every iteration without solving the pricing problem exactly, maximizes a smoothed dual at an explicit rate, and measures by an entropy how much the relaxation leaves undecided. We show that the proposed algorithm outperforms the state-of-the-art methods on the standard benchmark in both the number of instances solved and the computational time.

papers.title: Chaos, Fractals, and Ergodicity in Nonlinear Quantum Protocols
papers.abstract: Iterated nonlinear quantum protocols provide a straightforward way of realizing nonlinear dynamics in quantum systems through measurement and postselection. We investigate a family of protocols in which the order of the induced nonlinearity is controlled by the number of qubits involved in a single step. By examining the resulting rational maps and applying a set of numerical diagnostics, we identify extended parameter regions that exhibit ergodic-like dynamics for protocol orders $n=3,4,$ and $5$. We further characterize the associated chaotic behavior through the distribution of Lyapunov exponents. Our results show that ergodic-like dynamics persists beyond the quadratic case, while the geometry of the corresponding parameter regions and the typical degree of chaoticity depend strongly on the order of the nonlinear transformation.

papers.title: Modular proof analysis and cut elimination for the Reflection Calculi $\mathsf{RC}_1$ and $\mathsf{QRC}_1$
papers.abstract: The reflection calculus with one modality is denoted by $\mathsf{RC}_1$ and its quantified generalization is known as $\mathsf{QRC}_1$. These decidable calculi are of interest since they generate the strictly positive fragments of the (quantified) provability logic for theories like Peano Arithmetic and Heyting Arithmetic. We introduce analytic cut-free calculi ${\mathrm{GRC1}}$ and ${\mathrm{GQRC1}}$ for $\mathsf{RC}_1$ and $\mathsf{QRC}_1$ respectively. The new calculi derive sequents of the form $A\Longrightarrow B$ with $A,B$ strictly positive formulas. In particular, the new calculi do not use (multi)sets nor nested sequents. For both ${\mathrm{GRC1}}$ and ${\mathrm{GQRC1}}$ it is shown that the cut-rule is admissible. As a consequence, it is proven that the calculi are deductively equivalent to $\mathsf{RC}_1$ and $\mathsf{QRC}_1$ respectively. The cutfree systems are used to prove uniform interpolation for the two reflection calculi. In addition, ${\mathrm{GRC1}}$ is used to give a syntactic proof of Dashkov's Theorem to the extent that $\mathsf{RC}_1$ is the strictly positive fragment of the provability logic ${\mathsf{GL}}$. The paper also introduces non-analytic calculi that are conceptually easier but proof-theoretically behave badly. It is shown that even those systems allow direct cut-elimination: the benefits of the strict positivity outweigh the draw-backs of a non-analytic calculus in these cases.

papers.title: When Pedal Shapes Come Back: a Complex Story
papers.abstract: Under the usual nondegeneracy assumptions, repeatedly projecting a fixed point onto the side lines of an $n$-gon returns its shape after $n$ steps. We explain this classical theorem through a short complex-number identity: the multipliers of one step move cyclically around the polygon. The same calculation allows a different common angle of projection at each step. A sharp angle-dependent contraction bound identifies the incircle centre as the maximiser for tangential polygons. In space, even a regular tetrahedron can fail to recover its shape after four steps. We give an exact example, then show how concentric inscribed and circumscribed spheres restore a two-step return. Rectangular boxes provide a further four-step family.

papers.title: Resonance varieties of Schubert arrangements
papers.abstract: We compute the resonance varieties of the Orlik--Solomon algebras of Schubert matroids. Previously known results have been largely confined to matroids of rank $3$, and the Schubert matroids give a family of nontrivial examples of arbitrary rank. We give an expression for the cohomology of the Orlik--Solomon algebra that we show holds for Schubert matroids as well as for simple, complex-realizable rank-$3$ matroids that do not support multinets. Our proof introduces a family of matroids for which the Orlik--Solomon algebra is isomorphic to an exterior Stanley--Reisner algebra.

papers.title: Varieties of associative algebras with slow central codimension growth
papers.abstract: Central codimensions measure the dimensions of spaces of multilinear polynomials modulo those taking values in the center of an algebra. We classify associative algebras over a field of characteristic zero whose central codimensions grow at most linearly. The classification is given up to equality of polynomial identities, in terms of explicit generating algebras and an equivalent finite exclusion criterion. We also give a direct structural characterization of the bounded case. As a consequence, we determine the five varieties of quadratic central codimension growth whose proper subvarieties all have at most linear central growth. As an application of the bounded-growth classification, we characterize algebras graded by an arbitrary finite group whose graded central codimensions are bounded. Up to graded PI-equivalence, these are direct sums of commutative and nilpotent graded algebras, possibly together with the Grassmann algebra on two generators endowed with the trivial grading.

papers.title: Halving Partitions and Hyperbinary Expansions
papers.abstract: Starting from a positive integer, repeatedly halve the current value, rounding up or down. Which resulting sequences have terms that add to the starting integer? A simple balance identity turns the rounding choices into hyperbinary expansions, in which each power of two occurs at most twice. This correspondence gives exact counts by length and an injection into the expansions counted by Stern's diatomic sequence. We characterize equality in the resulting bound by the binary digits of the odd part of the integer. We also determine the unique longest partition and give a short recursive counting algorithm. When the required total is allowed to vary, the chain counts eventually equal Stern's number, and we determine the exact threshold. A direct proof shows that the counts of hyperbinary expansions in the three length classes modulo three differ by at most one. For sufficiently long halving partitions, the counts by length first weakly increase and then weakly decrease, although the full sequence need not do so.

papers.title: Linear maps preserving the Cullis' determinant. III
papers.abstract: This paper is the third in the series of papers devoted to the explicit description of linear maps preserving the Cullis' determinant of rectangular matrices of size $n\times k$ with entries belonging to an arbitrary ground field which is large enough. In this part we study the remaining case where $k = 3$ and $n \ge k + 2 = 5$ and prove that every linear map preserving the Cullis' determinant admits the same description as for the case where $k \ge 4$ and $n \ge k + 2$ obtained previously.

papers.title: Representability of Graphical Symplectic Matroids
papers.abstract: Chow associated with every finite multigraph $G$ a symplectic matroid $\GraphS{G}$ on the signed edge set $E\sqcup E^{*}$, whose restrictions to transversals are frame matroids of signed graphs, and Sarvepalli asked which of these matroids are representable. For a connected graph containing a cycle, we show that every isotropic representation of $S(G)$ admits an incidence-flow normal form. The remaining representation conditions are expressed through its admissible minors. Consequently, if $\GraphS{G}$ is $\F$-representable, then the bridgeless part of $G$ has a nowhere-zero $(\F,+)$-flow. In characteristic other than two, $\GraphS{G}$ is representable if and only if every non-loop edge on a cycle has a parallel mate. In characteristic two, we characterize the loopless graphs without two vertex-disjoint cycles by the existence of a nowhere-zero $(\F,+)$-flow, and we show that rigidly linked short cycles, and hence subdivisions of the prism, are obstructions. For $3$-connected simple graphs this gives a complete answer: $\GraphS{G}$ is $\F$-representable if and only if $\F$ has characteristic two, $G$ has no two vertex-disjoint cycles, and either $|\F|>2$ or $G\cong K_5$. In particular, the matroid of the Petersen graph is representable over no field. Finally, the admissible corank--nullity polynomial of an arbitrary symplectic matroid is intrinsic and satisfies a three-term contraction identity. For graphical symplectic matroids, this becomes a deletion-contraction recursion that closes up once marked vertices are allowed, and polynomials built from enveloping matroids agree with it exactly for sheltering envelopes.

papers.title: Persistence of Fractal Structures in Iterated Quantum Protocols: Robustness to Preparation and Gate Errors
papers.abstract: Repeatedly combining entangling gates on an ensemble of qubits with measurement and postselection on a part of them induces a nonlinear evolution of the unmeasured qubits' state, whose fractal convergence boundaries make the outcome sensitive to the initial state. We study a family of iterated protocols in which $n$ identical qubits are coupled by CNOT gates, $n-1$ of them are postselected, and a parametrized single-qubit unitary acts on the survivor. For orders $n=2$ to $5$, we map the box-counting dimension of the pure-state Julia sets over the complex parameter plane and identify the symmetries that constrain it. Allowing mixed initial states, we find that moderate preparation noise preserves the main parameter-dependent trends of the boundary dimension over much of the studied range, and that the three-dimensional quasi-Julia boundary in the Bloch ball has a dimension that is approximately equal to the dimension of the pure-state Julia set plus one. We further model gate imperfections by an effective depolarizing channel and by fixed coherent interactions. Weak errors leave the estimated dimensions consistent with their ideal values even where the convergence regions visibly deform, and $ZZ$ errors are shown to be exactly conjugate to the ideal protocol at a rotated parameter. Finally, we analyze the postselection and storage cost of an implementation and propose a diagnostic test combining conditional fidelity with acceptance statistics, which we demonstrate on IQM Emerald and Rigetti Cepheus-1-108Q.

papers.title: How Much Can Approximate Equilibria Change the Social Cost of Selfish Routing?
papers.abstract: We study approximate Nash equilibria in nonatomic congestion games, with the goal of understanding how much the social cost can change when the equilibrium condition is relaxed. We consider $ε$-approximate Nash equilibria ($ε$-NE), in which each player uses a strategy whose cost is at most $1 + ε$ times the minimum available cost. We compare the social costs of $ε$-NE and exact Nash equilibria. This lets us quantify, for example, how much a navigation app can reduce total travel time when drivers tolerate routes slightly slower than the fastest available route. For degree-$d$ polynomial latencies in both general nonatomic congestion games and single-commodity routing games on series-parallel networks, we give tight lower and upper bounds on the relative change in social cost from an exact Nash equilibrium to any $ε$-NE, with matching instances for every $ε$. For small $ε$, the largest possible relative reduction and increase in general congestion games are both $Θ(\sqrt{dε})$, independently of the number of resources and populations. In contrast, on series-parallel networks of depth $h$, the largest possible relative reduction is $Θ(hε)$, while the largest possible relative increase is known to be $ε$.
