papers.abstract: For an integer $k\ge 2$ and $r^2>2(2k-1)\ln (2k-1)$, we construct a bipartite graph $G$ whose two vertex classes are disjoint copies of the family of all $k$-subsets of a $(2k-1)$-element set, two vertices being adjacent when their sets intersect in at most $r$ elements. Assigning each vertex its corresponding subset as its color list, $G$ is not colorable, and thus its choice number $\ch(G)\ge k+1$. This implies that there are graphs with maximum degree $Δ$ and $$\ch(G)\ge\Bigl(\frac1{32}-o(1)\Bigr)\frac{(\lnΔ)^2}{(\ln\lnΔ)^3}.$$ When $k\to\infty$, consequently $\ch(G)/\lnΔ$ tends to infinity, which disproves the Alon--Krivelevich conjecture. In order to show the uncolorability, we use tools from probability (conditional product measure, nested coupling, and Doob martingale), which we write in an elementary language of weighted counting, and topology (Brouwer fixed-point theorem).

papers.title: Mean curvature bounds for CMC foliations of manifolds with sectional curvature bounded below
papers.abstract: Let $M^{n+1}$ be a complete Riemannian manifold with $\sec_M\ge-K_0$, $K_0\ge0$, and let $\mathfrak{F}$ be a codimension one foliation of $M$ by hypersurfaces of constant mean curvature, the constant depending on the leaf. We prove that the mean curvature of every leaf satisfies $|H|\le(n+1)\sqrt{K_0}$. In particular, the mean curvature of the leaves of a CMC foliation of a complete manifold with $|\sec_M|\le1$ is bounded by $n+1$, which answers positively a conjecture of Meeks III, Pérez, and Ros.

papers.title: Landscape Intervals: A Geometric Framework for Multiparameter Persistence Landscapes
papers.abstract: Classical persistent homology provides a summary of the multiscale topology of a filtration of a space. These summaries are not naturally valued in a vector space, limiting their direct use in standard machine learning pipelines. To address this issue, Bubenik introduced persistence landscapes, vector-valued invariants of persistence modules, which operate by conveniently encoding the behavior of rank functions of modules along the parameter axis. When passing to multiparameter persistent homology, changes in the rank functions vary by different amounts in different directions. In this paper, we introduce the landscape interval, a subset of the parameter space of a multiparameter persistence module which records changes in the rank function in all directions simultaneously. This geometric perspective leads to two novel invariants which serve as notions of persistence landscapes for multiparameter modules. We show that our invariants generalize existing landscape-type invariants: in particular, they recover Bubenik's landscapes in the one-parameter setting and allow us to obtain the multiparameter landscapes introduced by Vipond. For our main theoretical contributions, we establish two exact identities connecting landscapes with erosion distances, prove that our invariants are stable under perturbations, and refine the interleaving-stability bounds for the existing landscape-type invariants. We also show that on a certain class of multiparameter persistence modules, the full invariants can be recovered from finite information about the module. On the practical side, we introduce a robust numerical framework for extracting our invariants from real data and for incorporating them into standard machine learning pipelines. The framework is illustrated on surface mesh and medical image data.

papers.title: Delocalized region of bipartite Erdős-Rényi graphs
papers.abstract: We consider bipartite Erdős-Rényi graphs $\mathbb{G}(n, p, d/\sqrt{np})$ with two parts of sizes $n$ and $p$, respectively, and edge probability $d/\sqrt{pn}$. We show that for $d > b_* \log (n+p)$ all eigenvectors of its adjacency matrix, with eigenvalues away from zero, are delocalized with high probability. The threshold $b_*$ is an explicit function of the size ratio $n/p$ and optimal for eigenvector delocalization near the spectral edges. Our results extend to bulk eigenvectors down to the optimal threshold $d\geq \mathcal{D}\sqrt{\log (n+p)}$ for a constant $\mathcal D \geq 1$. In the supercritical scale $d \gg \log (n+p)$ we show that all eigenvectors are delocalized. Our results also hold for sparse rectangular random matrices with independent entries.

papers.title: Dirichlet form approach to stochastic thin-film equations
papers.abstract: The thin-film equation describes the evolution of a thin liquid film driven by capillarity and limited by viscosity. For sufficiently small film heights, thermal fluctuations may not be neglected. Since the thin-film equation as an overdamped evolution equation has a gradient flow structure, the informal implementation of the fluctuation-dissipation principle is straightforward. In this paper, we work out that the concept of Dirichlet forms and the related construction of Markov processes are tailor-made for this type of overdamped continuum evolution with thermal noise. However, the concept of Dirichlet forms relies on the availability of a Gibbsian equilibrium measure, which, in case of the thin-film equation, limits the treatment to the $(1+1)$-dimensional case. By means of Dirichlet form theory, we obtain the existence and uniqueness of the evolution of laws on configuration space. We show that the regularity of the realizations of this Markov process matches the heuristics. In a simplified situation with a Gaussian reference measure and a non-degenerate mobility function, we characterize it as what is called an energy solution. The latter provides a pathwise decomposition of the driving forces into a deterministic and a thermal one, which was the starting point. Applying the same techniques in the spatially discretized setting proposed in [Math. Comp. 92 (2023), 1931--1976], we obtain the same results uniformly in the discretization parameter. In particular, Galerkin as well as spectral approximations of the stochastic thin-film equation are shown to be uniformly tight in optimal topologies. In the simplified setting, we also prove Mosco convergence of the associated Dirichlet forms and thereby obtain convergence of these approximations.

papers.title: Cost-Aware Stopping for Freeze-Thaw Bayesian Optimization: When Does One-Step Lookahead Suffice?
papers.abstract: Freeze-thaw Bayesian optimization (BO) evaluates candidates in resumable increments but usually stops at a budget or convergence test. We maximize a budget-free utility, the best observed score minus a cost per increment, with a one-step lookahead: advance the candidate with the largest expected improvement (EI) under a fixed surrogate, and stop once no EI exceeds the cost. This rule, EI stopping, never falls below stopping immediately in expected utility, yet it can stop too early. We construct a certificate, a lower bound on the value of two-step lookahead, that proves such a stop premature, and repeating this correction never lowers expected utility under the surrogate. Under the surrogate, EI stops are premature on average at low costs and lose little at high costs. On three hyperparameter optimization benchmarks, a pre-registered test finds EI stopping noninferior to the correction in most high-cost settings, while the correction gains at low costs on two of the three; more information sharing in the surrogate raises EI stopping's utility. On the surrogates of two published methods, EI stopping trades lower scores for fewer training increments. EI stopping is a simple cost-aware reference whose utility depends on the surrogate.

papers.title: Nonlinear stability of Schwarzschild black holes for the Einstein-massless Dirac system in spherical symmetry
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish the nonlinear stability of the Schwarzschild exterior for the spherically symmetric Einstein-massless Dirac system. More precisely, we consider sufficiently small perturbations of Schwarzschild characteristic initial data and prove that the corresponding maximal development remains globally controlled in the exterior region (orbital stability), and converges, in a suitable teleological double-null gauge, to a Schwarzschild spacetime with a final mass (asymptotic stability). In particular, the maximal future development contains a complete future null infinity and a regular event horizon, with a nonempty black hole region in its interior. The main difficulties in the proof arise from the delicate coupling between the Dirac operator and the geometry, compared with the scalar wave counterpart, as well as from the failure of the Dirac stress-energy tensor to satisfy a positive energy condition. To overcome these difficulties, we rely on a bootstrap argument coupling the geometry and the Dirac field. Working in suitable teleological double-null gauges adapted to the asymptotic null boundaries, we establish weighted energy estimates combining integrated local energy decay, red-shift estimates near the event horizon, and an rp-estimates towards null infinity. A core ingredient is the use of suitable reweightings of the spinor components, which allow us to close these estimates despite the nonlinear coupling to the geometry.

papers.title: Long-time stochasticity for periodic iterations of random surface maps
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a closed Riemannian surface, and let $f_1,\ldots,f_s$ be area-preserving $C^2$ diffeomorphisms with fixed positive probabilities such that the resulting random dynamical system is uniformly expanding on average. For each $n$, choose $ω_1,\ldots,ω_n$ independently according to these probabilities and set $F=f_{ω_n}\circ\cdots\circ f_{ω_1}$. We prove that there exists $α>0$ such that, with probability at least $1-e^{-αn}$, the correlations of any two Hölder observables $φ,ψ$ under $F^m$ are bounded by $e^{-αn}\|φ\|_{C^β}\|ψ\|_{C^β}$, for all $m\leq e^{αn}$. These estimates imply a law of large numbers and a central limit theorem for the Birkhoff sums along $F$ of any zero-mean Hölder observable $φ$, for exponentially long times in $n$. The limiting Gaussian has variance $\int_Mφ^2\,d\mathrm{vol}$.

papers.title: Relative homological algebra of filter modules
papers.abstract: Over an arbitrary ordered set we consider the class of filter modules, i.e. indicator modules of filters in the ordered set. We show that the induced exact structure of filter modules, the so-called filter exact structure, which has filter modules as relative projective modules, admits an explicit projectivization by the distributive lattice of filters. This allows the reduction of the projective-homological properties of the induced exact structure to the standard homological algebra of $k{\operatorname{Fil}(Q)}$, the incidence algebra of $k$-representations on the lattice of filters. In the case of finite join-semilattices, we leverage the combinatorial structure of the distributive lattice of filters to determine the standard global dimension of $k{\operatorname{Fil}(Q)}$. By virtue of projectivization we provide lower and upper bounds for the global dimension of the filter exact structure. Moreover, we call an ordered set filter-tiny if its relative injective modules one-to-one-correspond to the standard injective modules. We exploit relative derived functors to show that filter-tiny ordered sets do not admit relative injective prehulls if the relative global dimension is larger than 1. It is open to which classes of ordered sets $Q$ the filter-tininess condition applies, and what the relative injective modules are in the case of non-filter-tiny ordered sets.

papers.title: Holonomies of hyperbolic surfaces with one branch point
papers.abstract: Let $S$ be a closed oriented surface of genus $g\geq 2$. We prove that any representation of $π_1(S)$ into $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ with Euler class $3-2g$ is the holonomy of a hyperbolic metric on $S$ with one simple branch point.

papers.title: Polynomial-Time Algorithms for Links
papers.abstract: Every link in the \(3\)-sphere admits a generalised \(T\)-link presentation. In this paper, we give an explicit polynomial-time algorithm which, given a signed Artin braid word and the number of strands, computes such a presentation. Combining this construction with Yamada--Vogel braiding gives a polynomial-time conversion from arbitrary oriented combinatorial link diagrams to generalised \(T\)-link parameters. We prove polynomial bounds on the number of strands and crossings in the resulting braid. As an application, we prove that a link property or a link invariant is computable in polynomial time from diagrams if and only if the corresponding problem is solvable in polynomial time from generalised \(T\)-link parameters, with parameter input measured by the total number of strands and crossings in the corresponding braid diagram. Whenever a classification criterion or an explicit invariant formula is available in these parameters, it can be applied to the original link by substituting the parameters obtained from the diagram. A polynomial-time test or evaluation then gives a polynomial-time procedure on diagrams. We also establish the corresponding transfer for approximating real-valued invariants to prescribed accuracy.

papers.title: Constructing Lagrangian surfaces in all symplectic toric $4$-manifolds from multi-grid diagrams
papers.abstract: We present a new diagrammatic construction of Lagrangian surfaces in all symplectic toric $4$-manifolds from objects called multi-grid diagrams. These are a generalisation of triple grid diagrams for Lagrangian surfaces in $\mathbb{CP}^2$ wherein the underlying trisection is replaced by the more general notion of a toric decomposition. We give examples of multi-grid diagrams for Lagrangian surfaces in a range of symplectic toric $4$-manifolds, including Evans' recent non-squeezable Klein bottle in $S^2 \times S^2$.

papers.title: Spectra of stochastic matrices with a Toeplitz interior
papers.abstract: For stochastic matrices of order $n$, the Karpelevič region is the set of all possible eigenvalues. We study matrices whose first and last $m$ rows are arbitrary probability vectors, while the remaining middle rows come from one probability vector by successive cyclic shifts to the right, moving the last entry to the first position each time. As $m$ increases, their eigenvalue regions expand from the polygon spanned by the $n$th roots of unity. For $n\ge3$, they first equal the full Karpelevič region at $m=\lceil(n-1)/4\rceil$. Reproducing all $n$ eigenvalues, counted with multiplicity, of every stochastic matrix of the same order requires $m=\lfloor n/2\rfloor$. Thus, in even order $n\ge4$, retaining two consecutive rows with the Toeplitz pattern can exclude eigenvalue lists even when every possible eigenvalue occurs individually. The boundary of the Karpelevič region consists of arcs joining roots of unity. We determine the least $m$ for which every point of each arc occurs as an eigenvalue in our family. For arcs whose nonreal points first become possible eigenvalues at order $n\ge4$, and for $m\ge1$ below this minimum, no point on the arc other than its endpoints occurs in the family. At the minimum, every point on the arc becomes attainable. At the smallest order $n\ge4$ at which a nonreal point on a boundary arc away from its endpoints can occur as an eigenvalue, that point determines the characteristic polynomial of every stochastic matrix of order $n$ having it as an eigenvalue. Further results describe the smaller regions and the angles at which their boundaries approach roots of unity.

papers.title: Stochastic Rayleigh-Ritz Ascent: Global Linear Convergence under a Spectral Gap
papers.abstract: We consider the adjoint-free random-plane iteration algorithm for finding the top eigenvector of a matrix proposed in (SIAM J. Matrix Anal. Appl. 47 (2026), 1349-1374). Unlike standard methods such as the power method or gradient descent, the above algorithm lacked linear convergence guarantees in the presence of a spectral gap. In this paper, we establish explicit spectral-gap-dependent global linear convergence rates in expectation, providing quantitative guarantees for the empirically observed convergence.

papers.title: Lane-Emden equation for the superposition of a local and nonlocal operator with the "wrong sign"
papers.abstract: We consider the Lane-Emden equation associated with the operator $-Δ- γ\, (-Δ)^s$ (for positive $γ$). First we consider the equation in the entire space and we prove that no Serrin-type critical exponent arises in the $H^1(\mathbb R^n)$ framework. Secondly we consider the problem settled in an open, bounded and connected set and we prove the existence of a positive solution for sufficiently small $s$.

papers.title: The Quartic Gap Between Quantum and Dequantized Algorithms for Linear Algebra Is Tight
papers.abstract: Quantum algorithms for linear algebra that access a matrix $A$ through quantum random access memory (QRAM) prepare quantum states proportional to the solutions of linear systems and related problems. Dequantized classical algorithms, when given sampling and query access to $A$, return sampling and query access to an approximate solution. Both kinds of algorithms use a number of queries that is polynomial in the normalized Frobenius norm $ρ=\|A\|_F/\|A\|$ and does not directly depend on the dimension. For linear systems at fixed condition number and accuracy, quantum algorithms use $\widetilde O(ρ)$ queries, whereas the best dequantized algorithms use $\widetilde O(ρ^4)$. We prove that this quartic gap is tight in the worst case, up to a logarithmic factor. For every constant $κ_0>1$, we construct dense linear systems with condition number at most $κ_0$ for which sampling from the solution within a sufficiently small constant total variation distance requires $Ω(ρ^4/\logρ)$ classical queries but only $Θ(ρ)$ quantum queries. The same separation holds, for errors below smaller thresholds, for positive-definite systems, least squares, ridge regression, matrix powers and square roots, imaginary-time and real-time Hamiltonian evolution, and sampling from the top principal component. Our results therefore show that many quantum algorithms for linear algebra, achieve a near-quartic speedup in the worst case, over classical algorithms with sampling and query access. All of these classical lower bounds follow from the same framework, which is based on a lower bound for sampling from distributions that depend on a fixed set of Fourier coefficients of an unknown Boolean function.

papers.title: Two choices suffice: $k$-out sampling leaves $O(n/k)$ intercomponent edges for $k\geq 2$
papers.abstract: Given a simple undirected graph on $n$ vertices, random $k$-out sampling forms a spanning subgraph by having each vertex independently choose $k$ incident edges uniformly with replacement. We prove that, for every integer $k\geq2$, the expected number of original edges joining distinct sampled components is $O(n/k)$. This resolves the conjecture of Holm, King, Thorup, Zamir, and Zwick in its full range, improving their logarithmic sampling requirement to the optimal threshold of two choices per vertex. The bound fails for $k=1$, and the dependence $O(n/k)$ is tight up to constant factors. Our result holds with replacement and consequently also without replacement. In particular, this implies that contracting just two independent local choices per vertex suffices to reduce an arbitrary simple graph to a quotient with $O(n)$ edges in expectation, which is crucial in reducing the instance size for many contraction-based algorithms. Our proof uses switching arguments to relate intercomponent edges to bridges and a degree-weighted component potential, whose expectation we also bound with a switching argument.

papers.title: Asymmetric $L^p$-improving and maximal estimates for the triangle averaging operator
papers.abstract: Let $d\ge2$ and $t>0$. We study the bilinear triangle averaging operator $$\mathcal T_t(f,g)(x)=\int_{\mathcal I}f(x-ty)g(x-tz) dσ(y,z),$$ where $σ$ is the normalized surface measure on the manifold $\mathcal I=\{(y,z)\in\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^d:|y|=|z|=|y-z|=1\}$ of equilateral triangles of side length one with a vertex at the origin. We prove the strong-type asymmetric $L^p$-improving estimate $$\mathcal T_1:L^{\frac{d+1}{d-1}}(\mathbb R^d)\times L^{\frac{d^2-1}{d^2-3d+4}}(\mathbb R^d)\longrightarrow L^{\frac{d+1}{2}}(\mathbb R^d)$$ in every dimension $d\ge4$. This enlarges the range of exponents $(p,q,r)$ for which the triangle averaging operator is known to map $L^p(\mathbb R^d)\times L^q(\mathbb R^d)$ to $L^r(\mathbb R^d)$, and symmetrization produces new symmetric estimates in every such dimension as well. The proof combines Sobolev smoothing estimates, obtained through a microlocal decomposition of the triangle incidence relation, with complex interpolation in an analytic family of averages over triangles of varying shape that contains the triangle averaging operator. We also establish maximal estimates for triangle averages. Let $E\subset[1,2]$ be a nonempty set of upper Minkowski dimension $β$, and let $\mathcal T_E(f,g)=\sup_{t\in E}|\mathcal T_t(f,g)|$. We prove that $$\|\mathcal T_E(f,g)\|_2\lesssim\|f\|_{H^{-s_1}}\|g\|_{H^{-s_2}}$$ whenever $s_1,s_2\ge0$, $s_1+s_2<\frac{d-3-β}{2}$ and $d>3+β$. This improves the previously known Sobolev smoothing estimate by half a derivative and lowers the dimension requirement. We also obtain asymmetric localized maximal estimates of the form $\mathcal T_E:L^p(\mathbb R^d)\times L^q(\mathbb R^d)\to L^r(\mathbb R^d)$ in an enlarged range of exponents.

papers.title: Rapid mixing of Potts Glauber dynamics throughout uniqueness
papers.abstract: Sampling from the ferromagnetic $q$-state Potts model is a fundamental problem in statistical physics and approximate counting. Although computationally hard in the worst case, sampling is expected to be efficient throughout the high-temperature uniqueness regime of the model using the natural single-site Glauber dynamics. We establish fast mixing bounds for every $q$, in the full high-temperature regimes in the two central graph families on $n$ vertices. (1) For every $Δ\ge 3$, the Potts Glauber dynamics mixes in $n\operatorname{polylog}(n)$ steps with high probability on a uniformly random $Δ$-regular graph for all $β<β_u(q,\mathbb T_Δ)$ where $β_u(q,\mathbb T_Δ)$ is the uniqueness threshold on the $Δ$-regular tree; (2) For every $d\ge 2$, the Potts Glauber dynamics has inverse spectral gap $n^{1+o(1)}$ on cubes or tori in $\mathbb Z^d$ for all $β<β_c(q,\mathbb Z^d)$ where $β_c(q,\mathbb Z^d)$ is the critical point on $\mathbb Z^d$. Both temperature thresholds are sharp as the Glauber dynamics slows down exponentially above them. These results overcome the challenge of bounding mixing times without access to correlation decay bounds in the presence of pinnings (i.e., without spectral independence or strong spatial mixing). For this purpose, our proof introduces a new dichotomy principle: throughout the high-temperature regime, any initial spin distribution is either such that its pinnings ensure good correlation decay, or Glauber dynamics escapes from that distribution quickly. We expect this kind of dichotomy to have further applications. As a demonstration, we also develop its analog for random-cluster dynamics and use it to prove that Swendsen-Wang dynamics on random $Δ$-regular graphs mixes in $O(\log n)$ time throughout uniqueness. The results in this paper were arrived at with the assistance of ChatGPT 5.6 and 6.

papers.title: Variance-adaptive Chernoff bounds: nonasymptotically valid, asymptotically sharp confidence sets for unbounded means
papers.abstract: Consider the classical statistical problem of sub-Gaussian mean estimation under martingale dependence: given $n$ observations with conditional mean $μ$ and a known conditional sub-Gaussian proxy $s>0$, we seek a nonasymptotically valid confidence interval for $μ$. The usual Chernoff interval has half-width $s\sqrt{2\log(2/α)/n}$; it neither adapts to the actual standard deviation $σ\le s$ nor attains the Gaussian quantile $z_{1-α/2}$. We construct an analytically closed-form nonasymptotically-valid interval under martingale dependence whose endpoints, at every iid law with $σ> 0$, agree almost surely to first order with $\bar X_n\pmσz_{1-α/2}/\sqrt n$. The two new building blocks are a sub-Gaussian exponential supermartingale with an \emph{empirical} quadratic variance and a cubic correction term, and a sub-Gaussian continuation supermartingale, the former delivering variance adaptivity ("Empirical-Bernstein'' for unbounded data), the latter also providing the Gaussian quantile ("Empirical-Berry-Esseen'' for unbounded data). The same constructions yield a closed-form time-uniform confidence sequence with asymptotically unimprovable half-width $σ\sqrt{2\log\log n/n}$. We also give closed-form multivariate ellipsoids with the true-covariance chi-square limit, and extend the scalar Gaussian and LIL constructions to handle heavy-tailed settings where one only knows a bound on any absolute central moment of order greater than two. Experiments show substantial width reductions when the true variance is smaller than the implied variance bound, at small loss in the boundary cases. The surprising (to us) takeaway message is: given any more than two moments, one can construct fully data dependent nonasymptotic confidence sets for the mean that are asymptotically efficient.

papers.title: Hopficity of braided and labeled Thompson groups
papers.abstract: We prove that the braided Thompson groups $BV$ and $BF$ are Hopfian, answering the two parts of Zaremsky's question. We also prove that, for every discrete group $G$, the labeled Thompson group $V(G)$ is Hopfian if and only if $G$ is Hopfian, proving a conjecture of Wu--Wu--Zhao--Zhou. The second result allows us to prove a new embedding result for Hopfian groups: every Hopfian group of type $F_n$ embeds quasi-isometrically as a subgroup of a Hopfian, boundedly acyclic, acyclic group of type $F_n$ that has no proper finite-index subgroups.

papers.title: Exact Theory and Optimal Stepsizes for Stochastic Gradient Descent in Smooth Convex Minimization
papers.abstract: This work considers the design of stepsize schedules for stochastic gradient descent in smooth convex optimization. Throughout, we assume that gradient noise is conditionally zero-mean with bounded variance. Among problems with dimension $d\geq N+1$, we provide an exact worst-case analysis of the expected suboptimality of stochastic gradient descent's final iterate. Our analysis applies to any (potentially nonconstant) schedule of $N$ stepsizes in $[0,1.5]^N$. Here, exact means that we provide a matching objective function and noise distributions where our guarantee is attained. Whenever the variance bound is at least $Ω(1/\sqrt{N})$, our theory provides the minimax optimal stepsize schedule for stochastic gradient descent and proves its uniqueness. These optimal stepsizes monotonically decrease, ruling out any accelerations in expected final suboptimality from fixed fractal schedules observed in the deterministic case.

papers.title: Motivic invariants of birational hyper-Kähler manifolds
papers.abstract: We prove that birational projective irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifolds have equivalent integral cohomological motives as commutative algebra objects in $\mathrm{SH}(\mathbb C)$. Consequently, their algebraic K-theory spectra are equivalent as $E_\infty$-algebras, and their integral graded K-theory rings are isomorphic.

papers.title: Benchmarking Single-Photon Sources for Measurement-Device-Independent Quantum Key Distribution
papers.abstract: Measurement-Device-Independent Quantum Key Distribution (MDI-QKD) enables secure communication without trusting the measurement devices, but its performance critically depends on the quality of the employed photon sources. We compare MDI-QKD implementations based on Weak Coherent Pulses (WCPs) with those employing Quantum Dot (QD) single-photon sources. WCP-based schemes are fundamentally limited by Poissonian photon-number statistics, imposing a trade-off between single- and multi-photon emissions, whereas QD sources exhibit sub-Poissonian statistics with low antibunching parameter $g^{(2)}(0)$. Using a decoy-state analysis for both source types, we find that even at moderate mean photon numbers, QD-based implementations outperform the best-case WCP configuration - where the mean photon number is optimised at each transmission distance - across the full range of transmission distances. We further incorporate the effect of imperfect photon indistinguishability via Hong-Ou-Mandel interference visibilities into the security framework and demonstrate that both source types are highly sensitive to even small deviations from ideal indistinguishability, significantly affecting achievable key rates and maximum transmission distance.

papers.title: Near-Optimal Second-Order Convex Finite-Sum Optimization under Individual Smoothness
papers.abstract: We study the stochastic second-order oracle complexity of solving smooth convex finite-sum optimization with $n$ components. Very recently, Tsedenov \& Kovalev (2026) showed that the minimax optimal complexity under averaged smoothness and convexity is $\tildeΘ(n + n^{6/7} ε^{-2/7})$ by establishing nearly matching upper and lower bounds. In this paper, we show that individual smoothness and convexity provably enable further acceleration, where the lower complexity bound is $Ω(n+ n^{5/7} ε^{-2/7})$ under this stronger assumption. Then, by establishing a novel second-order self-bounding inequality, we design a new Taylor-corrected lazy Newton method, which can lead to a better complexity of $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(n + n^{5/7} ε^{-2/7})$ by applying the optimal Monteiro-Svaiter acceleration, matching our lower bound up to only logarithmic factors.

papers.title: Berenstein-Zelevinsky polytopes for type $\mathrm{G}_{2}$
papers.abstract: In 2001, Berenstein and Zelevinsky presented a polyhedral model for the problem of computing tensor-product multiplicities for semisimple Lie algebras. We provide explicit linear equations and inequalities for Berenstein--Zelevinsky (BZ) polytopes of type-$\mathrm{G}_{2}$ Lie algebras. We prove that the denominator of a type-$\mathrm{G}_{2}$ BZ polytope divides $180$, and that this bound is sharp, while the quasi-period of the Ehrhart quasipolynomial of such a polytope is always a divisor of $6$. We also show that BZ~polytopes of type-$\mathrm{G}_{2}$ Lie algebras can fail to satisfy Ehrhart positivity, in contrast to a conjectured property of BZ polytopes for all classical types.

papers.title: Treedepth is NP-Hard on Planar Graphs of Maximum Degree 3
papers.abstract: Treedepth is an important parameter in algorithmic graph theory. It is known that the problem of computing the treedepth of a graph is NP-hard. It has been an open problem whether treedepth can be computed in polynomial time when the input graph is restricted to be planar, or of bounded degree. Assuming $P \neq NP$, we answer both questions in the negative: Under polynomial-time Turing reductions, it is NP-hard to compute the treedepth of planar graphs with maximum degree 3. This degree bound is best possible, since treedepth can be computed efficiently on graphs of maximum degree 2.

papers.title: Empirical Evaluation of Quantum Kernel Methods for Classification: A Comparative Study with Classical Kernels
papers.abstract: Quantum kernel methods are the most concrete near-term proposal for quantum machine learning on classical data, yet published benchmarks disagree on whether they outperform tuned classical kernels, and the disagreement cannot be resolved from the literature because the comparisons are not protocol-controlled. We argue that the obstacle is one of measurement, not theory: the usual setup fixes the quantum feature map's data scaling while grid-searching the classical kernel's hyperparameters, recomputes nothing per fold, and reports cost in simulator time. We therefore treat the comparison itself as the object of study and impose three controls. The bandwidth is tuned on the same grid budget as the classical $γ$, the kernel is recomputed inside every fold from fold-fitted preprocessing, and cost is counted in hardware circuit evaluations. On top of these we run a factorial design of 324 cells in which dimensionality, training size, class separability and data structure are explicit covariates, together with four standard datasets, a shots-versus-gate-noise ablation, and a cost sweep. The dominant effect we measure is not quantum: tuning the feature map's bandwidth is worth 0.120 accuracy on synthetic data and 0.339 on real data, exceeding every quantum-classical difference we observe. Tuned quantum kernels are then statistically indistinguishable from a tuned RBF on all four real datasets. The advantage on synthetic data is confined almost entirely to data generated by the feature map itself, and it shrinks with dimensionality (-0.0045 per qubit) while growing with sample size. Finite sampling costs an order of magnitude more accuracy than gate and readout noise, and a fidelity kernel needs $5\times10^{7}$ circuits at n = 10,000. Protocol variance is thus sufficient to explain the field's contradictory conclusions.

papers.title: Stochastic processes on reductive homogeneous and symmetric spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper we present a method to effectively and efficiently provide pathwise approximations of the Riemannian Brownian motion on a reductive homogeneous space $M\cong G/H$ endowed with a $G$-invariant metric. This setting includes spheres, hyperbolic spaces, the space of symmetric positive-definite matrices, flag manifolds and Stiefel manifolds. The simulation is based on Wong--Zakai approximations of an appropriately chosen SDE in $G$ that is projected down onto $M\cong G/H$. The effectiveness lies in the fact that well-established results on the convergence rate of the Wong--Zakai equation immediately carry over to the homogeneous space thanks to Nash's embedding. The efficiency lies in the fact that explicit representations of the Wong--Zakai approximations can be obtained in this setting using the Lie exponential map.

papers.title: Spectral Beurling-Selberg Approximation and Applications to Effective Motivic Chebotarev-Sato-Tate Estimates
papers.abstract: We establish a spectral Beurling-Selberg approximation theorem on compact connected Riemannian manifolds for sets whose boundaries have finite upper Minkowski content. Our majorants and minorants have controlled spectral coefficients and explicit stability under Hausdorff perturbations, uniformly over families satisfying a common Minkowski content bound. We extend the construction to singular spaces arising from Riemannian submetries with basic mean curvature, and apply it to equidistribution on quaternionic Shimura varieties. Assuming the conjectural formalism of the specified motivic L-functions, including the motivic Riemann hypothesis, we develop effective Chebotarev-Sato-Tate estimates for fixed sets and varying families with controlled boundary geometry and Hausdorff variation, and describe how additional symmetries improve the error exponents. The proofs combine classical analytic methods with new methods from differential geometry, analytic geometry, and Riemannian spectral analysis. Applications include an asymptotic formula for a motivic analogue of Atkin-Serre estimates and tubular estimates for Picard-rank jumps of K3 surfaces via their transcendental motives.

papers.title: Modulo k-orientations of highly edge-connected signed graphs
papers.abstract: A modulo $k$-orientation of a signed graph is an orientation in which the outdegree and indegree are congruent modulo $k$ at every vertex. We show that, for every odd integer $k\ge3$, every essentially $k$-unbalanced $(6k-10)$-edge-connected signed graph admits a modulo $k$-orientation. This improves the edge-connectivity bound of Zhu [JCTB, 112 (2015)] from $6k-7$ to $6k-10$.

papers.title: Logical Bell Inequalities for Marginal Wigner Negativity
papers.abstract: We construct logical Bell inequalities whose violations are determined by the Wigner function of a reduced quantum state. For odd-prime qudits, each phase-space point of any nonempty proper subsystem defines an inequality, violated precisely when the corresponding Gross Wigner value is negative. This correspondence allows us to quantify the contextuality that a reduced state guarantees for the composite system. The normalized violation gives a lower bound on the contextual fraction in the complete Weyl measurement scenario, valid for every joint state with that marginal, irrespective of its correlations. We identify a family of product states that saturates this bound. For these states, one marginal Wigner value fixes the contextual fraction of the entire system.

papers.title: Central values of additive twists of automorphic $L$-series
papers.abstract: We study series $L(x,s):=\sum_n ρ(n)e^{2πi n x}/n^s$, where $ρ(n)$ are Fourier coefficients of an automorphic form $φ$ for a discrete cofinite subgroup $Γ\subset \mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ and $x\in\mathbb{R}$. Let $\mathfrak{b}\in\mathbb{R}\cup\{\infty\}$ represent a cusp of $Γ$. Ordering the orbit $Γ\mathfrak{b}$ by increasing denominators, we prove that the values $L(x,1/2)$ for $x\inΓ\mathfrak{b}$, suitably normalized, become equidistributed according to a standard complex Gaussian law, under natural assumptions on the Laplace eigenvalue of $φ$. Previously this was known either when $Γ=\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ or when $φ$ is associated to a holomorphic cusp form. This applies in particular to central values at $s=1/2$ of additive twists of Maass form $L$-functions $\sum_{n\geq1}λ(n)e^{2πi n x}/n^s$, or to the Dirichlet-theta series $\sum_{n\geq1}χ(n)e^{2πi n^2 x}/n^s$.

papers.title: Extremal character spectra of finite projective systems
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal M$ be a finite spanning multiset of points in ${\rm PG}(k-1,q)$, and let ${\rm Char}_{\mathcal M}$ be its character function. For $1\le r\le k$, we study the maximum number of distinct values attained by ${\rm Char}_{\mathcal M}$ on the codimension-$r$ flats under a total-multiplicity budget. The spectrum is subject to two natural upper bounds, whose extremal cases lead respectively to $r$-maximum character spectrum ($r$-MCS) and $r$-full character spectrum ($r$-FCS) systems. We establish the existence of $r$-FCS systems in a broad parameter range, and solve the size-constrained extremal problem completely when $r=k-1$, including the minimum-cost multiplicity profiles. For $1\le r<k$, put $M_r=\qbinom{k}{r}$ and $B_r=\qbinom{k-1}{r}$. The minimum size $ν_r(k,q)$ of an $r$-MCS system satisfies \[\left\lceil\frac{\binom{M_r}{2}}{B_r}\right\rceil\le ν_r(k,q)\le \binom{M_r-1}{2}+\frac{q^k-q^{k-r}}{q-1}.\] The upper bound is at most $\binom{M_r}{2}$, strictly less when $r\le k-2$, and exact when $r=k-1$. Its proof applies positive additive labelings to the complement of one flat, whose trace is empty while all remaining traces are distinct. For $r=1$, we improve the known upper bounds on the minimum length of such systems. We also develop global moment identities and local flat-incidence bounds that impose strong structural constraints on large character spectra. Under the projective-system correspondence, complementary character spectra are the support-weight spectra of $r$-dimensional subcodes.

papers.title: Tiling without a subspace complement: a sharp counterexample in dimension nine over the field with two elements
papers.abstract: We construct an explicit 64-point subset of $\mathbb F_2^9$ which tiles by translation but has no linear-subspace tiling complement. Together with our earlier dimension-eight theorem and a product argument, this shows that every nonempty tile in $\mathbb F_2^d$ has a linear-subspace complement precisely when $d\le8$. The example is spectral, so it is not a counterexample to Fuglede's conjecture. Its construction uses six three-dimensional subspaces of $\mathbb F_2^6$, specified by a small table. We classify all its tiling complements and spectra: there are exactly 512 complements and 64 spectra, with one translation class of each. Every spectrum has normalized Wiener norm $15/8$. An appendix proves that Goyal's related construction is affinely inequivalent but has the same tiling complements and spectra. The construction and both classifications are proved from first principles. We also give elementary proofs of the positive assertion in dimensions at most seven and for all tile sizes other than sixteen in dimension eight. The remaining case uses our previously established theorem based on the classification of perfect binary codes of length fifteen.

papers.title: Ramsey numbers $R(K_{1,4},K_{m,n})$ for small $m$
papers.abstract: We determine all currently unknown values of the generalized two-color Ramsey number $R(K_{1,4},K_{m,n})$ for $\min(m,n) \leq 8$. We also prove that the number $R(K_{1,4},K_{m,m})$ equals $26, 29, 31, 33$ for $m = 9, 10, 11, 12$ respectively.

papers.title: Rationally slice knots that are not biprojectively H-slice
papers.abstract: We show that rationally slice knots need not be biprojectively H-slice (BPH-slice), answering a question in the study of the rational knot concordance group. Our main tool is a lattice embedding obstruction to H-sliceness in $\#^n\mathbb{CP}^2$ for knots with vanishing signature, extending work of Kjuchukova--Miller--Ray--Sakallı. We apply the obstruction to an infinite family of rationally slice knots, beginning with $8_{18}$. As additional applications, we obstruct the BPH-sliceness of a family of 2-bridge knots which is not obstructed by the instanton knot concordance invariant $r_0$, we obstruct a non-alternating family of Montesinos knots, and we give prime alternating knots that are topologically but not smoothly biprojectively H-slice. We discuss why these knots remain plausible candidates for detecting exotic smooth structures on $\#^n\mathbb{CP}^2$ and suggest natural sources of further candidates.

papers.title: On Statistical-Computational Gaps in Graph Combinatorial Testing Problems
papers.abstract: We study high-dimensional graph combinatorial hypothesis testing problems in which a signal is supported on the edge set of an unknown subgraph drawn from a class invariant under vertex relabeling. For Gaussian observations, we characterize sharp statistical and computational thresholds (at polynomial order) for the signal magnitude required for strong detection across various combinatorial graph alternatives. Our analysis is based on bounding the second moments of the full and low-degree likelihood ratios in terms of the overlap of two independent latent structures and comparing the resulting lower bounds with scan, average, and coordinatewise maximum tests. Under an appropriate low-degree conjecture for computational hardness, we obtain planted-clique thresholds matching those known for Gaussian submatrix detection and identify new statistical-computational gaps for multiple planted cliques and hypercliques, thick cycles and thick paths. We also establish a novel transfer principle across natural exponential family observation models: matching the one-coordinate chi-square divergence preserves full likelihood-ratio second moments exactly and makes low-degree second moments equivalent up to constant factors under a degree condition. Under local regularity, we obtain corresponding testing upper bounds in terms of an effective signal strength. When these upper and lower bounds match, they yield universal threshold scales in the local alternative regime. As a consequence, statistical-computational gaps for planted-clique detection in Erdős--Rényi settings can be deduced from the Gaussian model.

papers.title: Large-Time Upper Decay Estimates for Weakly Coupled Time-Fractional Diffusion Systems
papers.abstract: We prove conjectured-optimal large-time upper decay estimates for solutions of weakly coupled systems of $m\ge2$ time-fractional diffusion equations. Our result establishes the upper-bound assertion in the conjecture of Li, Liu, and Wada~\cite{LLW26}. The sharpness of these upper exponents for $m\ge3$ remains open in general; see Section~\ref{sec:discussion}. Assume that the diffusion matrices are uniformly elliptic, the coupling coefficients are bounded and may depend on time, and the matrix of $L^\infty$-norms of the coupling coefficients satisfies a spectral-radius stability condition. Let $α^*$ denote the smallest fractional order among the components with nonzero initial data. Then the $L^2(Ω)^m$-norm of the solution is $O(t^{-α^*})$ as $t\to\infty$ if $α^*<1$, whereas it is $O(t^{-(1+α_m)})$ if $α^*=1$, where $α_m$ is the smallest fractional order occurring in the system. For $m=2$, the result yields the same upper decay exponents as \cite[Theorem~1.1]{LLW26}; in the absence of self-coupling, the matrix stability condition is weaker than the corresponding small-coupling condition in that work. The case $m\ge3$ is new. Our proof uses a large-time weighted Volterra framework. If $α^*<1$, the weight is a regularly varying power weight; if $α^*=1$, it is constructed by convolution with the resolvent kernel associated with the smallest fractional order. These weights yield the required large-time bounds for all resolvent kernels in the system. In particular, the argument avoids the Laplace-transform and residue-calculus methods used in \cite{LLW26}, which become difficult to implement for systems with three or more components.

papers.title: When is the deepest drawdown also the longest?
papers.abstract: Does the deepest drawdown take the longest to recover? For random walks with iid increments of positive finite mean, we find that the deepest and longest episodes are eventually distinct almost surely under light-tailed losses, but coincide with probability tending to one under heavy-tailed losses. More precisely, when losses have a finite exponential moment, the deepest episode's duration, relative to the longest among $n$ episodes, converges in probability to an explicit $ρ\in(0,1)$, while its descending duration rank is $n^{1-ρ+o_{\mathbb{P}}(1)}$. These limits hold for every fixed number of leading depths; in the Gaussian model, $ρ=1/2$, independently of drift and variance. The separation reflects the different exponential costs of reaching a large depth and sustaining a long episode. For regularly varying losses, a common large loss governs both depth and duration: the duration ratio tends to one almost surely, and for every fixed $k$, the $k$ deepest and $k$ longest episodes have the same indices in the same order with probability tending to one. For any $k_n\to\infty$ with $k_n=o(n)$, the proportion of common episodes among the $k_n$ deepest and $k_n$ longest converges in probability to zero in the light-tailed case and to one in the heavy-tailed case. These ranking laws also hold for completed drawdowns within a deterministic observation horizon.

papers.title: Maximum of the Two-Dimensional Directed Polymer in the Critical Window
papers.abstract: Let $Z_N^{β_N}(x)$ denote the partition function of the two-dimensional directed polymer started at $x\in \mathbb{Z}^2$, in Gaussian environemnt, in the critical window, with parameter $β_N=\sqrt{(1-\vartheta/\log N)/R_N}$. Here $R_N\sim (\log N)/π$ is the truncated collision Green function at the origin for the simple random walk on $\mathbb{Z}^2$. Let $\mathfrak M_N$ denote the maximum of $\log Z_N(x)$ over $|x|_\infty\leq \sqrt{N}$. We prove that, for any $\vartheta\in \mathbb{R}$, in probability, $$\mathfrak M_N/\sqrt{\log N}\to 2\sqrt{2}\text{ as }N\to\infty.$$

papers.title: Resource efficient Sample Based Quantum Simulation through Fragmentation and Virtual Partitioning of QPU
papers.abstract: Present-day sample-based quantum algorithms within quantum-centric supercomputing workflows require substantial classical post-processing, large circuit depths to produce chemically relevant samples, and long QPU times to execute the many circuits needed for molecules of chemically relevant size. We introduce FMO-QVM-HCI-HSQD, a resource-efficient sample-based framework that breaks a large problem into fragments, runs the fragments in parallel on virtual regions of the QPU, and reduces circuit depth through a half-qubit ansatz whose samples seed an HCI expansion. We demonstrate the algorithm on ibm_marrakesh and ibm_boston for the water trimer and the carmofur_Mpro complex with up to 52 qubits, benchmarking against FMO-CCSD(T), FMO-CASCI and FMO-HCI. For the water trimer (14 spin orbitals for monomers, 28 for dimers), our method reduces the two-qubit depth by 39% compared to FMO-QVM-SQD and the QPU time by 82% compared to sequential FMO-SQD, and accesses 3% of the determinant subspace versus 40% for FMO-SQD, while achieving more accurate energies. For the carmofur_Mpro complex (16 and 32 spin orbitals), it reduces the two-qubit depth by 47% and the QPU time by 20% compared to FMO-QVM-SQD, and accesses 0.007% of the determinant subspace versus 40%, while remaining within chemical accuracy. Extending the carmofur_Mpro active space in the 6-31G basis to 52 and 104 spin orbitals, sampled on 26 and 52 qubits, the total energy deviates from FMO-HCI by only 1.22 mHa. These results show that combining fragmentation, virtual QPU partitioning and half-qubit sampling makes sample-based quantum simulation of chemically relevant systems feasible on current hardware.

papers.title: Suspense and surprise in matroid bingo
papers.abstract: We present the game of Matroid Bingo and prove that it gets more suspenseful the longer the game goes on.

papers.title: Hilton-Zhao vertex-splitting conjecture for triangle-free graphs
papers.abstract: Every graph obtained from a regular Class $1$ graph by a vertex-splitting is overfull and hence is of Class $2$; the central question is whether the resulting graph is edge-chromatic critical. We consider a revised version of the Hilton-Zhao vertex-splitting conjecture for triangle-free base graphs, excluding the known cubic exception that arises from the Wagner graph. Let $G$ be a connected $n$-vertex triangle-free $Δ$-regular Class $1$ graph, and let $G^{*}$ be obtained from $G$ by splitting one vertex into two adjacent vertices. We first show that any non-extreme vertex-splitting produces a $Δ$-critical graph provided $Δ>\frac{n-1}{3}$. Consequently, for non-extreme vertex-splittings, the revised version of the conjecture is valid across its entire conjectured degree range, and indeed even under a slightly weaker degree condition. We next turn to arbitrary vertex-splittings, extreme ones included. It is shown that $G^*$ is $Δ$-critical provided $n \ge 10$ and $Δ>\frac{2n-3}{5}$. In addition, for $n>24$, the non-strict condition $Δ\ge \frac{2n-3}{5}$ is already sufficient. This extends the bipartite range $Δ>\frac{2n}{5}$ to the boundary range that the bipartite argument does not cover. In particular, our arguments give a complete treatment of the case of triangle-free $6$-regular base graphs in the conjectured range. The proofs bring together structural properties of full-deficiency pairs, homomorphism theorems for dense triangle-free graphs, and Hamilton decompositions built via graph detachment.

papers.title: Hedetniemi's conjecture for Shannon OR-capacity: counterexamples and asymptotic separation
papers.abstract: We disprove the analogue of Hedetniemi's conjecture for Shannon OR-capacity, which asserts that the capacity of a categorical product equals the smaller capacity of its factors. For every sufficiently large complete graph, we construct a second graph of larger capacity such that their categorical product has capacity strictly below that of the complete graph. Further constructions show that, for every real threshold above an explicit constant, both factor capacities can exceed that threshold while the product capacity lies below it. We also construct graph pairs, again with one complete factor, whose capacities tend to infinity while their product capacity is subpolynomial in the smaller factor capacity. Whether the product capacity must nevertheless tend to infinity whenever both factor capacities do remains open. The proofs use spectral interpolation, which also yields a single spectral point violating Hedetniemi's identity throughout the complete-factor family. Finally, we identify the categorical product as the distinguishability graph of a random-switching model for zero-error communication. In this model, our constructions show that switching can reduce the zero-error rate to a vanishing fraction of the smaller individual rate.

papers.title: Limit theorems for cuspidal orbits on Fuchsian groups
papers.abstract: Let $Γ\subset \operatorname{SL}(2, \mathbb{R})$ be discrete, co-finite with cusps, and let ${\frak b}\in \mathbb{R}\cup\{\infty\}$ be a cusp of $Γ$. Let $f: Γ{\frak b} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a quantum modular form in the sense that the maps $$ φ_γ(x) = f(x) - f(γx) \qquad (x\in Γ{\frak b}, γ\in Γ) $$ extend to Hölder-regular functions. Under bounded moments assumptions of the shape $\sum_n n^{-2} \int |φ_{γ^n}(x)|^αd x < \infty$ for some $α>0$ and every fixed parabolic element $γ\in Γ$, we prove asymptotic formulas for the characteristic functions of the values $f(x)$ for $x\in Γ{\frak b}$, ordered by growing denominators. These yield Gaussian limits when $α>2$ and other stable limit laws under suitable further assumptions. This generalizes to Fuchsian groups the work of Baladi-Vallée on rational orbits of the Gauss map. In companion papers, we use this result, and in particular its flexible assumptions on $φ_γ$, to deduce limit theorems for automorphic $L$-series at the central point. One ingredient in our proof is a particular cuspidal acceleration of the Bowen-Series map, whose inverse branches admit a convenient parametrization, and for which we describe explicitly a natural extension.

papers.title: The 3-Color 2-Chromatic Gallai-Ramsey Number for Complete Graphs
papers.abstract: For $1\le i\le j\le k$, let $gr^3_2(K_i, K_j, K_k)$ be the least $n\in \mathbb{N}$ such that every rainbow triangle-free $3$-coloring of $K_n$ (using red, blue, and green) contains a red/blue $K_i$, a red/green $K_j$, or a blue/green $K_k$. In this paper, we completely evaluate $gr^3_2(K_i, K_j, K_k)$ for all values of $i$, $j$, and $k$ in which $r(K_i,K_j)$ is known.

papers.title: A Robust High-order Approximation of the Gray Thermal Radiative Transfer Equations
papers.abstract: We present a high-order, positivity preserving, and asymptotic preserving approximation of the gray radiative transfer equations. The time and space approximation is done using a diagonally-implicit Runge-Kutta method with stabilized, continuous finite elements, and the angular approximation uses the method of discrete ordinates. We detail a simple and robust inner/outer iteration strategy to solve these equations and prove that the proposed scheme is exactly conservative, independent of iterative tolerances. A maximum and minimum principle is enforced using a conservative redistribution limiting technique, and the method is demonstrated to be robust in the thick diffusion limit.

papers.title: On Universal Minkowski Classes of Polytopes: Theory and Applications
papers.abstract: This paper establishes the existence, in every dimension, of universal Minkowski classes of configuration-constrained polytopes, with direct applications to set-theoretic control. For any prescribed accuracy, such a class contains an approximation of every compact convex set to that accuracy and admits a jointly affine parameterization of facets and vertices. The construction is explicit and relies on a combinatorial averaging procedure that produces minimal configuration enclosures. In control, these polytopic templates enable convex reformulations of otherwise non-convex problems, including invariant-set computation and control Lyapunov function design. Tutorial examples illustrate both the geometric construction and its control applications.

papers.title: No generalised contextuality from the vacuum
papers.abstract: We show that, under certain conditions, generalised contextuality, in the sense introduced by Spekkens, cannot be created from the vacuum of a quantum field. Initial noncontextual qudit states do not become contextual just by interacting with a quantum field. This is verified in two scenarios. First, in a perturbative approach where the time evolution operator is expanded in powers of the coupling constant. Second, in the limit of zero energy gap in the spectrum of the free detector Hamiltonian. Our results are at the opposite side of what has been recently obtained in the literature regarding the harvesting of Kochen-Specker contextuality. Our results demonstrate that the existing notions of contextuality can be independent of one another and that contextuality harvesting depends on which precise notion is used.

papers.title: GENIE: learned quantum circuits as embedding impurity solvers, and why compactness, not correlation strength, decides when they work
papers.abstract: Sample-based quantum diagonalization has been used as an impurity solver in density matrix embedding theory (DMET), but always with fixed-form circuits and without comparison to classical selection at the same subspace size. We introduce GENIE, a DMET impurity solver in which a generative transformer learns the sampling circuit, trained on the quantum-selected configuration interaction energy. On N2, hydrogen chains, water and a hydrogen ring, we compare GENIE at equal determinant budget with classical selected configuration interaction (CIPSI, ASCI, heat-bath CI) and with DMET combined with sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD). GENIE selects: for N2 at 200 determinants it is within a factor of 1.7 of CIPSI and 25 to 1000 times more accurate than the determinants a fixed circuit actually samples, while standard SQD reaches good energies mainly by filling the subspace. GENIE does not beat the best classical selection, and its circuits require fault-tolerant hardware. Its failures are governed by the compactness of the wavefunction relative to the budget, not by correlation strength. A cheap estimate from coupled-cluster amplitudes predicts this compactness. A router built on it never recommended GENIE where it then failed, apart from seed-to-seed variance, and it transferred unchanged to a blind test on new systems. We also identify two benchmarking pitfalls that can create apparent quantum advantages of one to two orders of magnitude.

papers.title: The metric Zariski multiplicity conjecture in dimension 4
papers.abstract: Recently, OpenAI announced a counterexample to the Zariski multiplicity conjecture in dimension 4. Here, we prove that the metric Zariski multiplicity conjecture is true in dimension 4. More precisely, let $f,g\colon(\mathbb{C}^n,0)\to(\mathbb{C},0)$ be germs of reduced holomorphic functions, and let $\varphi\colon(\mathbb{C}^n,0)\to(\mathbb{C}^n,0)$ be a bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism such that $\varphi(V(f))=V(g)$. We prove that if every irreducible component of the tangent cone of $V(f)$ at the origin has a singular locus of dimension at most two, then $V(f)$ and $V(g)$ have the same multiplicity at the origin. In particular, the multiplicity of complex analytic hypersurface singularities in $\mathbb{C}^n$, $n\leq 4$, is an embedded bi-Lipschitz invariant; the cases $n=2$ and $n=3$ were known. This extends a previous result of the author for tangent cones whose components have singular loci of dimension at most one. We also prove that two irreducible homogeneous hypersurfaces whose singular loci have dimension at most two, and which are mapped onto each other by a homeomorphism of $\mathbb{C}^n$ fixing the origin, have the same degree.

papers.title: Strong edge-colourings of truncations of cubic graphs
papers.abstract: We study a problem posed by Kardoš asking whether the truncation of every connected simple bridgeless cubic graph has strong chromatic index six. The truncation $T(G)$ is obtained by replacing each vertex of $G$ with a triangle and attaching its incident edges to distinct vertices of that triangle. An affirmative answer was previously established for prism bases by Han and Cui. We prove that $\sidx(T(G))=6$ whenever $G$ is a connected simple cubic graph that is bipartite or is both bridgeless and claw-free. Both proofs are constructive and use a common compatibility criterion for combining colourings of smaller pieces. The bipartite result also extends to non-det-extremal multigraphs.

papers.title: Optimal Average Distortion for Non-Expansive Embeddings of Euclidean Metrics into the Line: With applications to cut-matching games and vertex expansion
papers.abstract: We show that any $n$-point Euclidean metric admits a non-expansive embedding into the line with average distortion at most $O\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{\log\log n}}\right)$, matching a known lower bound. We also present two applications of this result. First, we give a cut-player strategy with an optimal spectral guarantee for the undirected cut-matching game. Second, we give an improved spectral approximation for vertex expansion in high-degree graphs.

papers.title: Locality, Probability and the Relevance of History
papers.abstract: Relativistic theory and experiments teach us that causal influences are constrained by the speed of light. Deterministic theories incorporate this lesson in $\textit{functional}$ terms: whether an event occurs or not is functionally determined by events that occur in its immediate causal past. In this paper we suggest a natural generalization of this constraint that applies to probabilistic theories: the $\textit{probability}$ that an event occurs is to be functionally determined by the $\textit{probability}$ of the event-occurrences in its immediate causal past. This constraint differs from Bell's criterion of local causality and turns out to imply it only under an additional assumption that requires history to be, in a sense, $\textit{ir}$relevant. Bell-inequality-violating quantum phenomena are thus arguably $\textit{not}$ in tension with relativity, locality, "statistical independence", nor with a supposed "realism". What they instead show is that history is, in a sense, $\textit{relevant}$.

papers.title: Type classifiers
papers.abstract: We extend dependent type theory by type classifiers and construct an interpretation in the category of contextual categories with families. Type classifiers extend contexts by type variables, complementing the usual context extensions by term variables of specified types. This allows statements with arbitrary type parameters to be formulated without assuming a universe. We show that substituting isomorphic types induces isomorphisms between the resulting types even in extensional type theory, giving an analogue of the invariance supplied by the univalence axiom in homotopy type theory. Omitting function types from the theory, so that all type formers are covariant, extends this naturality to arbitrary, possibly noninvertible maps.
